docs.title: Round 44-A — PH3-02 Effect annotations + Fork warnings (v0.3.0)
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-25 CST ~12:30 Branch: main Release: v0.3.0 Tests: 427 pass / 2 skip / 94% coverage (up from 386 in v0.2.1)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Land PH3-02 — the first Phase 3 on-ramp brick. Adapters annotate each node with an effects list, and the Web UI warns users before they fork a node that touched the real world. Per ADR-019 (R43-B) Chronos stays explicitly non-sandboxed — warnings are the honest compromise, not fake safety.

docs.title: 1. Adapter heuristic — src/chronos/adapters/effects.py (170+ lines)
docs.text:
classify_effects(kind: NodeKind, node_name: str, override: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:

  • NodeKind.LLM → ["llm"]
  • Regex on node_name (snake_case-aware):
  • network — http/api/fetch/request/get/post/download/upload
  • fs — read/write/file/path/save/load
  • db — db/postgres/redis/sql
  • external — send_slack/send_email/run_shell/subprocess

DANGEROUS_EFFECTS_DEFAULT = {"network", "fs", "db", "external"} — llm deliberately excluded because forking is precisely about re-running LLM reasoning; flagging it would spam warnings on every interesting fork.

count_dangerous_downstream(store, run_id, from_step) — helper for the fork-plan preview (counts how many dangerous nodes will be re-executed if you fork at from_step).

docs.title: 2. Adapter integration
docs.text:
Both LangGraphRecorder.__init__ and AutoGen Recorder.__init__ now accept effects_map: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None (per-node-name override for power users). Every recorded Node gets metadata["effects"] = classify_effects(kind, node_name, override=effects_map.get(node_name)).

Zero SQL migration: metadata_json column has existed since v0.1.0; Node.model_dump() auto-exposes metadata.effects through the API.

docs.title: 3. UI effects badge + Fork warning — frontend/src/components/NodeDetails.tsx
docs.text:
• Effects row under the identity table: <Tag color=...> per effect. Color map: llm=purple, network=orange, fs=gold, db=volcano, external=red.
  • Amber <Alert warning> banner at the top of the drawer when hasDangerous. Title: "This node may have side effects". Body explains forking re-runs the real-world operation (re-charge, re-send, re-write) and suggests forking from a pure node for reasoning-only exploration.
  • Danger-styled Fork button when onFork prop is provided AND node is dangerous: AntD danger styling + · re-triggers side effects appended to the label.

docs.title: 4. i18n + ConceptTip glossary
docs.text:
• effects.tags.{llm,network,fs,db,external} — tag labels (zh/en)
  • effects.forkWarning.{title,body,buttonHint} — banner + button hint copy
  • help.concepts.effects — glossary entry ("副作用" in the term-explanation drawer)
  • nodeDetails.fields.effects — drawer row label

docs.title: 5. Tests — tests/unit/test_effects.py (41 tests)
docs.text:
Covers: - LLM kind → always ["llm"] - Each of 4 keyword families with positive + negative cases - snake_case compound: http_get, send_slack_notification, http_write_db - Override precedence (override wins) - count_dangerous_downstream correctness

Full suite: 427 pass / 2 skip / 94% coverage.

docs.title: Browser validation
docs.text:
• Generated demo DB /tmp/r44a_demo.db with 7-node run covering all 5 effect categories
  • chronos web --db /tmp/r44a_demo.db --port 8123
  • Clicked fetch_weather_api node in TreeView → drawer renders "Side effects: Network" tag + amber warning banner with correct copy ✅
  • Fork button danger styling is predicated on onFork prop (not wired in current TreeView; the warning Alert is the v0.3.0 user-visible signal)

docs.title: Key lessons
docs.text:
1. Python regex \b word-boundary trap: _ is a word character in Python regex, so \bhttp\b does not match http_get. For snake_case compound names use \bhttp(_\w+)?\b or the looser \b\w*http\w*\b. Saved as skill python-regex-word-boundary-underscore-trap.
  2. SqliteStore construction: class factory is SqliteStore.open(path), not SqliteStore(Path(path)) directly. The raw __init__ takes a sqlite3.Connection.
  3. Run.adapter_thread_id not thread_id: the field is namespaced to distinguish from Chronos's own thread concept.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Option B (metadata-only) beats Option A (first-class column) — zero SQL migration, API/UI transparent. R43-D recommendation validated.
  • LLM in DANGEROUS_EFFECTS_DEFAULT: no. Forking to re-run LLM reasoning is the core happy path; warning would be noise.
  • Fork button danger styling is predicated, not default: the v0.3.0 user-visible primary signal is the Alert banner. When future onFork integration happens, the button auto-activates.

docs.title: Round 45-A — PH3-03 Fork-plan downstream side-effects preview (v0.3.1)
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-25 CST ~16:00 Branch: main Release: v0.3.1 Tests: 435 pass / 2 skip / 94% coverage (+8 from v0.3.0), cli/fork.py 97%

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Land PH3-03 — close the effect-aware UX loop on the CLI side. v0.3.0 (R44-A) gave the Web UI a per-node Fork warning banner; PH3-03 brings the same honesty to chronos fork plan so terminal users see "if you fork here, N dangerous downstream nodes will re-execute" before they save the plan.

Zero schema change, pure CLI-layer enhancement. Continues the R43 / R44-A line: ADR-019 — Chronos does not sandbox, it warns.

docs.title: 1. Pure helper — src/chronos/cli/fork.py::build_effects_summary
docs.text:
def build_effects_summary(
    downstream_nodes: Sequence[Node],
    *,
    dangerous: frozenset[str] = DANGEROUS_EFFECTS_DEFAULT,
) -> dict[str, Any]:

Returns {total, dangerous_count, tag_counts, samples}: - total — count of downstream nodes (step_index > parent.step_index) - dangerous_count — subset that carry any tag in dangerous - tag_counts — {tag: int} across all downstream nodes (sorted alphabetically on render) - samples — up to 3 dangerous nodes, each {step, name, tags} (prevents 50-node dangerous runs from flooding the terminal)

Defensive: if metadata["effects"] is missing or not a list (malformed runs), the node is treated as tag-less rather than crashing. No I/O, no console — trivial to unit-test.

docs.title: 2. Renderer — render_effects_preview(summary, console)
docs.text:
Rich Panel(border_style="yellow") titled "Downstream side-effects preview":

⚠ 4 dangerous / 5 total
breakdown: db=1, external=1, fs=1, network=2
• step 1: fetch_api (network, llm)
• step 2: write_file (fs)
• step 3: db_insert (db)
… and 1 more
Chronos does not sandbox forks — review before running (ADR-019).

Silence principle: renders nothing when total == 0 (forking at the last node) OR dangerous_count == 0 (pure-LLM downstream). Prevents false-alarm fatigue.

docs.title: 3. CLI wiring — render_plan_preview + fork_plan_command
docs.text:
• render_plan_preview() gains effects_summary: dict | None = None kwarg (backward-compatible — existing callers pass nothing and get the old behavior).
  • fork_plan_command() after parent resolution: 
    downstream = [n for n in nodes if n.step_index > parent_node.step_index]
effects_summary = build_effects_summary(downstream)
    Both emit paths (JSON stdout + Python-literal stdout) pass it to render_plan_preview.

docs.title: 4. Tests — 8 new in tests/unit/test_fork_cli.py
docs.text:
Helper block (pure-function tests, no Click runner): - empty downstream → {total:0, dangerous_count:0, tag_counts:{}, samples:[]} - pure-LLM downstream → dangerous_count == 0, tag_counts == {"llm": N} - mixed tags → correct dangerous count + alphabetical tag breakdown - >3 dangerous → samples capped at 3, still reports correct dangerous_count - malformed metadata["effects"] = "not a list" → treated as no tags, no crash

CLI block (CliRunner against synthesized run + SqliteStore): - mixed run, fork mid-run → stdout contains Downstream side-effects, dangerous count, tag breakdown - fork at last node → stdout does not contain the panel - pure-LLM downstream → stdout does not contain the panel

docs.title: 5. Bonus fix — test_cli_info phase-marker stale assertion
docs.text: R44-A bumped the chronos info CLI output to "Phase 3 on-ramp" but didn't update tests/unit/test_cli.py::test_cli_info which still asserted "phase 2". Full-suite run in R45-A caught it. Fixed + listed in v0.3.1 CHANGELOG. Lesson added to CONTEXT §5: release cut must run full pytest -q, not just the test file of the feature branch.

docs.title: Key facts (pinned to CONTEXT.md §5)
docs.text:
1. Per-run linear downstream, not DAG-topological: step_index > parent.step_index matches the replay/fork consumer mental model (forking replays the timeline from that point forward). Walking the DAG via parent_node_id edges is a Phase 4 concern and would change semantics.
  2. Silent-by-default: no panel at total == 0 or dangerous_count == 0. ADR-019's honesty is "warn when it matters", not "spam on every fork".
  3. Sample cap 3 + … and N more: realistic ergonomic cap; enough to give users a feel for what's downstream without flooding a terminal.
  4. Defensive metadata parsing: metadata["effects"] treated as optional-and-possibly-garbage input. One-line isinstance(x, list) guard, no recovery magic.
  5. Pure helper / renderer split: build_effects_summary() is easily unit-tested (no I/O, no console); render_effects_preview() is a thin renderer smoke-tested via CLI key-string assertions. Good pattern for future CLI additions.

docs.title: What this closes
docs.text: Phase 3 "make users feel side effects" now has three entry points all lit up: - Adapters auto-tag nodes (R44-A, v0.3.0) - Web drawer: per-node effect Tags + amber warning Alert + danger Fork button hook (R44-A, v0.3.0) - CLI fork plan: downstream side-effects preview Panel (R45-A, v0.3.1) ← this round

docs.text:
Activate the danger-styled Fork button that R44-A (v0.3.0) pre-wired into NodeDetails but that TreeView never powered on. Close the R46-A plan from CONTEXT.md §6:

  1. Expose chronos fork plan as an HTTP endpoint so the Web UI can call it without shelling out.
  2. Add a ForkPlanModal to the Tree page that shows the plan JSON + the same downstream side-effects preview the CLI got in v0.3.1 (R45-A).
  3. Stay true to ADR-013 (Chronos plans, never executes) and ADR-019 (no sandbox, honest warnings).

docs.title: Context: state picked up mid-air
docs.text:
This round inherited a partial implementation from a prior cron slot that landed code but never committed, pushed, or wrote a progress doc. Recovery steps:

  • git log origin/main..HEAD showed 8 unpushed commits going back to R42-A (push was stalled since last cron).
  • Working tree had the API endpoint + frontend plumbing for R46-A already written, but the i18n forkModal.* keys referenced from ForkPlanModal.tsx didn't exist yet → frontend would build but render raw keys at runtime.
  • No progress doc was written for this chunk.

Decision: finish R46-A in this cron slot, merge into a single R46-A progress doc with full credit to both slots, then push everything. No ADR needed (pure UX, stays inside ADR-013 + ADR-019 envelope).

docs.title: 1. GET /runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}/fork-plan — new FastAPI endpoint
docs.text:
src/chronos/api/server.py (+46 lines):

@app.get("/runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}/fork-plan")
def get_fork_plan_preview(run_id: str, node_id: str) -> JSONResponse:
    ...
    plan = build_plan(parent_run=run, parent_node=parent_node,
                      overrides={}, child_thread_id=None, reason=None, tags=[])
    downstream = [n for n in nodes if n.step_index > parent_node.step_index]
    effects_summary = build_effects_summary(downstream)
    return JSONResponse({"plan": plan.to_dict(), "effects_summary": effects_summary})
  • Reuses the build_plan + build_effects_summary pure helpers already exported from chronos.cli.fork (R45-A designed them to be console-free for exactly this purpose). Zero duplication.
  • Empty overrides={} envelope — the UX is "download the JSON, edit overrides in your editor, then chronos fork apply <plan.json>". No in-browser editing (ADR-019 explicitly rejected that: any editor invites users to assume Chronos executes the fork, which it doesn't).
  • 404 branches: "Run not found" and "Node not found" — distinct detail strings so the frontend can surface a useful message.

docs.title: 2. Frontend fetchForkPlanPreview in frontend/src/api.ts
docs.text:
Typed response envelope:

export interface ForkPlanPreviewResponse {
  plan: Record<string, unknown>;
  effects_summary: {
    total: number;
    dangerous_count: number;
    tag_counts: Record<string, number>;
    dangerous_samples: Array<[number, string, string[]]>;
  };
}

plan stays loosely typed as Record<string, unknown> — the UI just serializes it to JSON for download/copy, no structural destructuring. Keeps us decoupled from the ForkPlan Pydantic schema (R45-A still calls v1 "the v0.1.1+ contract" but the UI doesn't need to enforce shape).

docs.title: 3. ForkPlanModal component (frontend/src/components/ForkPlanModal.tsx, 252 lines)
docs.text:
AntD Modal (not Drawer) because the plan JSON is a deliverable, not a sidebar aux panel. 760px wide, footer has Close / Copy / Download buttons.

Layout top-to-bottom: 1. Intro paragraph — "Chronos plans, doesn't execute" reminder (ADR-013 in plain English). 2. Loading / error states. 3. Effects summary panel: either a warning Alert mirroring the CLI panel ("⚠ This fork re-runs N node(s) with real-world side effects", tag breakdown as Tags, up to 3 example nodes as bulleted list) — or a success Alert for the last-node/pure-LLM case. 4. Plan JSON block — dark-themed <pre> with maxHeight: 320px scroll (so 200-step runs don't blow out the modal). 5. Next-steps paragraph telling the user exactly what command to run.

Silence principle mirrored from R45-A: if dangerous_count == 0 we still show a success Alert instead of nothing, because in a modal context silence is confusing (user clicked "Fork from here" expecting feedback). CLI can silently skip the panel; modal cannot.

docs.title: 4. TreeView wiring (frontend/src/pages/TreeView.tsx, +23 lines)
docs.text:
• New state: const [forkNodeId, setForkNodeId] = useState<string | null>(null); — separate from selectedId so dismissing the fork modal doesn't close the node detail drawer behind it.
  • <NodeDetails onFork={(n) => setForkNodeId(n.id)}> — activates the pre-wired danger button from R44-A.
  • <ForkPlanModal runId={...} nodeId={forkNodeId} nodeName={...} stepIndex={...} onClose={() => setForkNodeId(null)}> — mounted alongside the Drawer.

docs.title: 5. i18n keys — this cron slot's main completion work
docs.text:
Both en.ts and zh.ts gained a full forkModal: block (19 keys: title/atNode/intro/loading/errorTitle/planJson/close/copy/copied/copyFailed/download/downloaded/nextSteps + dangerous.{title,breakdown,examples} + safe.{lastNode,pureLlm}). Without these the modal would have rendered literal "forkModal.title" strings at runtime.

Place them after effects.forkWarning — keeps fork-related copy grouped.

docs.text:

    # plan envelope: parent_run_id, parent_node_id, overrides={}, chronos_fork_plan_version=1
    # effects_summary envelope: {total, dangerous_count, tag_counts, dangerous_samples}
    # scenario has n2 (step_index=1), n3 (step_index=2) → total == 1 exactly

def test_fork_plan_preview_404_for_unknown_run(client):

def test_fork_plan_preview_404_for_unknown_node(scenario, client):
    # asserts "Node not found" in detail

The happy-path asserts on structural shape of the summary envelope (key set), not tag-specific content — because the existing scenario fixture's nodes don't carry metadata[\"effects\"], so dangerous_count == 0 is correct. Asserts total == 1 to lock the downstream-count math against future fixture drift.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• uv run pytest tests/ -q → 438 passed, 2 skipped in 12.59s (+3 from R45-A's 435).
  • Coverage 94% maintained. api/server.py at 98% (was 97%).
  • uv run ruff check src tests → All checks passed.
  • uv run ruff format --check src tests → 67 files already formatted.
  • uv run mypy src → Success: no issues found in 27 source files.
  • cd frontend && npm run build → tsc -b && vite build clean, 5.21s, one pre-existing chunk-size warning (unrelated; same warning as R44-A).

Not run this round (budget + no code change warranted): - chronos web manual browser dogfood. Next cron slot should smoke-test the modal in-browser (see R46-A followup below).

docs.title: Key facts / pitfalls surfaced
docs.text:
• build_plan + build_effects_summary are callable from the API layer without any Rich Console import. R45-A got this split right for exactly this reason — R46-A validates the separation. Note for future: anything that needs a console.print() (e.g. render_effects_preview) is NOT reusable; only the pure helpers are.
  • scenario fixture carries n2 at step_index=1 and n3 at step_index=2 — so forking at n2 has exactly 1 downstream node (n3). Locking this in the test makes it a canary if someone adds a 4th node to the fixture.
  • "Run not found" vs "Node not found" separation: always check run existence first — otherwise a bad run_id + bad node_id surfaces as "Node not found" which is wrong (run wasn't there to begin with).
  • Modal-vs-Drawer for secondary content: drawer = aux/passive (node metadata), modal = deliverable/action (fork plan). Followed R38/R39-A visual-review norms.
  • Cron slot handoff without progress doc = silent recovery burden: this round inherited live uncommitted code with broken i18n. The frontend would have built clean and shipped visibly-broken copy to any user who ran chronos web between cron rounds. Lesson: always either commit WIP behind a feature flag, or stash/reset before ending a cron — never leave half-wired runtime dependencies in working tree. Add a new CONTEXT §5 bullet for this.
  • gh-proxy.com push still the only working route (R22 fact, re-verified this round — see push log in git).

With R46-A merged, all three effect-aware UX surfaces are active:

Surface Phase 3 landing Status Adapter auto-tagging + Web UI node badge + Drawer warning banner PH3-02 (v0.3.0, R44-A) ✅ CLI fork plan downstream preview panel PH3-03 (v0.3.1, R45-A) ✅ Web UI Fork-from-tree modal with same preview PH3-04 (R46-A) ✅ (this round)

Phase 3 is functionally closed from the effect-aware-UX angle. ADR-019's "warn, don't sandbox" is now tangible from every Chronos entry point. Roadmap §Phase 3 was already signed off at commit 93b76fd (the previous cron slot).

Candidate was v0.3.2 for the new /fork-plan endpoint. Deferring because:

  3. No external consumers complaining — repo is PUBLIC but no open issues referencing this.

Next release cut candidate: v0.4.0-alpha after R46-A in-browser smoke + R46-C guide lands.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text: Phase 3's three safety layers (effect tags, CLI preview, Web modal) all shipped separately in v0.3.0/v0.3.1/R46-A. This round closed the user-facing gap: three publishable dogfood screenshots proving the Web modal works end-to-end, and a 391-line bilingual guide (docs/guides/forking-safely.md) explaining when Chronos warns you vs. stays silent and why it deliberately doesn't sandbox. Then cut v0.4.0a1 as an alpha — the bundle is production-shaped, but R48+ may extend Phase 3 (AutoGen adapter rewrite, effect-tag badge redesign) so the alpha label reserves room.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
1. Prove the R46-A Web fork modal works for non-trivial cases by capturing three dogfood screenshots with fresh seeded data (warning / safe-pure / safe-last-node).
  2. Ship docs/guides/forking-safely.md — the first user-facing synthesis of Phase 3's safety story.
  3. Cut v0.4.0-alpha bundling R46-A + R46-B + R47-A + R47-B.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Seeded dogfood.db with three hand-crafted runs using scripts/seed_r47a_effects.py:
  • r46a-warn — 5 downstream nodes, 4 carry dangerous effects covering all 4 family tags (db, network, fs, external).
  • run_a728acd21e95 — 3 downstream nodes, all pure LLM calls, 0 dangerous effects.
  • run_a6d8e2a78cef — 4 nodes total, fork target = last node, 0 downstream.
  • Ran CHRONOS_DB=dogfood.db web server on port 8768.
  • Drove the browser tool through: navigate → close tour → click run → click step 0 (or last node) → click "Fork here" in drawer → modal opens → screenshot.

docs.title: The drawer-leakage problem and its fix
docs.text:
R46-A intentionally keeps the right drawer open when the fork modal opens — users want to keep browsing node details while deciding. Good UX, but bad for docs screenshots: both panels competing for attention makes the hero image look cluttered.

Fix: do not change the code. In the browser tool, after clicking "Fork here" and waiting for the modal to mount (setTimeout(1500)), inject:

document.querySelectorAll('.ant-drawer').forEach(d => d.style.display = 'none')

via browser_console just before the screenshot. Modal stays visible, drawer disappears from the image only. Recorded as a skill candidate: web-docs-screenshot-drawer-hide.

docs.title: AntD modal mount timing
docs.text: .ant-modal-content selector returned null immediately after the click in some cases. [role="dialog"] was more reliable but also needed ~1500ms for AntD's enter animation to settle. Consistent wait > faster flaky click.

docs.title: scripts/seed_r47a_effects.py as ground truth
docs.text: The seed script is committed (197 lines, 3 runs). Anyone (future agent included) can regenerate the exact database that produced these screenshots by running uv run python scripts/seed_r47a_effects.py --db dogfood.db. This closes the loop between "the screenshot I see" and "the code that produced it" — no more mystery demos.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. R46-A does NOT ship as v0.3.2. Per CONTEXT.md §5 strategy, bundle R46-A + R46-B + R47-A + R47-B into one alpha. Single-commit patches aren't worth a release, and the fork modal lands more coherently alongside its docs.
  2. Alpha (not v0.4.0 final). Phase 3 is mostly done but not entirely — R48+ may rewrite the AutoGen adapter (currently thin), and the effect-tag badge redesign is still on the table. Alpha reserves that room.
  3. Bilingual guide, English first. Per user's repeated preference (Chinese to user, English in code/docs), forking-safely.md is ~200 lines English + ~190 lines Chinese mirror. TL;DR decision table is at the top so busy readers don't scroll.
  4. README pointer uses GFM reference links. Matches the existing [chronos-release-pattern]-style pattern in the Phase 2 row — consistency over expedience.

docs.title: Round 48-A — AutoGen effects classifier fix + ADR-020
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-27 (CST, ~01:30) Round: R48-A Theme: Close the Phase 3 blind spot — effects classifier was broken on AutoGen tool events for 4 rounds (v0.3.0 → v0.4.0a1)

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
Phase 3's fork-safety pipeline (ADR-019 + effects classifier + Web modal warning) looked like it worked across all adapters because every unit test passed. R48-A ran the first real LLM × real AutoGen tool-calling spike (spike 10) and discovered the classifier was emitting effects=[] on every single AutoGen tool node — the Web UI warning pipeline was silently blind. Root cause: the recorder synthesized node_name = "{source}:{ClassName}" (e.g. "coder:ToolCallExecutionEvent") with zero tool-function-name signal, and the classifier's keyword regexes only match function-shaped strings.

Fix: embed the FunctionCall.name from msg.content[*].name as a third segment in node_name. {source}:{EventClass}:{tool_name[+tool_name...]}. Classifier now fires. 4 new unit tests, 1 spike, 1 ADR (ADR-020 codifying the convention for future message-based adapters), + forking-safely.md §6 on per-tool effects_map overrides.

This was inherited WIP from a prior cron slot that did the spike + research + recorder fix + test scaffolding, left it uncommitted. This round (a) applied lint/format fixes (SIM108 + RUF001), (b) wrote ADR-020, (c) wrote the guide §6, (d) wrote this progress doc, (e) committed + pushed.

docs.title: Context — inherited WIP
docs.text:
Opened the round with git status showing:

  • 3 modified files: src/chronos/adapters/autogen/recorder.py, tests/unit/test_adapter_autogen.py, uv.lock
  • 2 untracked files: docs/research/r48a-autogen-tool-effects.md (162 lines), tests/spikes/spike10_autogen_tool_effects.py (229 lines)
  • 3 commits ahead of origin (v0.4.0a1 bundle from R47 — already pushed per prior log; retried push this round)

Ran the cron-slot-handoff-recovery SKILL 60-second diagnostic. Verdict: Option A — finish and commit. The prior slot did the heavy lifting (research + real-LLM spike + recorder code + tests). All tests passed in isolation. What was missing to land the work:

  1. Lint errors — SIM108 (nested if/else should be ternary) in recorder.py, RUF001 (× multiplication sign) in the spike. Fixed via patch → ruff format auto-normalized.
  2. ADR-020 — the research note's "Follow-ups" checklist said "ADR-020 codifying {source}:{Kind}:{tool_name} convention (this round)". Written (9.2 KB, three-trigger re-open rule mirroring ADR-013 / ADR-019).
  3. forking-safely.md §6 — guide never mentioned per-tool overrides. Added a bilingual (EN + 中文) section before the "Related reading" footer, with a effects_map example and a "Discovery path" debug snippet.
  4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section — rewrote from "Nothing yet — R48 will decide." to describe the fix + additions + soft break.
  5. Progress doc — this file.

docs.title: Why the bug shipped for 4 rounds
docs.text:
R44-A's classifier tests used synthetic node_name strings that were already function-shaped ("fetch_weather", "read_file"). No test ever exercised the actual AutoGen-adapter → classifier data path. The stack went green end-to-end without ever proving the pipeline worked on real adapter output.

LangGraph was accidentally fine because graph-level node names come from graph.add_node("fetch_weather", ...) — already function-shaped by construction. AutoGen, being message-based, has no natural function-shaped identifier per node; the recorder had to synthesize one and chose a shape that lost the tool name.

Lesson (added to ADR-020): "every classifier test with NodeKind.TOOL should either (a) use a name we've empirically confirmed the adapter produces, or (b) feed through the real recorder path."

docs.title: The three-segment convention
docs.text:
Decided (ADR-020) that all message-based adapters should synthesize:

{source_or_agent}:{Kind_or_ClassName}:{tool_name[+tool_name...]}

Rationale: it's cheap (~15 lines per adapter), it preserves the existing single-string effects_map contract, and it gives users per-tool × per-event × per-agent override granularity. LangGraph and other graph-based adapters are exempt — the invariant is "classifier's input contains the tool function name", not "exactly three segments".

docs.title: Soft-break on effects_map keys
docs.text: Users with old-shape keys ("coder:ToolCallExecutionEvent") will see their overrides silently no-op after upgrade. Acceptable because (a) effects on AutoGen didn't actually work before this fix, so very few users had production overrides, (b) CHANGELOG calls it out, (c) discovery path is obvious once a user inspects nodes[i].node_name.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Commit inherited WIP + new artifacts as one logical unit (Option A from the handoff skill). Don't fragment into "lint fix" + "ADR" + "guide" commits — the story is "close the Phase 3 AutoGen blind spot" and it lands as one thing.
  2. node_name shape change does NOT trigger a major version bump. Node.node_name is documented as adapter-internal; we've never promised stability. The soft-break is on effects_map keys, which is documented in the CHANGELOG as expected from an alpha → alpha transition.
  3. ADR-020 separate from ADR-019. ADR-019 is charter-level ("Chronos does not sandbox"). ADR-020 is a convention for a specific mechanism (how adapters must shape node_name so the classifier works). They live at different altitudes.
  4. No release this round. v0.4.0a2 is the natural next alpha, bundling this fix with whatever R48-B / R48-C produce (badge redesign, i18n hardening). A single-fix release would duplicate the R47 mistake of too-small releases.
  5. Spike 10 stays as a spike, not promoted to a @pytest.mark.live test this round. Research doc's Follow-ups says "consider promoting next round if OneAPI/GLM-5 remains stable" — one round of stability isn't enough yet.

docs.title: Lessons (CONTEXT.md §5 new bullet candidates)
docs.text:
• Classifier tests MUST use real adapter output, not synthetic strings. If you're testing a function that reads node.x and x is produced by adapter code, your test fixture's x must come from exercising the adapter. Otherwise you validate the function, not the integration.
  • cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill Option A works well when the prior slot did the hard thinking. Spike + research + code was all there; this round's job was to polish (lint), codify (ADR), document (guide §6), narrate (progress doc), ship. Total: ~45 minutes of agent time, no wasted work.
  • Keyword-regex classifiers are fragile to input-shape drift. When we add CrewAI / AG2, the first test must be "feed an actual adapter-produced node_name into the classifier and verify it fires". Not "unit test the classifier with a hand-chosen string".

docs.text: Pure frontend: effect-tag rendering now shows a lucide icon per family (llm → Brain, network → Globe, fs → HardDrive, db → Database, external → ExternalLink) in both the NodeDetails drawer and the ForkPlanModal. Factored out a shared EffectTag component so drawer / modal tag-count histogram / dangerous-samples list all share one render path. Zero backend / schema / API change. 442 pass / 2 skip / 94% cov unchanged. frontend tsc -b && vite build clean.

docs.title: 1. Why this round
docs.text:
CONTEXT.md §6 listed R48-B as "优先推荐" (0.5 round): before cutting v0.4.0a2 I want the visual density of the fork-safety UX to actually match the prose in forking-safely.md. Four dangerous-effect families all reading as orange-ish text chips with subtle color hue differences is readable on a 27" monitor but starts to blur at modal widths on a 13" laptop, and the dangerous_samples list in the fork modal was rendering tags as a flat "network, fs" comma-joined text rather than as chips at all.

Icons are a cheap, low-risk affordance: they raise the scan speed of a tag on a crowded screen without changing any semantics, schema, or test fixture.

docs.title: 2.1 frontend/src/components/NodeDetails.tsx
docs.text:
• Imported five lucide icons: Brain, Globe, HardDrive, Database, ExternalLink.
  • New EFFECT_ICONS map (parallel to existing EFFECT_COLORS), typed as Record<string, ComponentType<{size?: number | string}>> so unknown tags cleanly fall through (undefined → no icon).
  • Extracted EffectTag as a named export: a thin wrapper around AntD Tag that composes EFFECT_COLORS[tag] + EFFECT_ICONS[tag] + an optional label override. display: inline-flex; gap: 4px keeps the icon + text vertically centered.
  • Replaced the inline effects.map(tag => <Tag color={...}>...</Tag>) loop with <EffectTag tag={tag} label={t(...)} />. Behavior identical except for the leading 12px icon.

docs.title: 2.2 frontend/src/components/ForkPlanModal.tsx
docs.text:
• Imported the new EffectTag from ./NodeDetails.
  • Tag-count histogram in the dangerous-effects Alert: now renders <EffectTag tag={tag} label={${tag}:${n}} /> instead of <Tag color="orange">{tag}:{n}</Tag>. Biggest visible change: previously every tag was orange regardless of family, now each one wears its own color + icon.
  • Dangerous-samples list: previously <Text code>step 3</Text> name — <Text type="secondary">{tags.join(", ")}</Text>. Now each tag in the row renders as its own chip. Space size={2} with wrap keeps the layout tidy when a sample has three tags on it.
  • AntD Tag import kept in the ForkPlanModal file: the "forks at last node" geekblue chip higher up still uses raw Tag (not an effect tag), and there's no point forcing it through the new abstraction.

I'd rather fold the screenshot refresh into the v0.4.0a2 release cut (R48-C) so the release PR ships with both the badge redesign and the updated hero image in one coherent commit, rather than committing the code now and the image later.

docs.title: 5. Risks / follow-ups
docs.text:
• Icon font weight in dark mode — lucide icons inherit stroke color from CSS. AntD colored Tags set their own text color contextually; the 12px icon size should read fine in both themes, but this deserves an eyeball pass on the screenshot refresh in R48-C.
  • ExternalLink icon semantic clash — ExternalLink in lucide is the standard "opens in a new tab" arrow. Using it for the external effect family (meaning "external side effect like payment / email send") may be misread as "this opens a link". If users flag confusion during dogfood, swap to Send or Zap. Noted in follow-up but not escalated — external is the lowest-frequency effect family empirically.
  • SIM / visual-density vs. reading-speed — I didn't run an A/B comparison. The change is defensible on aesthetics; if it turns out icons slow reading (they can if icon-text binding is weak), we can drop to icon-only with i18n tooltips. Keep this in the pocket for v0.4.0a2 dogfood feedback.
  • EffectTag export from NodeDetails.tsx — the component is conceptually about effects, not about node-details specifically. Cleanest refactor is moving it to a new file EffectTag.tsx and re-exporting from NodeDetails. Didn't do that here to keep the diff small; if a third consumer appears in R49+, that's the moment to promote it.

CONTEXT §6 and the R48-B progress doc both flagged "refresh docs/images/fork-modal/01-warning.png (+ optionally 02 / 03) so the screenshots reflect the new badge icons" as an R48-C pre-cut checklist item.

Deferred to R49. Rationale:

The consequence is that for ~1 cron cycle, docs/images/fork-modal/*.png will show the pre-R48-B (single-color, no-icon) Alert. This is honest (the code that produced them was that code), and the prose in forking-safely.md is unchanged, so no text drifts.

docs.title: 2.1 tests/spikes/spike11_langgraph_tool_effects.py (new, 260 lines)
docs.text:
An offline, no-LLM-needed spike that builds a 4-node StateGraph(State) with function-shaped names intentionally chosen to trip each effect-classifier group:

plan               → pure FN / router        (expected effects: [])
fetch_weather_api  → matches NETWORK_PATTERNS (expected: ["network"])
read_file          → matches FS_PATTERNS      (expected: ["fs"])
query_db           → matches DB_PATTERNS      (expected: ["db"])

The spike runs the same compiled graph twice through LangGraphRecorder:

  • Run A (no kind_map) — all nodes default to NodeKind.FN, so classify_effects's kind == NodeKind.TOOL gate never fires, and every node gets effects=[]. Documents the real usage gotcha.
  • Run B (kind_map={"fetch_weather_api": TOOL, ...}) — tool nodes produce the expected per-node effect tag.

Four findings, all ✅ on first run:

  • F1: LangGraph node_name is single-segment and equals the add_node(name, fn) key (no prefix / suffix / colons).
  • F2: Without kind_map, every node gets effects=[] — confirms the usage trap.
  • F3: With kind_map, classifier picks the right tag per node (["network"] / ["fs"] / ["db"]).
  • F4: ADR-020 vacuously satisfied. The invariant ("classifier input contains the tool function name") is met by LangGraph's default node naming — no three-segment surgery needed.

Ruff-clean, ruff-format-clean, not collected by pytest (lives in tests/spikes/ which is pytest-excluded per spike convention).

docs.title: 2.2 docs/research/r49-langgraph-adr020-audit.md (new, 184 lines)
docs.text:
The audit closure note. Documents:

  • The spike's four findings in prose with the ADR-020 section cross-references.
  • The kind_map gotcha: LangGraph has no framework-level concept of "tool node vs function node", so the adapter conservatively defaults everything to NodeKind.FN, and the classifier correctly refuses to guess. Users who want Phase 3 effect annotations must declare their tool nodes via kind_map={"name": NodeKind.TOOL, ...}.
  • Consequence for Phase 3 UX: LangGraph users who don't know about kind_map will silently see green "no dangerous side effects" fork-modal Alerts even when their graph writes files / hits HTTP / queries DBs. Silent false-safety is worse than a loud false-alarm, which is why documentation is the remediation, not a code change.
  • Recommendations:
  • Add a one-paragraph note to LangGraphRecorder.__init__ docstring telling users to pass kind_map if they want effect annotations (R50 candidate patch, bundled with the screenshot refresh).
  • Amend ADR-020 follow-ups to mark LangGraph closed (done this round).
  • No test suite addition needed — the classifier pipeline is already covered by tests/unit/test_effects_classify.py (R44-A) and tests/integration/test_dual_adapter_dogfood.py.
  • Explicit non-targets: langgraph.prebuilt.ToolNode branches and subgraph-as-node behavior. Both are expected-but-unverified; neither is blocking R49 and neither is currently in any Chronos test path.

docs.text:
CONTEXT.md §6 (R48-C) named this an R49 must-do. It is deferred again for the same reason R48-C deferred it from R48-C itself: the wall-time risk profile inside a cron slot is wrong.

  • No Playwright is in pyproject.toml deps; installing it in-slot risks a 2-3 minute uv sync + browser download (~400 MB Chromium).
  • The Vite dev server needs cold-build and bind-port negotiation.
  • The hot-reload race between seed DB → API restart → dev-server re-fetch is well-known to be flaky on first attempt.
  • R49 has one low-risk deliverable (the audit) and one high-risk deliverable (the screenshots). Shipping the audit alone is strictly better than failing to ship both.

R50 plan for the screenshots (documented so next round's agent doesn't re-litigate):

  1. Add playwright to [project.optional-dependencies.dev] or a new [project.optional-dependencies.screenshots] group.
  2. Write scripts/capture_fork_modal.py that:
  3. Opens SqliteStore.open(dogfood.db) and runs scripts/seed_r47a_effects.py if the three runs are absent.
  4. Launches chronos web --no-browser --db dogfood.db in a subprocess.
  5. Launches cd frontend && npm run dev in a subprocess (or uses the pre-built frontend/dist/ via CHRONOS_FRONTEND_DIST).
  6. Uses Playwright async API to open three pages (#/runs/<warn>, #/runs/<safe>, #/runs/<lastnode>), click the fork-plan CTA, wait for the modal, save the three PNGs to docs/images/fork-modal/{01,02,03}-<suffix>.png.
  7. Document the script in docs/guides/screenshot-capture.md (new).
  8. Run the script, commit the three new PNGs, update docs/forking-safely.md image references if the filenames changed.

Work budget estimate: 1 full R50 slot.

Loud false-alarm is annoying; silent false-safety is a fork-time footgun.

Both items are strictly docs-or-docstring — the riskiest work in R50 was the browser capture flow, which the pre-existing chronos-docs-screenshots skill already documented down to "hide the Drawer with a CSS override before screenshotting the Modal".

docs.title: 2.1 LangGraph docstring warning (<20-line change)
docs.text:
src/chronos/adapters/langgraph.py — inserted after the kind_map Args entry on the LangGraphRecorder class docstring:

.. warning::
    **Pass ``kind_map`` for any node that performs I/O** (network calls,
    filesystem writes, database access, external subprocess) if you rely
    on Phase 3 fork-plan *effect annotations* (the dangerous-effect
    warnings shown in the Web fork modal and CLI ``fork-plan``).

    LangGraph adapters have no reliable way to infer a node's kind from
    the graph alone, so un-mapped nodes fall back to
    :attr:`NodeKind.FN`. The effects classifier's TOOL-gate then
    short-circuits those nodes to ``effects=[]``, which looks like
    *safe-to-fork* in the UI — even if the node actually hits the
    network. This is silent false-safety, which is strictly worse than
    a loud false-alarm.

    Explicitly mark I/O-doing nodes as :attr:`NodeKind.TOOL` in
    ``kind_map`` to opt them into effect annotation. See
    ``docs/research/r49-langgraph-adr020-audit.md`` for an empirical
    walkthrough (spike 11).

First draft also mentioned NodeKind.IO as an alternative — caught myself pre-commit (IO does not exist; only LLM/TOOL/FN/ROUTER/FORK/END). Trimmed to NodeKind.TOOL only. Lesson noted for future adapter docs: verify enum surface before citing it, even in a docstring.

docs.title: 2.2 Fork-modal screenshot recipe (3 PNGs, all R48-B-styled)
docs.text:
Used the chronos-docs-screenshots skill's "Fork Modal Screenshot Recipe" section verbatim:

  1. uv run python scripts/seed_r47a_effects.py --db /tmp/chronos-r50.db → three runs (warn / safe / lastnode).
  2. uv run chronos web --db /tmp/chronos-r50.db --no-browser --port 8765 in a watched background process. curl /healthz confirmed boot.
  3. For each scenario: browser_navigate to the run URL, close the Tour on first visit, click the target node's inner generic (NOT the group ref), click "Fork here" in the Drawer, wait ~1.5 s, then inject document.querySelectorAll('.ant-drawer').forEach(d => d.style.display='none') to hide the Drawer behind the Modal.
  4. browser_vision for one final QA pass, then copy the cached screenshot into docs/images/fork-modal/.
# Scenario Run Node Alert colour Effect-tag icons rendered? 01 Warning run_25b301997e6f (warn) step 0 plan_agent Amber / warning ✅ 4 badges (db / network / fs / external) with lucide icons 02 Safe — pure LLM run_3fc9ecfa7954 (safe) step 0 plan Green / success ✅ (trivially — zero dangerous tags, so zero badges is the point) 03 Safe — last node run_9265693398c2 (lastnode) step 1 answer Green / success ✅ (trivially — zero downstream)

docs.title: 3.3 CliRunner stderr capture regression (R52 blocker)
docs.text:
click>=8.2 / typer>=0.22 changed the default CliRunner(mix_stderr) behaviour — stderr now always goes into result.output combined with stdout unless you pass mix_stderr=False. That makes accessing result.stderr raise ValueError: stderr not separately captured. Our test suite (tests/unit/test_cli.py) uses the combined-read pattern on exactly the affected code paths. Two clean fixes:

  1. Easy: replace the module-level runner = CliRunner() with runner = CliRunner(mix_stderr=False) at tests/unit/test_cli.py:~1. Expected to green all 7 failures.
  2. Safer long-term: pin click>=8.1,<8.2 and typer>=0.12,<0.22 in pyproject.toml until we decide to migrate.

R52 should go with option 1 — pinning ops-level tools fixes the symptom but invites rot. Migrating to mix_stderr=False is strictly a better test-fixture, matches what click's own docs recommend as of 8.2.

docs.title: 2. What the inherited scaffold actually implements (ADR-021 D1–D8 audit)
docs.text:
This section is the hermeneutic audit — walk each ADR-021 Decision, confirm the code satisfies it. Done as part of the "verify shape before commit" close-out step in Option A2.

ADR-021 § Decision Implemented where Verified D1 scoped_handlers() CM + flush(timeout=flush_timeout_s) barrier recorder.py::CrewAIRecorder.record() — with crewai_event_bus.scoped_handlers(): ... crewai_event_bus.flush(timeout=self._flush_timeout_s) in both success else and exception branches ✅ (also covered by TestRecordCM.test_record_flushes_before_draining via _FakeEventBus) D2 threading.Lock + list buffer, handlers push through lock recorder.py::CrewAIRecorder._append + _lock: threading.Lock + _buffer: list[_PendingNode] ✅ (also covered by TestThreadSafety.test_concurrent_appends_no_drop using ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) firing 30 synthetic events, asserting buffer length = 30) D3 Three-segment node_name matching ADR-020 recorder.py::{_tool,_llm,_task,_end}_node_name — "{agent_role}:{EventClassName}:{tool_name}" etc. ✅ (covered by TestHelpers.test_*_node_name_*) D4 Default kind_map over 7 event classes, kind_map override merges over default recorder.py::_DEFAULT_KIND_MAP (Task→FN, ToolUsage→TOOL, LLMCall*→LLM, CrewKickoffCompleted→END) + CrewAIRecorder.__init__ merges kind_map over default ✅ (covered by TestHandlers.test_kind_map_override) D5 Sync Crew.kickoff — no ADR-017 asyncio wrap record() is @contextmanager over a plain generator, no asyncio.run in sight ✅ (contextmanager shape matches AutoGen's sync path, not AutoGen's asyncio.run wrap) D6 Telemetry kill-switches documented, not encoded Documented in ADR-021 §D6, spike12 docstring, and chronos-spike-authoring skill — intentionally not env-bashed by the adapter so the adapter stays importable in test envs that never touch real crewai. Recorder record() lazy-imports crewai.events so module import is free of CrewAI telemetry. ✅ (test suite proves the module imports without crewai installed) D7 usage_extractor callback unsupported, raises AdapterError __init__.py::_CrewAIAdapter.build_recorder — if usage_extractor is not None: raise AdapterError(...) ✅ (covered by TestAdapterFactory.test_usage_extractor_rejected) D8 Version pin crewai>=0.80,<1.0 pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] crewai + _CrewAIAdapter.version_constraint = ">=0.80,<1.0" + ImportError → AdapterError in record() with explicit install hint ✅

No deviations. The inherited scaffold is a faithful implementation of ADR-021. The effects classifier (R44-A) is wired through _persist_run_and_nodes — classify_effects(node_name=..., kind=..., model_name=...) — so a future spike13 real-LLM run will get effect tags on TOOL nodes for free.

docs.title: Minor ergonomic beats worth noting
docs.text:
• record_from_pending() replaced by _drain_buffer_to_store() test hook — the inherited scaffold gives tests a direct _drain_buffer_to_store(ref=..., ...) hook that reads buffer under lock and clears it, so tests can exercise handlers without running a real event bus. TestDrain uses it extensively. Name is underscore-private so it doesn't bloat the public surface.
  • _FakeEventBus in test_adapter_crewai.py — a ~100-line handcrafted fake that mirrors CrewAI 0.80's scoped_handlers() + on(event_type)(handler) + flush(timeout=...) contract closely enough that the record CM can be driven end-to-end. Proves the CM lifecycle (attach → yield → flush-on-success → drain → detach) on a non-CrewAI environment. This is how we end up green without the real crewai dep.
  • Optional CrewKickoffCompletedEvent import — ADR-021 §D4 lists it in the default kind map, but CrewAI has moved that class across subpackages across minor versions. The recorder wraps the import in its own try/except ImportError and only subscribes _on_end_event if the class is available. Failure mode: CrewKickoffCompletedEvent-less installs get a run with no explicit END node, but all other events still record. This matches ADR-021's "make events optional at the right granularity" posture.
  • _persist_failed_shell() — writes a minimal failed Run when the with block body raises, so partial runs aren't orphaned. Same pattern as AutoGen's failure path.

docs.title: Round 53 — ADR-022: CrewAI pin bump <1.0 → <2.0 (spike13a surface probe)
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-07 (CST 09:00 cron slot, inside 0–11 window) Prior round: 2026-05-07-round-52.md — CrewAI adapter scaffold landed per ADR-021 §D1–§D8; 474 pass / 32 new duck tests. Status: ✅ Shipped — ADR-022 written, pin bumped, gates green, scope re-planned.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
R53 went in expecting to write spike13_crewai_tool_effects.py (2-agent crew, 3 tools, real LLM via baidu-int OneAPI) per CONTEXT §6. The first check of the environment revealed:

$ .venv/bin/python -c "import crewai; print(crewai.__version__)"
1.14.3

…while the R52 scaffold's pin was crewai>=0.80,<1.0. The pin was documented as pre-emptive in ADR-021 §D8 ("CrewAI hasn't cut a 1.0 yet"), i.e. it was a guess that is now empirically falsified. Two ways to proceed:

  1. Install crewai<1.0 into the environment, run spike13 against the old line, keep the pin.
  2. Verify CrewAI 1.x didn't break the event-bus, write a revision ADR, bump the pin, defer spike13 P0 one round.

Option (2) was picked because (a) pinning to a past-EOL line is hostile to every downstream user, (b) a 30-minute surface probe (spike13a) would tell us whether the event-bus API actually broke or whether the pin was just tight. The probe found CrewAI 1.14.3 is a source-compatible superset of 0.80+ on every ADR-021 §D1–§D7 surface the recorder uses. The R52 scaffold needs zero code changes.

  • Final gate: 474 passed / 2 skipped / 94% cov (unchanged from R52 — no new tests, this is a pin-and-ADR round).
  • mypy src/ ✅ 29 files; ruff check ✅; ruff format --check ✅.
  • Written: ADR-022 (~250 lines); spike13a_crewai14_event_bus_probe.py (~165 lines, green end-to-end).
  • Edited: pyproject.toml crewai pin; _CrewAIAdapter.version_constraint; recorder error-message hint.
  • CONTEXT §5/§6 refreshed; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] gets an R53 Changed block.
  • Slid: R53 P0 (real-LLM spike13_crewai_tool_effects.py) → R54 P0. R53 P1 (research note) / R53 P2 (v0.4.0 release) also slide by one. The slide is cheap: R52's 32-duck-test surface + R53's real-surface probe together give us confidence R54 P0 can proceed.

docs.title: 1.1 Pre-flight discovery
docs.text:
The plan for this cron slot was CONTEXT §6 R53 P0 verbatim: write tests/spikes/spike13_crewai_tool_effects.py modeled on spike10_autogen_tool_effects.py, assert F1–F6, run against baidu-int OneAPI. Standard pre-flight:

$ cd /workspace/chronos-agent
$ set -a; source /workspace/.hermes/.env; set +a  # OneAPI key loaded
$ .venv/bin/python -c "import crewai; print(crewai.__version__)"
1.14.3

R52 pinned crewai>=0.80,<1.0. The pin can't be "respected" without pip install 'crewai<1.0' — and the installed 1.14.3 came from some Phase 2/3 transitive dependency (uv sync against the current lock). Dropping back to 0.95 meant fighting the resolver and locking Chronos to a past-EOL line. That was the fork in the road.

docs.title: 1.2 Two-minute triage per ADR-021 §D8's own language
docs.text:
Re-reading ADR-021 §D8:

Pin upper bound at < 1.0 pre-emptively — CrewAI hasn't cut a 1.0 yet and the event schema is explicitly marked unstable in their docs.

That's the decision, stated as pre-emptive, not empirical. A pre-emptive pin that's been falsified by reality is a pin revision, not a scaffold bug. This matches the precedent from ADR-013 / ADR-019 / ADR-020 — ADRs can be revised once empirical evidence replaces prior guesses.

docs.title: 1.3 The decision
docs.text:
• R53 scope pivot: instead of spike13 P0 (real LLM, 2-3 hr wall clock, first leg requires the pin fixed anyway), do ADR-022 + spike13a_crewai14_event_bus_probe.py + pin bump. Self-contained 30-min deliverable. R53 P0 slides to R54.
  • No change to ADR-021 D1–D7 — the pivot is a version-pin revision, not an architectural re-think. The D1–D7 event-bus design survives CrewAI 1.0 entirely.
  • This is not drift. CONTEXT §6 explicitly lists "R53 known failure paths" and CrewAI version pin issues weren't among them — but CONTEXT §6 also says "If R53 discovers a real-world blocker, adjust scope and ratify with an ADR." That's exactly what we did.

docs.title: 2. spike13a findings (R52 scaffold × CrewAI 1.14.3)
docs.text:
tests/spikes/spike13a_crewai14_event_bus_probe.py is a surface probe, not a real-LLM spike. It imports the live crewai package, pokes every public API the R52 scaffold uses, fires one synthetic ToolUsageStartedEvent through the real bus, and drives CrewAIRecorder.record() end-to-end with a stubbed _FakeCrew.

F# Probe Result on 1.14.3 F0 crewai.__version__, crewai_event_bus importable 1.14.3, CrewAIEventsBus singleton present F0 scoped_handlers, flush, on, emit all on bus ✅ all present with same signatures F1 ToolUsage{Started,Finished}Event, LLMCall{Started,Completed}Event, Task{Started,Completed}Event import from crewai.events ✅ all import F1 CrewKickoffCompletedEvent from crewai.events.types.crew_events ✅ imports (ADR-021 §D4 "optional" path is unnecessary on 1.14.3; the optional-import guard is still good to have for older lines) F2 scoped_handlers() CM attaches and detaches cleanly around a real bus.emit(_Src(), event=ToolUsageStartedEvent(...)) ✅ received=['tus:probe_tool'], bus flushed clean F3 R52 crewai_adapter.build_recorder(store) returns CrewAIRecorder and record() CM completes with a stubbed crew + 1 synthetic event ✅ run_id + 1 node persisted

Net: zero surgery to the R52 scaffold needed. The 32 duck tests in test_adapter_crewai.py continue to pass against the live 1.14.3 resolver because they use _FakeEventBus (which matches the real API shape verified above).

Limitation acknowledged: spike13a only tests the surface. It emits one synthetic event. It does not certify that a real Crew.kickoff() run produces well-formed ToolUsage*Event / LLMCall*Event payloads end-to-end with effect classification firing correctly. That's R54 P0's job. spike13a's only deliverable is "the pin bump is safe"; it cannot and does not replace the real-LLM smoke.

docs.title: 3. ADR-022 summary
docs.text:
Full text: docs/decisions/ADR-022-crewai-version-pin-bump.md. One-line: CrewAI optional-dep upper bound goes from <1.0 to <2.0; floor stays at 0.80; ADR-021 §D1–§D7 untouched.

Rationale chain:

  • ADR-021 §D8 pin was explicitly pre-emptive ("CrewAI hasn't cut a 1.0 yet").
  • CrewAI 1.x exists; the environment already has 1.14.3.
  • spike13a empirically verifies the event-bus surface is unchanged.
  • <2.0 is SemVer-correct — we get one more major version's worth of runway before having to re-examine.

Consequences documented: no schema change, no CHANGELOG user-facing behavior change, no CLI/API/DB change. It's a manifest + ADR bump.

Three-trigger re-open rule inherits from ADR-021 with CrewAI-version-specific triggers layered on (breaking minor, CrewAI 2.0, observed 0.80–1.14 range failure). One of those fires → revisit the pin.

docs.title: 6. Decisions and rationale captured
docs.text:
• Why a new ADR (-022) instead of editing ADR-021 §D8 in place? — ADR-021 is Accepted. Accepted ADRs are append-only; revisions need their own ADR that cites the prior by number. This preserves the empirical trail (ADR-021 §D8 was correct on 2026-04-27; the pin bump is a later empirical finding). Future rounds reading ADR-021 will find ADR-022 listed in cross-references.
  • Why <2.0 specifically? — SemVer upper bound. CrewAI 2.0 is a future unknown; we reserve the option to re-examine at that boundary instead of letting unbounded pins silently absorb breakage. <3.0 would be a stronger bet than the empirical evidence justifies. Exactly one SemVer major of runway.
  • Why not install crewai<1.0 and keep the pin? — Locks us to a past-EOL line; hostile to downstream users; doesn't solve the underlying problem (the pin's claim that 1.x would break is unverified). The cost of the 30-minute surface probe is lower than the ongoing tax of pinning to a dead line.
  • Why defer R53 P0 one round instead of doing it this slot? — Budget. Real-LLM spike is 2–3 hr wall clock (first-party CrewAI + real LLM call latency). 30 min pin/probe/ADR fits a single slot cleanly; the combined 3+ hr work risks a third consecutive Option A2 handoff.
  • Why no spike12 amendment? — spike12 characterized CrewAI 0.80+ event bus on synthetic events. It's still correct for the 0.80 floor. spike13a is a separate artifact that characterizes 1.14.3. Both live side by side.

docs.title: R53 lesson — "pre-emptive pin" is a smell
docs.text: ADR-021 §D8's original rationale explicitly said "pre-emptive". A pre-emptive upper bound is a load-bearing guess; guesses get falsified. Future ADRs with <MAJOR upper bounds should (a) state the guess explicitly (good: ADR-021 did), (b) include a one-line test script that invalidates the pin the moment the ecosystem moves past it — so the next cron slot auto-discovers the falsification. That's a chronos-spike-authoring skill enhancement candidate, not in scope this round.

docs.title: R53 lesson — spike13a is the template for "pin bump spike"
docs.text: The probe style (surface check → module path check → handler lifecycle check → scaffold CM check, no real LLM, ~150 lines, ~2 min runtime) is reusable whenever chronos-agent hits the same shape: "our pin says this upstream version shouldn't work, but the ecosystem says it does". Capture in chronos-spike-authoring skill if the pattern recurs.

docs.title: R53 lesson — the R52 Option A2 handoff was structurally load-bearing

If R52 had shipped the scaffold with the pin bug embedded (e.g. because the cron-slot-handoff-recovery checklist didn't include "try actually importing the target extra under the current env"), R53 would have spent half its budget debugging a Heisenbug instead of writing ADR-022 cleanly. Noted for the next time the skill is touched.

docs.title: 1.1 CrewAI LLM wiring — a gotcha
docs.text:
CrewAI 1.x's LLM(...) constructor routes model strings through a native-provider constants table (openai, anthropic, azure, bedrock, gemini, deepseek, ...). Passing model="openai/GLM-5" fails because GLM-5 is not in the OpenAI constants list, and CrewAI falls through to LiteLLM — which isn't installed in our env.

Workaround: pass provider="openai" explicitly. That bypasses the constants check and routes straight to CrewAI's native OpenAI completion client, which is what OneAPI speaks:

llm = LLM(
    model="GLM-5",
    provider="openai",
    api_key=api_key,
    base_url="https://oneapi-comate.baidu-int.com/v1",
)

This is the OneAPI + CrewAI recipe — captured in the spike13 docstring. Candidate to bubble up to the CONTEXT.md "OneAPI recipes (R17/R18)" list; adding it in CONTEXT §5 tail-end lesson block rather than creating a dedicated ADR (it's a wiring detail, not a design decision).

docs.title: 2.1 Design
docs.text:
Modelled on spike10_autogen_tool_effects.py for shape consistency. Differences:

AutoGen spike10 CrewAI spike13 AssistantAgent + RoundRobinGroupChat Agent + Crew(Process.sequential) FunctionTool(fn, description=...) @tool("name") decorator on fn team.run(task=...) coroutine crew.kickoff(inputs={...}) sync asyncio.run(...) around run bare sync call (ADR-021 §D5) 1 task (group chat terminates on MaxMessageTermination) 2 tasks (investigate + summarize, sequential) Expected nodes: ~10–15 (ToolCall* pairs + LLM) Expected nodes: ~10–15 (Task + LLM pair + ToolUsage pair)

Three tools kept the same names across both spikes so the effects classifier code path is identical — fetch_weather_api → network, read_file → fs, query_db → db.

Assertions kept 1:1 in spirit with CONTEXT §6 R54 P0 F1–F6, with one documented relaxation: F2's node-count bar was lowered from ≥10 to ≥4 because CrewAI's event density is highly LLM-dependent and a strict ≥10 bound would make the spike brittle if the model chose a shorter path. The actual run produced 13 nodes on the first try, so the relaxation was not load-bearing — it's future-proofing.

docs.title: 2.4 Honest caveats
docs.text:
• Only 1 of 3 tools was called. The LLM picked fetch_weather_api for the Beijing-weather question and ignored read_file / query_db. F3 is met for the one tool that fired, and the other two tools' classifier mappings are already unit-tested in tests/unit/test_effects.py (R44-A). A future spike could use three separate prompts or a forced-tool harness for full 3-way classifier coverage. Captured in r51-crewai-event-bus-characterization.md §6 "gaps".
  • F1 uses an indirect signal. The bus's _handlers attribute wasn't readable in the way we expected at probe time; we fell back to "CM exit didn't throw + flush() after record didn't error" as the leak-free signal. This is weaker than a structural handler-registry diff, but is stable against CrewAI bus internals renaming private attrs. Noted for future tightening if a public-ish introspection hook appears.
  • LLMCall*Event.model = "GLM-5", which is the OneAPI channel name, not the underlying model. Fine for accounting; captured in node model_name as-is.
  • Task node_name third segment is the task_name fallback of "unknown" in code, but on 1.14.3 the Task.description leaks into the third segment (see spike13 output step=0 / 7 / 8 / 11 — the description text appears after the class name). Looking at the recorder, _task_node_name uses getattr(event, "task_name", None) or "unknown"; on 1.14.3 that attribute resolves to the description verbatim. Not a bug — just a slight cosmetic oddity; the classifier doesn't fire on FN kind so nothing breaks. Worth a follow-up to truncate long task_name segments for display, but not in R54 scope.

docs.title: 7. Decisions and rationale captured
docs.text:
• Why provider="openai" instead of model="openai/GLM-5"? — CrewAI 1.x validates native-provider model strings against a constants table. GLM-5 is not an OpenAI model constant, so the openai/GLM-5 route falls through to LiteLLM (not installed). Explicit provider="openai" bypasses the constants check and routes straight to the native OpenAI chat client, which speaks OneAPI's /v1/chat/completions endpoint fine. Captured inline in spike13 docstring and here. Not an ADR-worthy decision — it's a wiring quirk of CrewAI's LLM factory.
  • Why relax F2 from >= 10 to >= 4? — CrewAI's event density is bounded by the LLM's decisions (tool-use count, re-invocation iterations). A hard ≥10 bound could fail spuriously on a shorter run even when the recorder is correct. ≥4 catches the degenerate cases (zero tools, no tasks) without being brittle. Actual run produced 13, so the relaxation wasn't load-bearing — it's future-proofing.
  • Why defer v0.4.0 non-alpha one round? — Live-smoke discipline: prior live evidence is always wrapped in @pytest.mark.live tests in tests/live/ so future engineers can re-verify. Cutting v0.4.0 on a standalone spike script regresses that. 30-min R55 P0 wrap is cheap.
  • Why only 1 tool fired in F3? — LLM behaviour; not the adapter's fault. The question "what's the weather in Beijing?" only needs fetch_weather_api. Full 3-way classifier coverage is already in tests/unit/test_effects.py (R44-A) as pure-function tests, which spike13 doesn't replace.

docs.title: R54 lesson — CrewAI's native-provider routing has a constants gate
docs.text:
The model="openai/GLM-5" route goes through a constants validation step that rejects non-OpenAI model names, then falls back to LiteLLM if present. OneAPI routes a lot of non-OpenAI-named models through /v1/chat/completions under vendor-assigned names; the way to hit the native OpenAI client is provider="openai" bypass.

Candidate for the CONTEXT §5 "OneAPI recipes" block — "for CrewAI, use provider='openai' not model='openai/...' when using non-OpenAI-named OneAPI channels". Added in this round's CONTEXT refresh.

The "surface probe → real-LLM smoke → research doc promotion" chain (spike13a → spike13 → r51-*.md) is a reusable pattern for any new adapter landing that spans multiple rounds. The probe is cheap insurance against pin / API drift; the smoke validates end-to-end behaviour; the research doc stitches both with the ADR's claims for the next cron agent.

docs.title: 2.1 Design
docs.text:
Modelled directly on tests/live/test_real_llm_smoke.py (R37-A1 + R48-A pattern), which already hosts a LangGraph live smoke and an AutoGen live smoke. Shape:

  1. Module-level pytestmark list with three skipif:
  2. CHRONOS_LIVE != "1" (opt-in gate, matches existing live tests)
  3. OPENAI_API_KEY missing (API key guard)
  4. crewai not importable (optional dep guard — CrewAI is in [project.optional-dependencies].crewai, not core)
  5. sqlite_store fixture using tmp_path / "crewai_smoke.db" (isolated per run; spike13 used tempfile.mkdtemp which is fine for a one-shot script but pytest's tmp_path is idiomatic).
  6. Single test function test_crewai_tool_effects_smoke(sqlite_store, tmp_path) that does, in order:
  7. Builds the three @tool("fetch_weather_api" / "read_file" / "query_db") decorated functions inside the test (same stubs as spike13).
  8. Creates LLM(provider="openai", model=GLM-5, ...) — the R54 CrewAI + OneAPI recipe (explicit provider="openai" bypasses LiteLLM native-constants validation).
  9. Builds the investigator / summarizer agents, the two sequential tasks, the Crew(Process.sequential).
  10. Snapshots id(crew) pre-record (F5) and crewai_event_bus._handlers key list pre-record (F1).
  11. Enters rec.record(crew, thread_id=..., ...) CM, calls crew.kickoff(inputs={}), calls ref.submit_result(result).
  12. Post-CM: F1 handler-keys snapshot compared to pre; F5 id(crew) compared.
  13. F2 asserts len(nodes) >= 4 (spike13 observed 13; >= 4 is a safe floor that tolerates LLM path variation).
  14. F3 iterates ToolUsage* nodes and asserts the expected effect tag for each known tool_name.
  15. F4 soft-skips if no LLMCallCompletedEvent nodes exist OR if all usages are None (ADR-021 §D7 tolerance). If at least one usage is populated, assert prompt_tokens >= 0 and completion_tokens >= 0 for each — since CrewAI's Usage proto can legally be 0 on some channels, a strict > 0 would be over-specification.
  16. Closes sqlite_store (SQLite flush), then spawns .venv/bin/chronos runs list --db <path> and .venv/bin/chronos runs show <run_id> --db <path> subprocesses (F6), asserts exit 0 on both and that the run_id[:8] prefix appears in the list stdout.

docs.title: 2.2 Spec vs spike13 deltas
docs.text:
spike13 (standalone, stdout-report) test_crewai_smoke (pytest) print("[OK] ...") / print("[F? ❌] ...") assert ... / pytest.skip(...) Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="spike13_")) / "spike13.db" tmp_path / "crewai_smoke.db" F4 prints note even when all usage is None F4 pytest.skip(...) when all usage is None F3 unknown tool → print("[F3 ??]") F3 unknown tool → silently skip (not a contract violation per R54 finding: LLMs pick 1/3 tools per run) Module-level from crewai ... import Imports inside the test function (so @pytest.mark.skipif(not crewai_importable) can actually skip instead of erroring at collection) Exit code returned from main() Test fails on any assertion, skips on any guard

No logic deletions: every F1-F6 check survives the port. The only "loosened" branch is F4 (was "print and continue" in the spike; now pytest.skip with a self-explanatory reason because the ADR-021 §D7 tolerance would otherwise become an assertion hang).

docs.title: 2.3 Ruff gotcha — RUF002 × in docstring
docs.text: First draft used "Real CrewAI crew × real LLM × CrewAIRecorder" in the test docstring. Ruff RUF002 flagged U+00D7 (MULTIPLICATION SIGN) as ambiguous — per the existing CONTEXT §5 "Em-dash / U+2212 minus / × 乘号被 ruff RUF001 禁 (仅 py 源码, md 文档 OK)" invariant. Fixed by replacing × with + in the docstring. Zero behaviour impact, ruff clean after the patch.

docs.title: 2.4 Local verification
docs.text:
$ cd /workspace/chronos-agent
$ set -a && source /workspace/.hermes/.env && set +a
$ CHRONOS_LIVE=1 CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true \
  .venv/bin/pytest tests/live/test_crewai_smoke.py -m live -v --no-cov
...
tests/live/test_crewai_smoke.py::test_crewai_tool_effects_smoke PASSED   [100%]
======================= 1 passed, 12 warnings in 53.60s ========================

All 12 warnings are CrewAI's own DeprecationWarning noise (allow_code_execution, planning_config, multimodal on agent/crew internals) — unrelated to the adapter, same warnings fired in spike13. Wall-clock sits comfortably under the 60s soft target mentioned in the test module docstring.

docs.title: 2.5 Non-live suite — unchanged behavior
docs.text:
$ .venv/bin/pytest -q
474 passed, 3 skipped in 15.57s

The +1 skipped (was 2 from R54) is exactly the new live test being collected and gated out when CHRONOS_LIVE is unset. Coverage held at 94%.

docs.title: 3. R55 P1 — v0.4.0 non-alpha cut
docs.text:
Followed the chronos-release-pattern skill step-by-step for the 12th time (prior: R13 / R16 / R19 / R22 / R23 / R30 / R35-A / R38 / R41 / R47 / R48-C). Skill inputs all satisfied at P0 exit:

  • [Unreleased] non-empty with substantive content (R49-R55).
  • Ruff / format / mypy / pytest all green.
  • No uv.lock drift (didn't run uv sync this slot).
  • Semver target = 0.4.0 — minor bump from 0.4.0a2 (drop alpha suffix). New CrewAI adapter is minor-level feature surface; no breaking changes to existing LangGraph / AutoGen paths or to ForkPlan / Extractor v2 / Adapter / ADR-020 contracts.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-step
docs.text:
1. CHANGELOG.md roll — renamed ## [Unreleased] → ## [0.4.0] — 2026-05-08 (Round 49 + Round 50 + Round 51 + Round 52 + Round 53 + Round 54 + Round 55), inserted new empty ## [Unreleased] with _Nothing yet — R56 will decide._ placeholder. Added a theme paragraph summarising the seven-round CrewAI arc (ADR-021 §D1–§D7 empirically validated, ADR-022 revised §D8; scaffold zero-delta). Added a new R55 Added block above R54's.
  2. Version bumps (three-way lockstep):
  3. src/chronos/__init__.py::__version__ — "0.4.0a2" → "0.4.0".
  4. pyproject.toml::project.version — "0.4.0a2" → "0.4.0".
  5. src/chronos/cli/__init__.py::info status line — appended "CrewAI adapter (ADR-021 + ADR-022), " before the closing "v0.4.0a2" → "v0.4.0".
  6. CONTEXT.md §5 / §6 refresh — see §4 below.
  7. R55 progress doc — this file.
  8. Full-green verify: ruff check ✅ / ruff format --check ✅ / mypy src/ ✅ (29 files) / pytest -q ✅ (474 / 3 skip / 94% cov) / chronos --version → chronos 0.4.0.
  9. Commit — R55: live pytest wrap + v0.4.0: CrewAI adapter end-to-end with the 7-line body the skill template prescribes.

  11. GitHub Release page — POST /repos/chengfei867/chronos-agent/releases via urllib.request, prerelease=false.

No pitfalls hit. The pre-release grep sweeps (grep -nE "⏳|pending|target R[0-9]+" docs/roadmap.md, grep -rnE "phase [0-9]|v0\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+" tests/) both came up empty — the R50 → R54 rounds had already kept roadmap + test strings current, so no last-minute drift fixes were needed.

§6 pivots to Round 56 options: - Option A (首选): README + docs polish for v0.4.0 — add a CrewAI section to the README adapter table, update the feature list, add a CrewAI example to docs/guides/forking-safely.md (currently only LangGraph + AutoGen examples). Higher-leverage but open-ended. 60-90 min. - Option C: Adapter #4 exploration — begin evaluating Swarm / OpenAI Assistants / Anthropic's Agent SDK as the next adapter target. docs.text:

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
R56 is a textbook "post-release polish" round. R55 cut v0.4.0 and shipped the CrewAI adapter end-to-end but the discoverability surface (README, user guide, roadmap) still described a Phase-2-era project: "LangGraph + Linear today", "additional adapters (AutoGen / CrewAI ...) in next phases", etc. Four docs were out of sync with what the tagged release actually contains:

  1. README.md — status table listed LangGraph + Linear only; repo-layout comment said "LangGraph + Linear today"; test-count was 380+ (actual: 474 pass / 3 skip).
  2. docs/guides/forking-safely.md — had a per-tool override section for AutoGen (§6) but no CrewAI section despite CrewAI being the whole reason v0.4.0 was cut.
  3. docs/roadmap.md — Phase 3 was listed as "3.5 rounds landed" with [ ] R46-A candidate for the TreeView fork modal (actually landed in R47) and Phase 4 listed CrewAI as a candidate (actually shipped in v0.4.0).
  4. No explicit framing for what Phase 4 is supposed to be. The CONTEXT §6 R56 plan listed Option A (docs polish, chose), Option B (Phase 4 charter + ADR-023 skeleton), Option C (adapter #4 eval). Option A + Option B fit in one slot.

Total write-only round. src/ untouched. Gates: 474 pass / 3 skip / 94% cov (unchanged); 0 broken markdown links verified post-edit; ruff/mypy N/A (no .py touched).

docs.title: 2.1 README.md — five targeted edits
docs.text:
Did not rewrite the README wholesale. Five precise patches, each land-focused:

  1. "100% AI-generated" tagline — added a subclause calling out the R49-R55 seven-round arc as evidence of end-to-end autonomy. This is a strategic R33-era talking point (chronos-agent's marketing edge is "100% AI"), and the CrewAI arc is the first multi-round arc with a clean narrative the public can see.
  2. EN Status section — replaced the Phase-2-era table with a three-adapter-matrix table (LangGraph row, AutoGen row, CrewAI row each explicit), reference-style links to ADR-020 / ADR-021 / ADR-022, headline text changed from "Phase 2 in flight" to "Phase 3 complete — three-adapter matrix ... shipping, effect-aware fork UX end-to-end". "Next phases" line rewritten to point at Phase 4 candidates (multi-run compare / fork tree viz / adapter #4 / Jupyter).
  3. ZH Status section — matching rewrite in Chinese. Same three-adapter rows, same link shape.
  4. Repo layout — adapters/ comment changed from "LangGraph + Linear today" to "LangGraph + AutoGen + CrewAI + Linear"; tests/ tree gained live/ directory line and unit count changed from 380+ to 470+.
  5. Development section — uv run pytest # 380+ tests, ~92% coverage → 470+ tests, ~94% coverage.

docs.title: 2.2 Ruff RUF002 guard — × avoidance
docs.text: First draft of the EN table said "12× validated". The CONTEXT §5 invariant "Em-dash (U+2014) / U+2212 minus / × 乘号被 ruff RUF001/RUF002 禁 (仅 py 源码, md 文档 OK)" says md is technically safe — but I didn't want to relitigate it in a future round, so I preemptively rewrote to "12x validated" (ASCII x). Zero signal loss. This is the R55 meta invariant in action: the cheapest way to avoid a pitfall is to never take the bait.

docs.title: 2.3 forking-safely.md — new section §6a (EN + ZH)
docs.text:
docs/guides/forking-safely.md already had: - §6 "Per-tool effect overrides (AutoGen, v0.4.0a2+)" — AutoGen-specific

...and no CrewAI section. Inserted a matching §6a "CrewAI adapter — event-bus paradigm (v0.4.0+)" section in both EN and ZH halves, covering:

  • The three paradigms (LangGraph state-dict / AutoGen message-list / CrewAI event-bus) so the reader understands why this adapter has its own section.
  • A full recording example (Agent + Task + Crew + crewai_adapter.build_recorder(store).record(...) CM).
  • What gets recorded (event-bus subscriptions → Node with kind ∈ {llm, tool, fn, end}).
  • Five pitfalls, each empirically validated across R52-R55:
  • OneAPI LLM(provider="openai", model="GLM-5", ...) recipe — the R54 discovery.
  • CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 + OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true — the R54 / R55 env guard.
  • Optional-dep guard via importlib.util.find_spec — the R55 three-layer skipif pattern.
  • crewai_event_bus.flush(timeout=...) before store-read — the ADR-021 §D2 invariant.
  • fork() not yet supported — honest scope disclosure; deferred to Phase 4.
  • Live test reference: paths to tests/live/test_real_llm_smoke.py + tests/live/test_crewai_smoke.py + CHRONOS_LIVE=1 opt-in + ~3-4 min total wall-clock budget.

Each ZH paragraph is a faithful translation of the EN paragraph, not a machine translation but a reauthoring for ZH readers (e.g. "绕开 LiteLLM native-constants 校验" rather than a literal rendering).

docs.title: 3.2 ADR-023 skeleton — three-arcs framing
docs.text:
Wrote docs/decisions/ADR-023-phase-4-charter-skeleton.md (~150 lines). Key shape:

  • Status: Draft (not Accepted). Explicitly flagged as a framing document, not a binding decision.
  • Context: R55 closed Phase 3; Phase 4 has several non-sequential candidate themes; R56 is a polish round so it records framing, not a winner.
  • Three candidate arcs:
  • Arc A (Depth) — generalise R39-A two-run compare and R37.5 family tree into N-run / full-fork-DAG story. Five deliverables enumerated.
  • Arc B (Ecosystem) — adapter #4 + export surfaces (Parquet / Jupyter / OTel). Includes a TBD adapter-candidate table (Swarm, Assistants v2, Anthropic Agents SDK, Letta, LiveKit Agents, generic OTel receiver) with columns event-hook / license / popularity / ADR-016 mapping difficulty — all fields marked TBD pending R57+ research.
  • Arc C (Plumbing) — plugin system / Docker / LAN-sharing / demo site. Explicitly demand-driven, lowest priority.
  • Decision: Deferred to R57. R56 contribution is Phase 3 closure + roadmap skeleton + this framing ADR.
  • Why skeleton-now instead of decide-now: R56 is a post-release polish round; drift risk of a stale "Phase 4 candidates" list is real (already happened with CrewAI); better to document the framing than pre-commit.
  • Follow-ups (R57+): Arc A scoping → docs/design/n-run-compare.md; Arc B scoping → docs/research/adapter-4-survey.md; promote ADR-023 Draft → Accepted or replace with ADR-024 when R57 picks an arc.

This matches the R55 meta invariant "pre-emptive decisions are future rounds' falsification targets". ADR-023 is explicitly not a pre-emptive decision — it is a pre-emptive framing, which is much cheaper to revise.

docs.title: 7. Load-bearing findings (→ CONTEXT §5 sync)
docs.text:
• R56 R0-arc pattern — post-release polish round is canonically write-only: docs + ADR skeleton + progress. Avoid touching src/ entirely to keep the release-commit and the polish-commit narratives clean.
  • ADR filename verification pre-commit — always grep the actual ls docs/decisions/ADR-*.md output against typed filenames before committing; R56 caught one ADR-022-crewai-version-pin.md → ...-pin-bump.md typo that would have shipped otherwise.
  • Broken-link programmatic sweep is cheap (20ms Python one-shot) and should be run on any round that touches 2+ .md files with cross-references.
  • × avoidance in markdown is a cheap-to-adopt habit even though technically unblocked — keeps future ruff-discipline low-friction.
  • Phase transition rounds (like R56) are structurally different from in-phase rounds: they close the prior phase in roadmap, frame the next phase in an ADR skeleton, refresh external-facing docs. The pattern is now documented enough to be a skill candidate (see §8).

docs.title: 8. Skill candidate — chronos-post-release-polish-round
docs.text:
R56 executed a recognisable pattern that may justify a skill:

Trigger: The round immediately after a chronos-release-pattern round that cuts a non-alpha tag.

Steps: 1. Grep README.md for stale references to the previous Phase (status tables, "next phases" prose, repo-layout comments, test-count / coverage numbers). 2. Grep docs/guides/*.md for adapter-specific sections; if new adapter just shipped, add a matching guide section for it. 3. Grep docs/roadmap.md for [ ] items that actually landed, and for Phase-N candidate lists that include the just-shipped thing; reconcile. 4. If closing a Phase, write an ADR skeleton (Status: Draft) for the next Phase charter with explicit "decision deferred" framing. 5. Run broken-link sweep across all edited .md files before commit. 6. Run the full test suite even though src/ wasn't touched — catches accidental edits to .py fixtures under tests/data/*.md etc.

Defer skill authoring to R57+ (needs one more data point — R62 or whenever the next release happens — to confirm the pattern is stable).

docs.title: 9. Next round TODO — R57
docs.text: R57 is the Phase 4 kickoff round. Three options, choose one:

docs.title: Option A (highest leverage, 3-5 rounds): Arc A scoping — N-run compare design doc
docs.text:
• Write docs/design/n-run-compare.md with:
  • UX sketch: how does the user select N runs? (list multi-select, tree-lane picker, CLI chronos compare a b c?)
  • Alignment semantics: R39-A two-run alignment generalised to N. Is it O(N) or O(N²) alignment? Probably O(N) against a pivot run, with per-pair detail on click.
  • Data model: does this need new store APIs, or is the existing get_nodes_for_run sufficient?
  • API surface: GET /runs/compare?ids=a,b,c — does this return a merged tree or N parallel trees?
  • No code in R57. Design-doc only.

  • No adapter code. Research-only.

docs.text:
