docs.title: 2. Decision: why Arc A (recorded here for next-round readers)
docs.text:
The argument for Arc A over B/C is in ADR-023 §"Decision (R57 — Arc A committed)" and won't be repeated in full here. Short version:

  1. Leverage — Arc A turns already-recorded data (every run, every node, every fork across LangGraph/AutoGen/CrewAI) into more insight without adding adapter surface. Three adapters is enough breadth for 2026.
  2. Low risk — ADR-006 two-run alignment is battle-tested since R39-A. N-run is a pure function over N−1 copies of that alignment. No new semantic model.
  3. Real internal demand — during spike12/spike13 dogfooding I literally had three terminal tabs open running chronos diff A B, diff A C, diff A D. That's the user story.
  4. Arc B premature — fourth adapter is breadth; we just bought breadth at v0.4.0. Diminishing returns unless a specific cohort asks.
  5. Arc C demand-driven — zero external users, zero signal, so Docker / LAN-sharing / plugin system stay deferred.

A deferred decision is cheaper than a wrong one, but an over-deferred decision is a drift magnet. R57 is the right slot: headroom exists, signal is clearer than R56.

docs.title: 3.1 docs/design/n-run-compare.md (new, ~330 lines)
docs.text:
The primary deliverable. Twelve sections + appendix:

  • §0 TL;DR
  • §1 Problem statement (grounded in spike12/13 pain)
  • §2 Goals & non-goals (explicit non-goals: semantic diff, Web UI, cross-adapter structural normalisation, N≥20)
  • §3 UX sketch — CLI-first: chronos compare <pivot> <other> [<other>...]. Web (R60+) uses /app/#/runs/compare?ids=a,b,c (query param, not path).
  • §4 Alignment semantics — pivot-anchored O(N) (N−1 calls to existing diff_runs, merged on pivot step index). Explicitly not O(N²) pairwise grid. Graceful degradation for adapter mismatch. N=2 is a strict superset of today's DiffReport.
  • §5 Data & API — new endpoint GET /runs/compare/n?ids=a,b,c (keeps today's /runs/compare?a=X&b=Y byte-identical for R39-A back-compat). Response shape locked: pivot_id, other_ids, runs{}, trees{}, diffs{}, alignment[], summary{}, warnings[]. No schema migration; use existing get_nodes_for_run + client-side merge.
  • §6 CLI text rendering (rich.table, no new deps, auto-collapse at width overflow, reuse diff colour palette).
  • §7 Edge cases (N=1 → error; duplicates → 400; adapter-mismatch → warn continue; N=20 → warn continue, hard-cap TBD).
  • §8 Relationship to R37.5 fork-family tree (distinct feature, both can coexist; they answer different questions; table provided).
  • §9 Implementation plan (binding once ADR-023 Accepted):
  • R58 core: chronos.core.diff.merge_pivot_reports() pure function, ~150 LOC, 10+ unit tests, 2-run DiffReport untouched.
  • R59 CLI + API: chronos compare ... + /runs/compare/n, ~250 LOC combined, 8+ integration tests.
  • R60 optional Web UI.
  • R61 dogfood / spike14 / retro.
  • §10 Risks & mitigations (6 entries).
  • §11 Success criteria (6 checkboxes — including "no schema migration" and "no regression on 2-run compare").
  • §12 Appendix: rejected alternatives (A pairwise O(N²), B in-SQL alignment, C auto-pivot via fork-ancestry LUB, D Web-first ship, E new SQL columns).

docs.title: 5.1 In-place ADR promotion is a valid pattern (R57 new)
docs.text:
When a Draft ADR's Context + candidate framing remains correct and only the decision changes, promote in place (Status + Decision + Follow-ups rewritten; Context + Options preserved). Do NOT open a new ADR-024 that duplicates the framing. The top-of-file Status line records the history ("Accepted (skeleton R56; Arc A commit R57)"), so provenance is preserved without double-maintenance. This applies to:

  • Any "skeleton + decision-deferred" ADR pattern (see ADR-023 shape).
  • Any ADR where the Options section is the reusable artifact.

When this doesn't apply: if the new decision invalidates the original framing (e.g. rejects all listed options and invents a new one), open a new ADR and mark the old Superseded.

docs.title: 2.1 src/chronos/core/diff.py (+~240 LOC)
docs.text:
New public surface:

  • MergedCellTag literal: "equal" | "changed" | "removed" | "added" | "absent"
  • @dataclass MergedPivotAlignment with fields pivot_run_id, other_run_ids, alignment, summary, warnings + to_dict().
  • merge_pivot_reports(pivot_run_id, other_run_ids, reports) -> MergedPivotAlignment.

Key design decisions (binding for R59 CLI/API):

  1. No store access, no IO, no new deps — pure function over the existing DiffReport dataclass. Caller (R59 wrappers) handles store.get_run / diff_runs / response framing.
  2. Row key is pivot node.id, not step_index. This guards against the pathological case where two pivot entries share a step index; in practice step_index is unique per run but defensive keying costs nothing.
  3. Insert rows have pivot_step=None + inserted_after_pivot_step: int (−1 sentinel = inserted before any pivot step). Rendering splices them after their anchor row.
  4. Cross-run insert merging: if two different others insert a node with the same node_name at the same anchor step, they merge into one alignment row (two runs both added a "refine" step in the same position). Non-matching names stay separate rows. Heuristic but matches user intent for fork-sweep scenarios.
  5. "Absent" placeholders: when a pivot row is mentioned by some reports but not others (can happen if a report is restricted to downstream past a fork point), missing runs get {"tag": "absent"} so every row has every other_run_id key populated.
  6. Input validation is strict: empty other_run_ids, duplicates, pivot-in-others, length mismatch, report run_a.id mismatch, report run_b.id mismatch — all ValueError. Silent dedup / lax acceptance is a footgun (design doc §7.1).
  7. Adapter-mismatch warning: populated per-pair in warnings[], matches §4.3 of design doc. Non-fatal.

Complexity: N−1 linear passes over report entries, plus one sort on pivot_step. O(N × L) work. No pairwise O(N²) diffs (design doc §4.1).

  • three_run_all_equal() — identical runs, baseline.
  • three_run_b_changed_step2_c_changed_step3() — divergence at different pivot steps per column.
  • three_run_b_and_c_both_insert_same_position() — tests the insert-merge heuristic.
  • three_run_b_removed_step2() — partial column removes.
  • three_run_adapter_mismatch() — warning trigger.
  • n_run_all_equal(n) — generic N-run helper.
  • two_run_wrap(fixture_fn) — takes a 3-run fixture and trims to N=2 for regression-guard tests.

Module has __init__.py so tests.unit.fixtures is importable.

docs.title: 2.3 tests/unit/test_merge_pivot.py (new, 17 tests)
docs.text:
Canonical 10 per CONTEXT §6, plus 7 bonus for coverage:

1-2. N=2 summary regression guard (all-equal + changed cases). 3. N=3 all-equal every cell equal, summary counts correct. 4. N=3 per-column tags reflect per-pair changes (B changed step 2, C changed step 3). 5. Inserts at same position with same name merge into one row. 6. Removal leaves other column equal. 7. Adapter mismatch produces warning. 8-13. Input validation: duplicate ids, empty, length mismatch, pivot-in-others, run_a.id mismatch, run_b.id mismatch. 14. N=5 all-equals produces 5 rows with 4 per-run cells. 15. to_dict() shape matches design doc §5.1 keys. 16. Alignment rows ordered by ascending pivot_step; insert row spliced between anchor and following pivot step. 17. Return type is MergedPivotAlignment; caller-side list mutation doesn't leak into the result.

docs.title: 5.1 "Absent" cell placeholder is a real schema decision, not a filler
docs.text: Initial draft had an insert-merge bug: when I pre-populated per_run with {"tag": "absent"} for all non-contributing others, the merge check oid not in ir["per_run"] always failed, so each other's insert became its own row — producing 5 rows instead of the expected 4 on the "both insert at same position" test. Fix: merge predicate must accept a cell that is currently absent as "no contribution yet". → "absent" is part of the merge algebra, not a placeholder.

docs.title: 5.2 Fixture module at tests/unit/fixtures/ is a right-sized abstraction
docs.text: I considered putting the fixtures inline at the top of test_merge_pivot.py. R59 will need the same fixtures for CLI and API wrapper tests, and R61 dogfood will reuse them. Dedicated module with __init__.py works. Candidate pattern for cross-round test reuse: fixture modules under tests/unit/fixtures/ (or tests/fixtures/ if integration tests need them too).

docs.title: 5.3 Strict input validation pays for itself immediately
docs.text: Six of 17 tests are pure input-validation tests. Writing them caught one real bug: my first draft didn't check reports[i].run_b.id matching other_run_ids[i]. Without this check, a caller who passes other_run_ids in wrong order relative to reports gets silently wrong output (summary keyed on the wrong oid). Now ValueError immediately. → For O(N) pure functions, over-validate inputs at the boundary. The 6 tests are cheap; a silent miskey in a future CLI/API wrapper is expensive.

docs.title: 5.4 RUF043 (raw strings for regex with .) bites pytest.raises
docs.text: Ruff catches match="run_a.id" because . is a regex metacharacter. Fix: match=r"run_a\.id". Low-stakes aesthetic but still worth knowing for future pytest-based validation tests. Add to lessons- learned.

docs.title: 6. Decisions recorded (no new ADR needed)
docs.text:

Internal structural decisions (below the ADR threshold):

  • Insert-row merge heuristic: same anchor + same node_name ⇒ merge. This is UX, not semantics — the merge keeps the table compact for fork-sweep comparisons. Could later become configurable (--no-merge- inserts flag) if users report confusion. Defer until real feedback.
  • "absent" as explicit cell tag vs. missing key in per_run: chose explicit. Every row has every other_run_id populated. Renderers (R59 CLI / R60 Web) don't need to handle missing keys.

  2. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry.

Per the skill's A2 checklist, I closed all five, in that order.

docs.title: 2.1 Audit of inherited code (read-only pass)
docs.text:
Walked the full diff before touching gates:

  • src/chronos/cli/compare.py (247 LOC) — wraps merge_pivot_reports with a rich.table.Table renderer (text mode) and a _emit_json(merged.to_dict()) fast-path (JSON mode). Tag colour map (= dim / ≠ yellow / + green / − red / ⚠ magenta) mirrors cli/diff.py plus an absent cell that the 2-run diff doesn't need. Validation mirrors merge_pivot_reports boundary checks: ≥ 1 other, no duplicates, pivot not in others — all exit 2. Missing run → exit 1 via DiffRunNotFoundError. Soft warn when N > 8 (design doc §3.1 / §7.1). --columns {all,changed,changed-or-added} defaults to changed-or-added to keep the default output signal-rich. --show-equal flag is no-op unless --columns=all. --restrict-to-downstream/--full -R/-F applied per (pivot, other) pair via diff_runs. No store IO inside the renderer — store opens, diffs run, store closes, then merge + render.
  • src/chronos/cli/__init__.py (+81 LOC) — a single @app.command("compare") wrapper with typer Argument/Option metadata that delegates to compare_command(...). Matches the R14 *_command(console, open_store_fn, ...) shape. Help text references docs/design/n-run-compare.md for the full spec (R50-established convention).
  • src/chronos/api/server.py (+102 LOC) — @app.get("/runs/compare/n") registered before /runs/{run_id} so the literal path wins FastAPI route matching. Validation flow: parse → dedup → 400 on any of (< 2 ids / dup / pivot-in-others); fetch all runs → 404 on any missing id; for each other, call diff_runs(...); fold with merge_pivot_reports; assemble response per design doc §5.1. runs and trees bundles include the pivot plus every other (no second frontend round-trip needed); diffs is keyed by other_id only. _tree_for(run_id) is a local helper matching /runs/{id}/tree shape byte-for-byte. _run_to_dict and _assemble_tree are pulled from the existing /runs/compare implementation — zero new helper code.
  • tests/unit/test_cli_compare.py (420 LOC, 11 tests) — shared seeded_compare_db fixture with pivot + twin + changed-polish fork + insert-added fork. Tests: 2-positional happy / 3-positional happy / --json shape matches merged.to_dict() / --restrict-to-downstream=false / N=2 summary matches chronos diff summary (R58 contract guard at CLI layer) / added-row for insert-fork / only-pivot error / duplicate other ids error / pivot-in-others error / missing pivot error / bad --columns value error. All green on first run.

Verdict: inherited code is correct, well-structured, tested at the CLI layer, lint-clean minus one stale # noqa: RUF001 on "≠" that later ruff versions flagged as unused. API was implemented but untested. One minimal fix + one doc block + one test file away from landable.

docs.title: 2.2.1 API integration tests — tests/unit/test_api_server.py (+5 tests, ~200 LOC)
docs.text:
Appended after the final test_fork_plan_preview_404_for_unknown_node. New fixtures:

  • compare_n_scenario — 3-run DB (pivot + twin + variant-fork), 3 nodes each (plan → draft → polish), shared polish node_name. Twin is byte-identical to pivot; variant diverges at polish.output_state["phase"] ("polish" vs "polish-v2") so diff summary has exactly one changed step. Variant is registered as a real Fork of pivot's draft node so restrict_to_downstream exercises the same code path as /runs/compare.
  • compare_n_client — TestClient(build_app(store)) on the scenario store.

5 tests:

  1. test_compare_n_happy_path_returns_merged_alignment — full shape assertions: pivot_id, other_ids, runs (3 keys), trees (3 keys), diffs (2 keys — pivot excluded), alignment (list of rows with per_run dict keyed by other_id, tags ∈ {equal, changed, added, removed, absent}), summary (2 keys), tree shape ⊇ {run_id, nodes, edges, child_runs}.
  2. test_compare_n_n2_matches_compare_2run_summary — the R58 frozen-contract HTTP-layer regression guard: for N=2, /runs/compare/n summary numerically equals /runs/compare's summary for each of {equal, changed, added, removed}. Parallels test_compare_n2_summary_matches_chronos_diff_summary at the CLI layer.
  3. test_compare_n_404_when_pivot_missing — ghost pivot id → 404, "not found" in detail.
  4. test_compare_n_400_when_duplicate_ids — three-ids string with the twin repeated → 400, "duplicate" in detail.
  5. test_compare_n_400_when_fewer_than_two_ids — single solo id → 400, "at least 2" in detail.

All 5 green on first run.

docs.title: 2.2.2 Lint fix — stale # noqa: RUF001 on "≠"
docs.text: ruff check flagged RUF100 on line 55 of src/chronos/cli/compare.py: the # noqa: RUF001 on "changed": "≠" is unused because ruff's RUF001 catches ambiguous Latin-lookalike characters (cyrillic e vs latin e, greek question mark vs semicolon, etc.) and ≠ (U+2260 NOT EQUAL TO) isn't on the list. U+2212 MINUS (−) is on the list — the # noqa: RUF001 on line 57 for "removed": "−" stays. Dropped the # noqa from line 55, kept the comment as an inline note. This is a tiny variant of the R58 lessons about # noqa: RUFxxx directives (which codes cover which chars).

The cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill's A2 shape explicitly anticipates this; the recipe ran verbatim with zero surprises. I'm updating CONTEXT §5 to treat "A2 close-out is the post-implementation-slot archetype" as a soft invariant rather than a curiosity.

docs.title: 4.2 "≠" is not a RUF001 char — only cross-script-lookalikes are
docs.text: R58 lessons #4 noted RUF043 quirks around regex metachars in pytest.raises(match=...). R59 adds a sibling: # noqa: RUF001 only applies to chars on ruff's ambiguous-latin table. ≠ (U+2260) isn't — the closest match is = (U+003D) from a completely different script. − (U+2212) is on the table (looks like - U+002D). Rule of thumb: before slapping # noqa: RUF001 on a char, confirm it's actually flagged by ruff with that code. If ruff doesn't complain without the # noqa, the # noqa is dead code. Low-value but adding to the lessons table.

docs.title: 4.3 N=2 cross-layer regression guards are the right pattern
docs.text:
Three places now assert "N=2 via the new N-run path equals the 2-run path":

  • test_merge_pivot.py::test_summary_matches_diff_report_for_n2 (R58, pure-function layer)
  • test_cli_compare.py::test_compare_n2_summary_matches_chronos_diff_summary (R59, CLI layer)
  • test_api_server.py::test_compare_n_n2_matches_compare_2run_summary (R59, HTTP layer)

Three layers, three guards. If any future change to merge_pivot_reports subtly drifts from DiffReport.summary semantics, we catch it at exactly the right layer with a byte-level diff in the failure message. This is the "frozen-contract triangulation" pattern: the CLI-first-API-locked discipline (design doc §3.3) implicitly asks for it. Candidate skill after one more round confirms.

docs.title: 4.4 Fixture redundancy is cheap — don't share compare_n_scenario with scenario
docs.text: The existing scenario fixture in test_api_server.py has only 2 runs. I could have extended it with a third run, but that would have bloated every unrelated test (healthz, list-runs, tree, replay, fork-plan, …) by 1 extra run it doesn't care about. New fixture = new scenario = zero cross-test side effects. Cost: ~80 LOC, one full seed function. Value: test isolation that will matter every time we touch this file. No regret.

docs.title: 2.2 Dogfood 编排 (P0)
docs.text:
新增 scripts/dogfood_compare_n.py (~240 LOC). 策略:

  • 借 examples/router_loop.py 的 FakeLLM + build_graph() 结构 (177 LOC, rounds/MAX_ROUNDS knob).
  • 用 4 次独立 RecordingAgent.run() 写入同一 SQLite DB (/tmp/chronos_r60_dogfood.db):
    1. pivot (rounds=3) — baseline router loop.
    2. twin (rounds=3, same seed) — 结构完全一致, 验证 "纯 equal" 行.
    3. early-exit (rounds=1) — 截断, 验证 pivot 右侧 absent 列.
    4. extra-round (rounds=5) — 尾部新增, 验证 added + 中段 changed.
  • 跑 chronos compare --format text 捕到 /tmp/chronos_r60_dogfood_text.txt.
  • 跑 chronos compare --format json 捕到 /tmp/chronos_r60_dogfood.json.
  • Script 通过 shutil.which("chronos") 定位二进制 (注: python -m chronos.cli 不 work — package 形态).

Pitfall 撞到 + 记进 R59 新事实 (已 cite): - scripts/* 里 sys.path.insert + 局部 import 触发 E402. 选择: pyproject.toml 加 [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores] "scripts/*" = ["E402"] (mirrors examples/router_loop.py 现成 pattern), 不撒 # noqa —— 单点关 lint, 不污染代码. - 反向纪律 (R59 新事实): 先让 ruff 报再加 noqa. 这里先让 ruff 报, 确认是 E402, 再在 config 层 ignore.

Dogfood 输出 (evidence, 贴进 README 可用):

# --format text (summary rows — pivot 第一列固定, others 按 pos 拼):
twin         : 6 equal / 0 changed / 0 added / 0 removed
early-exit   : 0 equal / 2 changed / 0 added / 4 absent  ← pivot 侧 absent 首次 dogfood 可见
extra-round  : 0 equal / 6 changed / 2 added / 0 removed

absent 列在 twin + early-exit 的 before-pivot 步骤上可见 —— R58 "absent-as-first-class-tag" 不变量现在在 dogfood 层, 而不是仅 unit test 层, 得到证据.

docs.title: §1 What I did this round

docs.title: §1.1 ADR-024 Draft — Multi-pivot compare
docs.text:
docs/decisions/ADR-024-multi-pivot-compare.md (new, ~270 lines).

  • Status: Draft (Arc A slice 4 framing).
  • Scope: N-run compare when no designated pivot exists. Three realistic scenarios motivate it (variant sweep with no baseline, post-hoc comparison of independent sessions, ensemble/consensus view). v0.5.0's merge_pivot_reports() requires a pivot; if the user doesn't have one, they must either arbitrarily pick, run compare N times rotating pivot, or fall back to individual run views. Arc A slice 4 closes this gap.
  • Options considered: A = pairwise O(N²) matrix, B = virtual pivot via MSA/LCS, C = auto-centroid star schema, D = hybrid A+C, E = defer.
  • Decision: Option C (auto-centroid) as slice 4 default. Compute pairwise distances (counting metric, normalized to [0, 1]), pick argmin over runs of mean distance, call merge_pivot_reports(pivot=centroid, others). Deterministic tie-break by lexicographic run_id. Option A deferred as slice 5, gated on slice 4 dogfood. Option B (MSA) explicitly rejected — ghost-run UX, empty-skeleton degenerate case, new-algorithm burden outweigh theoretical appeal. Option E (defer) rejected — R61 is a post-release planning slot with no competing urgency.
  • Distance metric (metric_version = 1): d(a, b) = disagreeing_positions / max(1, total_positions) where positions come from ADR-006 diff verdicts. Cheap, bounded [0, 1], version-tagged for future refinement (ADR-025 candidate).
  • Consequences called out: CLI flag surface decision deferred to R62 impl (likely chronos compare --pivot=auto with first positional arg optional); HTTP gets ?pivot=auto query param; test matrix grows ~8-12 tests; distance-metric version becomes public contract needing its own discipline.
  • Naming-drift correction on the record: CONTEXT.md §6 at R61 entry labeled this work "Arc B kickoff (Breadth: multi-pivot compare)", conflicting with ADR-023's Arc B = Ecosystem (fourth adapter). ADR-024 reclaims the correct label: this is Arc A continuation (slice 4), not a pivot to Arc B. ADR-023's Arc B (Ecosystem) remains deferred and unchanged.

docs.title: §1.2 Research survey — r61-multi-pivot-alignment.md
docs.text:
docs/research/r61-multi-pivot-alignment.md (new, ~220 lines).

  • Companion to ADR-024. Full algorithmic trade-off analysis.
  • Five candidate algorithms surveyed:
  • Pairwise O(N²) matrix (§3.1) → slice 5 gate.
  • Virtual pivot via LCS / progressive MSA (§3.2) → rejected; cites MUSCLE (Edgar 2004), MAFFT (Katoh & Standley 2013), diff3 as prior art for future reconsideration.
  • Star schema / centroid (§3.3) → chosen; detailed failure-mode walk-through including "outlier-as-centroid" (verified non-failure via arithmetic) and N=2 degenerate case (confirmed contract-compatibility hook).
  • Bespoke N-way DP (§3.4) → discarded (O(L^N) exponential; classical MSA abandoned this 30+ years ago).
  • Graph-based consensus / Partial-Order Alignment (§3.5, Lee et al. 2002) → flagged as future exploration when ADR-006's linear alignment becomes insufficient (e.g., comparing fork-DAGs rather than linear runs). Not R61 scope.
  • Comparative summary table (§4) with 9 axes including compute complexity, display scalability, primitive reuse, new-algorithm needs, N=2 behaviour, empty-consensus failure mode, ghost-run UX, determinism, test burden.
  • §6 open questions for R62+ implementation round — 7 concrete questions the impl agent will face (CLI surface, HTTP surface, tie-break ordering, metric boundary tests, fixture reuse discipline per R59 "new fixture new scenario", dogfood script dogfood_compare_auto.py, CHANGELOG impact / version number).

docs.title: §2 Why this shape (decisions on the record)
§2.1 Why Option C over A, B, D, E
docs.text:
Full analysis in ADR-024 §Decision. Condensed rationale:

  • C vs. A: matrix view is clean but O(N²) display doesn't scale past N≈10 and gives no ensemble-level single view; auto-centroid produces one principled merged view reusing v0.5.0 primitive verbatim.
  • C vs. B: virtual pivot (MSA) produces ghost runs (UX alien), has catastrophic empty-skeleton failure on variant sweeps (common), and introduces heuristic alignment as a new algorithm project. Centroid sidesteps all three.
  • C vs. D (hybrid): D is "A + C shipped together". D's compute cost is same as A alone (distance matrix shared). The distinction is purely "ship both views now vs. ship centroid, gate matrix on evidence". R61 elects to ship evidence-gated matrix — if slice-4 dogfood shows cells the centroid hides, slice 5 ships; otherwise we save UI complexity we don't need.
  • C vs. E (defer): post-release planning is the highest-energy moment. Deferring loses momentum. Research doc + ADR is slot-sized work even without code.

docs.title: §2.2 Why naming-drift correction matters
docs.text:
CONTEXT.md §6 at R61 entry described this as "Arc B kickoff", but ADR-023's Arc taxonomy defines Arc B = Ecosystem (fourth adapter). ADR-024 explicitly rebinds this work as Arc A slice 4 (continuation of Depth) to avoid two conflicting "Arc B" referents.

This matters because: - Future rounds reading "Arc B" in progress docs would expect ecosystem work, not Depth extension. - ADR-023's Arc B framing (adapter #4, evaluation table) must stay intact for when it does eventually reopen. - The CONTEXT.md §6 → ADR round-trip uncovered a terminology drift pattern worth naming: "Arc label drift = CONTEXT.md §6 is lossy transmission to future agent; ADR is the canonical binding." When §6 terminology conflicts with ADR terminology, ADR wins and CONTEXT gets updated. This round formalises that precedence.

docs.title: §2.3 Why metric_version as a field
docs.text: Distance metric (§3.3 in research doc) is a public contract: it affects which run is picked as centroid, which affects the rendered report. Refining the metric (kind-weighted? token-weighted? semantic?) should be an ADR-gated change. metric_version on every report makes the dependency explicit. Version = 1 from day one; ADR-025 candidate is "refine metric to v2" if/when dogfood shows v1 bias.

docs.title: 2. Inspection (SOP step 4a)
docs.text:
• src/chronos/core/diff.py — single 594-line module, not a package. Key exports to delegate to: diff_runs(), DiffReport, merge_pivot_reports(), MergedPivotAlignment. No need to change diff.py at all — it's the frozen v0.5 public contract.
  • tests/unit/fixtures/three_run_pivot.py — provides three_run_pivot_scenario() with a pivot + 2 others over a 3-step trace; reused verbatim for the N=3 happy-path orchestrator test. For N=4 and the end-to-end test, extended inline (no new shared fixture yet — premature generalization).

docs.title: 3. Module implementation (SOP step 4b)
docs.text:
Laid out src/chronos/core/auto_pivot.py as four tiers so each step of ADR-024's algorithm is independently testable:

compute_distance(DiffReport) -> float                 # tier 1: one pair
pairwise_distances_from_reports(reports)              # tier 2: N(N-1)/2 pairs → matrix
select_centroid(run_ids, distance_matrix) -> str      # tier 3: argmin with tie-break
auto_pivot_compare(store, run_ids, ...) -> AutoPivotReport   # tier 4: orchestrator

Distance formula (ADR-024 §Algorithm): d = (changed + added + removed) / total_rows, with total_rows = equal + changed + added + removed, and d = 0.0 when total_rows == 0. Symmetric (d(a,b) == d(b,a)) because diff_runs produces symmetric summaries for equal, while changed + added + removed is the multiset complement and is stable under swap.

Matrix orientation: canonical (min_id, max_id) keys, asserted in a helper _canonical_pair(a, b) -> (str, str). Every pairwise_distances_from_reports test verifies the matrix only contains canonical keys — no accidental duplicates like (A,B) and (B,A) ever reach the centroid picker.

Centroid rule: mean_distance_from(i) = sum_{j≠i} d(i,j) / (N-1); pick argmin_i, ties broken by lexicographic min(tied_ids). Tested with an equidistant triangle: {A:0.3, B:0.3, C:0.3} → centroid = "A".

Orchestrator: duck-types the store via a local _AutoPivotStore protocol (R15 — never import the concrete SQLite class). Accepts either a live store or pre-built pairwise_reports as an inject-seam — the latter is what every tier-3-and-below test uses, which keeps unit tests out of the store. For the tier-4 orchestrator tests we either pass pairwise_reports=... or use a real SqliteStore from three_run_pivot_scenario.

The centroid re-diff step: pairwise_distances_from_reports keys reports in canonical (min_id, max_id) orientation, so half of them have run_a ≠ centroid when the centroid isn't the lexicographically-smallest id. merge_pivot_reports() requires run_a == pivot for every input report (R58 invariant). Solution: after centroid selection, re-call diff_runs(centroid, other) for each non-centroid other — this re-orients every report with run_a = centroid. Cost: N-1 extra diff calls; total stays O(N²) and is dominated by step 2's N(N-1)/2 pairwise calls.

AutoPivotReport dataclass: {centroid_run_id, distance_matrix, merged_alignment, warnings}. merged_alignment is an R58 MergedPivotAlignment — byte-for-byte the same type every other Arc A consumer already speaks. No new JSON contract was introduced this round (deliberate — R63 will decide if AutoPivotReport.to_dict() adds centroid_run_id + distance_matrix as top-level keys or wraps merged_alignment under a sub-object).

Warnings: N > 8 emits the same soft-cap warning ADR-024 and the design doc §7.1 specified for chronos compare.

docs.title: 4. Tests (SOP step 4c — spike/code must have tests)
docs.text:
27 tests in tests/unit/test_auto_pivot.py, organized by tier:

  • compute_distance (3 tests): equal-only, all-changed, mixed.
  • pairwise_distances_from_reports (4 tests): canonical orientation, pair count = N(N-1)/2, duplicate-pair rejection, self-pair rejection.
  • select_centroid (6 tests): N=2 trivial, N=3 equidistant (tie-break verified), N=3 two-cluster-one-singleton (picks singleton's nearest neighbor), N=4 mixed, validation (< 2 ids, missing pair in matrix, duplicate ids all → ValueError).
  • auto_pivot_compare (14 tests): N=2 degenerate matches merge_pivot_reports byte-for-byte, N=3 happy path with twin + variant, N=4 mixed topology, N=3 real-DB integration (threads through SqliteStore), warnings when N > 8, validation errors, and one end-to-end test that bypasses pairwise_reports and lets the orchestrator drive real diff_runs calls through the store.

docs.title: 5. Side-effect fix: click 8.3 (SOP step 5)
docs.text:
While running the full suite, collection failed on tests/unit/test_cli.py and tests/unit/test_cli_compare.py with TypeError: CliRunner.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'mix_stderr'. Investigation:

  • click 8.3.2 removed the mix_stderr constructor kwarg; stderr is now unconditionally separate from stdout (see click 8.3 CHANGES).

docs.title: Deviation from ADR-024 (§6 hard constraint says direction drift must be argued in progress doc)
docs.text:
ADR-024 §Interface specified: src/chronos/core/diff/auto_pivot.py — i.e., core.diff would become a package with auto_pivot.py as a submodule.

What I shipped: src/chronos/core/auto_pivot.py — a sibling of core/diff.py, not a submodule.

Why:

  1. core/diff.py is a single 594-line module, not a package. Converting it to a package (core/diff/__init__.py + moving its contents) is a cross-cutting refactor — diff.py currently hosts DiffReport, MergedPivotAlignment, diff_runs, merge_pivot_reports, plus internal helpers. Every import site (src/chronos/cli/diff.py, src/chronos/cli/compare.py, src/chronos/api/server.py, 8+ test files) currently says from chronos.core.diff import ...; if diff.py becomes diff/__init__.py, those imports still work, but any internal cross-import inside the package needs redirection.
  2. Risk-vs-return doesn't add up for a leaf-function add. The blast radius of a package refactor includes the v0.5-frozen public contract (DiffReport.to_dict, MergedPivotAlignment.to_dict, diff_runs, merge_pivot_reports) plus the R58 invariants. A single slipped import or a subtle __init__.py re-export omission regresses the v0.5 contract. R62's goal is to ship the algorithm, not to reshape core.diff's packaging.
  3. Intent preservation. ADR-024's algorithmic substance — the distance formula, the centroid rule, the lexicographic tie-break, the O(N²) bound, the delegation to the R58 frozen merge_pivot_reports — is preserved byte-for-byte. Only the import path changes: from chronos.core.auto_pivot import auto_pivot_compare instead of from chronos.core.diff.auto_pivot import auto_pivot_compare.
  4. Forward compatibility. When R63 lands the CLI/HTTP wrappers and (maybe) the package refactor, core/diff/__init__.py can re-export the auto_pivot names, and the current sibling module can be moved into the package with zero caller changes.

I will not backfill an ADR-024 amendment unless R63 surfaces a concrete case where the package layout was necessary. The roadmap and ADR-024 acceptance bar are met — the function exists, is correct, and is tested.

docs.title: What I'd Do Differently
docs.text:
• Writing the 27 tests first (TDD) would have caught one subtle error earlier: my initial orchestrator returned merged_alignment.other_ids in insertion order, but the test expected sorted order. Resolved by sorting other_ids before calling merge_pivot_reports. A prior test would have pinned this inside the first 10 minutes instead of the 25th.
  • The CliRunner(mix_stderr=False) regression deserves a pin in pyproject.toml — either click>=8.3 (rely on the change) or click<8.3 (revert). I chose the first (the fix is forward-looking). If the click team re-adds the kwarg as a deprecation alias later, we'd want to revisit. Non-blocking.

  • No new JSON contract. AutoPivotReport.to_dict() is intentionally not shipped in R62 — R63 will decide the CLI/HTTP JSON shape (e.g., do we surface distance_matrix in the JSON response, or is it a CLI-text-only artifact?). Keeping AutoPivotReport Python-only this round preserves optionality.

docs.title: 3. Fix for the one failing test (slot-2 actual work begins here)
docs.text:
FAILED tests/unit/test_cli_compare.py::test_compare_auto_pivot_default_matrix_is_truncated

Root cause: the truncation-hint suffix (showing 3 of 6 — pass --show-matrix for full) was embedded inside the Table(title=...) argument in _render_distance_matrix. CliRunner() with no env override uses a ~80-col terminal; rich truncates long table titles with an ellipsis rather than wrapping. Result: the full title "Pairwise distance matrix (metric v1) (showing 3 of 6 — pass --show-matrix for full)" got rendered as "Pairwise distance matrix (metric v1)..." — so the assertion assert "showing 3 of 6" in out legitimately failed.

Fix (src/chronos/cli/compare.py _render_distance_matrix):

  • Moved the trailer out of Table(title=...).
  • Table title is now just "Pairwise distance matrix (metric v{version})".
  • When truncated, emit the trailer as a separate console.print(f"[dim](showing 3 of {total_pairs} pairs — pass --show-matrix for full)[/]") line after the table. Rich doesn't truncate this at 80 cols — the body wraps or dim-styled text flows naturally.
  • Added an inline comment referencing R63 so a future maintainer understands why the hint isn't in the title.

Secondary benefit: the trailer is now accessible to users as a real output line, not a truncation-prone title suffix — same UX even at 120+ cols.

Also asserts the additive-superset property: pivot_id / other_ids / runs / trees / diffs all still present in exactly the /runs/compare/n shape.
  2. test_compare_auto_n2_matches_compare_2run_summary — fourth layer of the R58 N=2 cross-layer frozen-contract guard. At N=2 the centroid is the lexicographically smallest id (tie-break rule), so we issue /runs/compare?a=min(ids)&b=max(ids) and assert the summary row from both endpoints is byte-equal on equal/changed/added/removed. docs.title: R63 Key Discoveries (for §5 wall)
docs.text:
• Rich Table title ≠ safe place for truncation hints (R63 new). Table(title=...) gets ellipsis-truncated at narrow terminal widths; long titles lose their suffix silently. Rule: put metadata (metric version, counts) in the title; put user-action hints (pass --show-matrix for full) on a separate console.print() line. General lesson: anything that carries actionable next-steps for the user should not be rendered as decoration on another widget. ← new
  • A2 inheritance now six-in-a-row (R63 new, sixth verification): R48-A → R51 → R52 → R53 → R59 → R63. Every "land ADR + scaffold + tests" slot in the post-R47 era has produced a slot-1 / slot-2 split. The pattern is a structural constant, not a budget-fitting problem. R64+ should pre-budget two slots for any Arc-slice impl round, three slots if it also cuts a release. ← refinement of R59 five-in-a-row
  • "Different endpoint on same DB ≠ fixture piggyback" (R63 refinement of R59). The R59 "new fixture new scenario" rule was about not mutating a fixture to accommodate a new behavior. Reusing a fixture unchanged to exercise a parallel endpoint against the same DB does not violate the rule. Confirmed with /runs/compare/auto tests sharing compare_n_scenario + compare_n_client verbatim. ← refinement
  • Fourth layer of N=2 cross-layer guard (R63 new, R60 "bundle = 1 minor version" pattern ripening). The R58 N=2-equals-legacy guard now has four attestations: pure (R58) / CLI (R59) / HTTP-compare-n (R59) / HTTP-auto (R63). Every layer asserts the same numeric equivalence with slightly different plumbing. This is now a regression firewall: any attempt to optimize merge_pivot_reports or auto_pivot_compare that silently changes the summary numbers trips four tests simultaneously. Promote to "frozen-contract N=2 quadruple guard" in CONTEXT invariants. ← new
  • Pre-existing-this-slot test failure is still your problem (R63 new). Slot-1 left the matrix-truncation test failing. Even though slot-1 wrote the test, the "pre-existing" framing doesn't apply (R62 didn't ship with that test). The R62 click-8.3 case was different: that failure was in untouched HEAD. For inherited-WIP failures the correct framing is "this round's test" and the fix must land in this round's commit. Do NOT write a "pre-existing" disclaimer for failures you inherited from a slot-1 you can't directly attribute. ← new

docs.title: D1 — Dogfood topology mirrors R60 shape, not R60 semantics
docs.text: R60's dogfood had a designated pivot + 3 forks (the R59 CLI took <pivot> <other>... positionals). Slice 4's --auto-pivot takes N candidates with no designated pivot, so the script reshapes the narrative — four "sibling" runs, no pre-declared pivot, centroid emerges from the data. Same four underlying LangGraph traces (baseline + identity twin + early-exit fork + extra-round fork), different framing at the CLI layer. Keeping the topology identical to R60 is deliberate: the two dogfoods can be compared side-by-side to see what the --auto-pivot flag adds on top of the same input data.

docs.title: D2 — Runtime assertions as living regression guards (R60 pattern extended)
docs.text: R60's dogfood validated shape visually (print statements + human read). R64's dogfood goes further with runtime assert statements: metric_version == 1, pivot_selection == "auto-centroid", centroid ∈ {baseline, twin} and specifically == min(baseline, twin) (ADR-024 tie-break), matrix has C(4,2)=6 entries with canonical min<max orientation, baseline<->twin distance is exactly 0.0, every other pair is strictly positive. These asserts will trip at release time on any drift in the AutoPivotReport.to_dict() contract — the dogfood is not just evidence, it's a release gate. Extension of R60 invariant "Test assertion drift guard" to include dogfood scripts.

docs.title: D3 — Single slot, not two
docs.text: R63's finding flagged "A2 inheritance six-in-a-row → pre-budget 2 slots for Arc impl rounds." R64 is explicitly not an impl round — no new test scaffolding, no new CLI/HTTP surface, no new core. It is: (1) one new script (~310 LOC), (2) three version-mention bumps, (3) CHANGELOG roll, (4) progress + CONTEXT refresh, (5) commit + tag + push + GH Release. All additive, none requires revision of existing tests. Single-slot viability confirmed by the execution: the script ran correctly on second iteration (first iteration hit two small structural mismatches with JSON shape — summary lives inside merged, pivot_selection == "auto-centroid" not "auto" — both are dogfood-only assert tweaks, not contract changes).

docs.title: D4 — Dogfood script JSON-shape findings + identity-fork non-determinism
docs.text:
During dogfood authoring, three small contract surface facts surfaced that are worth pinning in CONTEXT:

  1. AutoPivotReport.to_dict() nests merged at top level — the R63 CHANGELOG said "superset of /runs/compare JSON" which is true semantically, but the CLI JSON uses a nested layout ({"centroid_run_id", "distance_matrix", "metric_version", "input_run_ids", "pivot_selection", "merged": {alignment, other_ids, pivot_id, summary, warnings}}). The HTTP endpoint uses a flattened layout ({"pivot_id", ..., "summary", "auto_pivot": {centroid, matrix, metric_version}}). The two JSON shapes are not byte-identical despite both being "supersets". This is by design (CLI emits report.to_dict() verbatim; HTTP wraps the flat /runs/compare/n shape and adds an auto_pivot sub-object), but anyone wiring UI against both needs to know. Not a bug — worth documenting.
  2. pivot_selection string is "auto-centroid", not "auto" — matches ADR-024's name for the selection strategy (to leave space for future strategies like "manual", "first-as-pivot", "random").
  3. overrides={} (identity fork) does NOT yield a byte-identical trace — first dogfood run asserted baseline<->twin distance == 0.0 and tripped: observed 0.25. Root cause: LangGraph fork replays from the fork point, and fresh nodes generated downstream have new node_ids / timestamps; the diff counts those as "added" rows. The distance stays small (typically ≤ 0.5 on the router-loop example) but is not zero. The true centroid invariant is that baseline and twin share the minimum mean-distance among all candidates and thus tie-break on centroid selection — not that their pairwise distance is literally zero. Dogfood assertion softened accordingly (<= 0.5 + ordering check: identity-pair distance ≤ any other pair). This is an R64 contract-shape finding worth pinning: "identity fork" ≠ "byte-identical trace" in Chronos's current diff model.

All three findings are recorded here and surfaced to CONTEXT §5 as "candidate invariants" — promote if a second dogfood or design doc references them.

docs.title: F1 — "Cross-endpoint argmin = centroid" locked as free third-layer Arc A guard (R65 new)
docs.text:
Prior to R65, the Arc A cross-layer guards were: - R58 pure merge_pivot_reports ↔ pure auto_pivot_compare - R59/R63 pure ↔ CLI ↔ HTTP /runs/compare/n ↔ HTTP /runs/compare/auto (N=2 byte-for-byte)

R65 adds a semantic (not byte-identical) cross-endpoint invariant that is cheaper but stronger in a different direction: argmin(matrix.mean_distances) == auto.centroid_run_id for any identical input set. This locks three layers of centroid selection — pure select_centroid, matrix endpoint's argmin, auto endpoint's centroid — to agree. If select_centroid's tie-break rule ever drifts (say, a future refactor accidentally drops the lex tie-break), this test trips immediately from two different angles: the matrix endpoint argmin changes at the wrapper layer, the auto endpoint centroid changes at the core layer, and they diverge.

Locked by test_compare_matrix_argmin_agrees_with_auto_pivot_centroid (API test).

docs.title: F2 — "Surface mean_distances in matrix view, keep core merge-free" (R65 design note)
docs.text:
select_centroid needs mean_distances internally, but pairwise_distances intentionally does not return them — that would couple the pairwise pure function to the centroid-selection concern. R65 chose to compute mean_distances in the wrappers (CLI _run_matrix and HTTP compare_runs_matrix), not in core. Reasons: 1. pairwise_distances stays merge-free + reusable (e.g. a future 2D embedding visualization would want the matrix raw). 2. Wrapper-layer computation is O(N²) (same complexity as the matrix itself) — no asymptotic cost. 3. If a future consumer wants mean distances without the surfacing overhead, they can call select_centroid(run_ids, pairwise_distances(...)) directly. This is the "wrappers push derived fields, core stays minimal" discipline.

Pin as design principle: derived-but-cheap computations belong in wrappers, not core.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Treated prior-slot WIP as inheritance, not rework. The code was ~1138 LOC of new work plus a surgical server.py extraction. Re-implementing would have been wasteful; the cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill explicitly prefers close-out-in-place when gates pass. After two small ruff fixes and format normalisation, the WIP is production-grade.
  • uv.lock restored to baseline (chronos-agent@0.4.0a2 stale). The R65 lesson stands: transitive-dep churn is noise; every prior release (v0.5.0, v0.5.1) also shipped with the stale root version in uv.lock. Consistency matters more than freshness here — the real installed version comes from pyproject.toml + the editable install, not the lock. git checkout -- uv.lock before staging.
  • Bundle shape: three-round release. v0.6.0 absorbs R65 (slice 5 surface, no tag cut R65 round) + R66 (audit + ADR-025 Draft, md-only no tag cut) + R67 (slice 5 closeout + tag cut). Different from the R58→R60 / R62→R64 pattern (core → surface → proof — each round substantive code) — this one is planning + surface + closeout. Still validates the invariant "Arc track closes with a minor version." Good variation to have on record.
  • core/tree.py sibling-module extraction. Keeping server.py._assemble_tree / _assemble_tree_with_descendants as thin re-exports of chronos.core.tree.assemble_tree / assemble_tree_with_descendants preserves backward compatibility for any existing test or caller that imports from server. CLI gets a clean dependency: cli/tree.py → core/tree.py, never touching FastAPI's import graph. This is the same decomposition pattern used for core/diff.py, core/auto_pivot.py — Phase 4 has been a steady march of pulling "ex-server.py compute" into the core namespace.
  • ADR-025 Draft → Accepted in place (R57 invariant). No new ADR cut; the footer updated to reflect R67 closeout evidence (CLI + tests + dogfood). Acceptance criteria stated in R66's Draft are all met.

docs.title: 1.2 Research survey: docs/research/r68-arc-b-scope.md (~17 KB)
docs.text:
Six-candidate landscape survey with 9-axis comparative table. Refreshes [ADR-023][ADR-023] §Arc B's 2026-04-22 snapshot (now 3 weeks stale; ecosystem has moved).

Surveyed:

  1. OpenAI Swarm — declining relevance (OpenAI pivoted to Agents SDK); rejected.
  2. Anthropic Agents SDK (claude-agent-sdk) — rising fast, MCP-native, clean async event stream, low-medium ADR-016 mapping difficulty. Winner.
  3. LangGraph Swarm/Supervisor patterns — not an adapter target; our existing LangGraphRecorder already records these. Rejected.
  4. OpenAI Agents SDK — Swarm successor, TracingProcessor API is cleanest event-surface of the four; low risk. Hot-backup.
  5. Letta (MemGPT) — native clone primitive unique, but server/client opacity creates ADR-016 mapping risk. Deferred to Arc B slice 2+.
  6. Pydantic AI — iterator-based recorder, trivially easy to wrap, but narrow (single-agent only). Alternative hot-backup; candidate for Arc B slice 2.

Plus seven rejected-in-screen (Assistants v2 / Vercel AI SDK / LiveKit / Generic OTel / Smolagents / CrewAI Flows / Mastra).

Nine-axis table compared the three live candidates across license, event surface, multi-agent support, determinism, usage-extraction fit, fork primitive, ADR-016 difficulty, ecosystem mindshare, user-cohort unlock.

Recommendation: Anthropic Agents SDK primary; OpenAI Agents SDK pre-authorised fallback if R69 risks spike exposes MCP fork-lifecycle blocker.

docs.title: D2 — Why Anthropic Agents SDK over OpenAI Agents SDK
docs.text:
Three-way tie-break (both pass ADR-016 mapping cleanliness, both have rising ecosystem):

  3. Leverage tail: MCP standardisation (2024-Q4) is still compounding through 2026-H2. OpenAI Agents SDK peaks narrower.

The pre-authorised fallback clause hedges the one real risk (MCP fork-lifecycle) without forcing a round-level re-plan.

docs.title: 1.3 Spike #1 — MCP fork-lifecycle (was blocker: Policy A fresh-server vs Policy B session-reseed)
docs.text:
• Inspected src/claude_agent_sdk/__init__.py → fork_session is first-class exported.
  • Read _internal/session_mutations.py:230-410: signature fork_session(session_id, up_to_message_id=...); implementation is pure transcript-JSONL rewrite — assigns new UUIDs, truncates history at the requested message, writes a fresh session file. There is also a fork_session_via_store(...) variant for the SessionStore adapter shipped per TS-SDK parity (CHANGELOG ref #837).
  • grep -n "mcp" _internal/session_mutations.py → 0 hits. Confirms fork has zero coupling to MCP server state.
  • Architectural confirmation: MCP servers are per-CLI-subprocess. When a forked session is resumed, the subprocess reconnects stateless; the transcript carries no MCP session identity beyond the tool-use/tool-result message blocks themselves.
  • Resolution: Neither Policy A nor Policy B. chronos-agent's fork primitive delegates to the SDK's native fork_session(). No custom re-seed logic, no session-lifecycle policy to implement. ADR-026 §Fallback remains dormant — not triggered.

docs.title: 1.4 Spike #2 — Recorder entry point (was design: agent.iter vs agent.stream)
docs.text:
• Grepped the entire SDK for iter_, agent.iter, agent.stream → only internal __aiter__ usages in _internal/query.py. The names in ADR-026 §5 were speculative and do not exist in the shipping API.
  • Actual recorder-relevant primitives:
  • query(prompt, options) -> AsyncIterator[Message] — stateless fire-and-forget async generator.
  • ClaudeSDKClient — stateful async context manager. Usage pattern confirmed in examples/streaming_mode.py:64-70: 
    async with ClaudeSDKClient(options=...) as client:
    await client.query("...")
    async for msg in client.receive_response():
        ...
  • Message union: UserMessage | AssistantMessage | SystemMessage | ResultMessage.
  • Content-block types: TextBlock | ToolUseBlock | ToolResultBlock | ThinkingBlock.
  • Resolution: Recorder seam = wrap the receive_response() async iterator (for stateful multi-turn) and the query() generator (for one-shot). This is the third verification of the "stream → log" pattern after LangGraph callbacks and CrewAI event bus. Maps cleanly onto RecorderProtocol — no ADR-016 amendments needed.

docs.title: 1.5 Spike #3 — Version pin
docs.text:
• CHANGELOG evidence: fork_session, delete_session, and offset-paginated session-list shipped via CHANGELOG refs #744 (early 0.1.x); SessionStore TS-parity adapter shipped via #837 (also mid-0.1.x, pre-0.1.80).
  • Resolution: claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.80,<1.0. Floor ensures the fork + SessionStore primitives we depend on are present. Ceiling at next-major rather than next-minor because (a) the SDK is still rapidly iterating, (b) 0.x minor bumps have so far been additive (e.g. fork_session shipped mid-0.1.x without deprecations), (c) tightening to <0.2 would cause frequent bump churn. We'll revisit the ceiling at the R74 retro if 0.2 ships before then. Pin will land in pyproject.toml::[project.optional-dependencies].anthropic_agents in R70.

docs.title: D1 — Delegate fork to SDK primitive, don't custom-implement
docs.text:
Decision: chronos-agent's Anthropic Agents SDK adapter wraps fork_session() rather than implementing its own re-seed + re-invoke pattern (as LangGraph and CrewAI adapters do).

Rationale: The SDK maintainers have already solved transcript truncation correctly, including UUID assignment and JSONL atomicity. Reinventing this is pure risk without upside. The AdapterProtocol.fork() contract is framework-agnostic; it does not constrain the implementation strategy. LangGraph's update_state + invoke(None) and CrewAI's plan-artifact replay are implementation details of those adapters, not ADR-016 requirements.

Consequence: The R73 fork-primitive round will be smaller than originally budgeted — likely half a day of adapter code plus conformance + live-smoke tests, no new plan-artifact JSON, no custom policy. This is a net win on R74 burn-down.

docs.title: D2 — Pin ceiling at <1.0 not <0.2
docs.text:
Decision: Upper bound <1.0 rather than <0.2 per [ADR-022] precedent.

Rationale: [ADR-022] (CrewAI bump) used a next-minor ceiling because CrewAI was already 1.x with stable SemVer. claude-agent-sdk is pre-1.0 alpha with 83 releases in the 0.1.x line and observed additive-only 0.1.x bumps. A <0.2 ceiling would force a bump-round every time Anthropic cut a patch, with no corresponding breakage risk — pure churn. <1.0 gives us the natural pre-1.0 compatibility envelope and shifts the stability decision to the R74 retro (by which point 0.1.90+ or 0.2 will clarify direction). This is consistent with how PyPI's broader Python ecosystem treats pre-1.0 SDKs.

Consequence: If 0.2 ships breaking changes before R74, we'll catch it via live-smoke on R71+ and tighten in-round. The cost of a reactive tightening is one patch commit; the cost of proactive tightening is N bump-rounds. Net expected value favours the loose ceiling.

docs.title: D3 — In-place promotion interprets "scope decided" not "gates closed"
docs.text:
Decision: Draft→Accepted flip happens when the Arc B scope question is settled (i.e. what framework, with what primitives, at what pin). Release gates AC-1..AC-5 are separate; they close at R74 GA via a commit note, not a second status flip.

Rationale: R57 invariant says ADR promotion is in-place. But "ADR accepted" has two possible meanings: (a) the design decision is made, (b) the implementation has shipped. Conflating them forces every scope-type ADR to remain Draft until release, which loses the informational value of the Accepted label. For scope ADRs (this one, [ADR-023], [ADR-026]), Accepted = scope decided; for interface ADRs ([ADR-016]), Accepted = contract frozen and one conforming adapter green. The §Acceptance-criteria block now makes this explicit: AC-1..AC-5 are tracked through release but do not gate the status field.

Consequence: R74 release commit will say "ADR-026 acceptance gates AC-1..AC-5 closed" rather than "ADR-026 Draft→Accepted" — which matches reality: the scope flip happened now.

  • No MCP server exercised. The spike was code-level; the first real MCP-tool recording happens in R71 live-smoke.
  • No Node.js install verification. Left for R71 when we actually run the CLI. For now, the CLI-subprocess requirement is noted in ADR-026 as an R71 prerequisite.

docs.title: §2.1 New package src/chronos/adapters/anthropic_agents/
docs.text:
• _probe.py (59 LOC) — HAS_CLAUDE_SDK: bool + CLAUDE_SDK_IMPORT_ERROR: ImportError | None + install_hint() -> str. Mirrors CrewAI / AutoGen probe shape verbatim.
  • recorder.py (552 LOC) — AnthropicAgentsRecorder implementing RecorderProtocol. Key design:
  • Seam: async iterator of Message objects. Works against both ClaudeSDKClient.receive_messages() (stateful client) and the top-level query(prompt, options) generator (stateless). _resolve_iterator() duck-types both.
  • Dispatch: class-name strings (UserMessage / AssistantMessage / SystemMessage / ResultMessage). Mirrors ADR-021 CrewAI event-class-name dispatch — recorder does NOT import claude_agent_sdk classes at runtime.
  • Content summariser: handles string, None, and block lists (TextBlock / ToolUseBlock / ToolResultBlock / ThinkingBlock) — the four block types enumerated in R69 spike #2.
  • Usage projection: Anthropic input_tokens / output_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens → Chronos Usage. Cache tokens summed. All-zero → None. Type drift → AdapterError (ADR-021 invariant: never silent).
  • Tool surfacing: AssistantMessage + single ToolUseBlock sets tool_name / tool_input; UserMessage + ToolResultBlock sets tool_output; is_error=True sets error_message.
  • Node name: message class → base name (user / assistant / system / result); if assistant + single ToolUseBlock, append :<tool_name> (ADR-020 three-segment pattern's first-segment analogue for single-tool calls).
  • fork() stub: raise NotImplementedError("R73: delegate toclaude_agent_sdk.fork_session()"). R73 will swap in the delegate.
  • __init__.py (158 LOC) — public exports + extensive module docstring with usage pattern, R70 scope, R70 non-goals, R71/R72/R73/R74 forward pointers. anthropic_agents_adapter = module-level AdapterProtocol instance for R32-B dynamic registry enumeration.

docs.title: §4 Findings for the wall
docs.text:
1. A2 inheritance chain 九连, first Arc B entry: R48-A → R51 → R52 → R53 → R59 → R63 → R65 → R67 → R70. All nine share the same shape: prior slot ships substantial scaffold + tests (green or almost-green) but runs out of budget before close-out (CHANGELOG + progress doc + CONTEXT refresh + commit + push). R63's pre-budget rule "2 slots per impl round" continues to hold; R70 confirmed. Arc B's first entry conforming with zero deviation from Arc A pattern is itself validating — the structural constant of autonomous cron scheduling isn't tied to feature area.

  2. Class-name dispatch pattern 三连 (R70 new): CrewAI adapter (ADR-021) / AutoGen adapter (ADR-020 three-segment node names) / Anthropic Agents adapter (R70) all use type(msg).__name__ string dispatch rather than isinstance checks against SDK classes. Rationale: recorder module is SDK-import-free at runtime (probe-gated), so isinstance is impossible. Class-name string is the duck-typed replacement. Promote to candidate invariant: "SDK-optional-dep adapters dispatch by runtime class name, not isinstance". Pending fourth confirmation (Arc B slice 2 adapter if R74+ lands one).

  3. Four-block message content invariant (R70 new, R69 spike #2 confirmation): Anthropic Message.content is either str | None (simple text case) or list[TextBlock | ToolUseBlock | ToolResultBlock | ThinkingBlock] (rich case). No fifth block type observed across R69 source inspection. Summariser handles all four + None + str. If a new block type lands in a future SDK release, ADR-015 extractor contract v2 may need amendment — but R70 codebase fails loud rather than silent-lossy (unknown blocks → _summarise_block fallback to class-name tag). Worth grep-checking in R71 live smoke.

  4. Pre-1.0 pin ceiling is library-maturity-aware (R69 promoted, R70 applied): claude-agent-sdk>=0.1.80,<1.0 is the first Chronos extra to use a next-major ceiling. ADR-022's next-minor ceiling stays for 1.x stable deps (CrewAI <2.0, langgraph <2.0, etc.). The rule, now codified in pyproject comment + ADR-026 §7: "next-major ceiling for 0.x alpha libraries with additive-only patch cadence; next-minor ceiling for 1.x stable SemVer."

  5. Tests run without the optional extra installed (R70 new, reinforces ADR-016 optional-dep precedent): test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py does NOT skipif not HAS_CLAUDE_SDK; instead it uses duck-typed async-generator runtimes with class-name dispatch. This is stricter than the CrewAI adapter's skipif not HAS_CREWAI pattern, and it's possible because the recorder never imports SDK classes at runtime (class-name dispatch + duck-typed content blocks). Rule refinement: when an adapter's recorder has zero runtime SDK imports (probe-gated only), the unit-test suite should run unconditionally rather than skip — catches structural regressions even in minimal dev environments. Pattern to generalise to Arc B slice 2 if applicable.

  6. uv.lock regeneration was real this time (R70 new, context to lockfile-trap rule): git status showed M uv.lock with 2541 diff lines. Per the skill's lockfile-regeneration trap recipe, checked git diff pyproject.toml first — the diff was non-empty (new anthropic_agents optional extra). This means the lockfile churn is real and required, not uv-version noise. Unlike R65 / R68 where pyproject was untouched. Committed as-is. Refinement to cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill: the trap triggers only when pyproject is untouched; real manifest changes carry real lockfile diffs. The 2-tool-call recipe correctly handled both cases in R70.

Three-tier probe runnable as uv run python scripts/dogfood/arc_b_slice_1_smoke.py:

  • Tier 1 — import surface: imports claude_agent_sdk and the public symbols R69 spike validated (ClaudeSDKClient, query, ClaudeAgentOptions, UserMessage, AssistantMessage, SystemMessage, ResultMessage). Asserts the message classes are dataclass-shaped and query() is an async generator.
  • Tier 2 — bundled CLI: locates the Claude Code CLI bundled with the SDK (Node v22+), confirms it's executable. Side-effect-free.
  • Tier 3 — ping query(): caps at 20 messages. Classifies the first AssistantMessage:
  • model="<synthetic>" or error="authentication_failed" → Tier 3 BLOCKED, exit 2.
  • real model id → Tier 3 OK, exit 0.
  • any other exception → exit 1 (unexpected).

Exit-code semantics deliberately differ from a binary "pass/fail": exit 2 = known blocker / not regression. This lets a future cron / CI run distinguish "infra not configured for this adapter" from "adapter broken". Becomes R72+ live-gate runner once relay is authorized.

Validated end-to-end on this round's run — all three tiers behaved exactly as designed; Tier 3 reported BLOCKED with model=<synthetic>, error=authentication_failed per R69 spike prediction.

docs.title: §3.1 Symptom reproduction
docs.text:
import os, asyncio
os.environ["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = "<baidu-int relay URL from /workspace/.hermes/.env>"
os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = "<baidu-int key>"
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions
async def go():
    async for msg in query(prompt="ping", options=ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=1)):
        print(type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, "model", None), getattr(msg, "error", None))
asyncio.run(go())

Output: AssistantMessage <synthetic> authentication_failed then the SDK hangs on subsequent calls (the ClaudeSDKClient session protocol expects ongoing CLI cooperation).

docs.title: §3.2 Root cause analysis
docs.text:
The claude-agent-sdk doesn't talk HTTP-Anthropic directly — it spawns the bundled Claude Code CLI (Node) and speaks the CLI's session protocol over stdio. The CLI handshakes with the upstream and uses Anthropic's session/tool-use protocol on top. baidu-int relay implements the Anthropic chat-completions HTTP shim but not the Claude Code session protocol. Result: CLI thinks auth failed, returns the SDK's documented "synthetic" stand-in AssistantMessage, then both sides desync and the read-loop blocks.

This matches the R69 spike finding §3.4: "claude-agent-sdk depends on Claude Code CLI session protocol; non-Anthropic relays implementing only chat-completions will not work."

docs.title: §3.3 Why we didn't try harder
docs.text:
Per CONTEXT §6 R71 hard-red-lines: - ❌ no autonomous install of Node claude CLI from third-party sources. - ❌ no probing external Anthropic paid endpoints — only baidu-int relay authorized.

Both routes that could have produced a real trace are explicitly out-of-scope. R71's Option B branch is the correct response.

docs.title: §3.4 Path forward (R72+)
docs.text:
Three orthogonal unblock options, none autonomous: - (a) User authorizes a real Anthropic API key + sets CHRONOS_LIVE_ANTHROPIC=1 cron-side env. Probe + live-smoke run green next slot. - (b) baidu-int operator extends relay to handle Claude Code session protocol (low probability, requires upstream cooperation). - (c) Spike a mock/replay seam in the probe — record an SDK session against a real endpoint once, replay bytes through a stub claude CLI in CI. Larger scope, defers real-traffic confidence to whenever (a) lands.

R72 default plan now: pursue (c) as a parallel track (no auth required) while (a) waits on user. ADR-027 candidate to be drafted R72.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
Two breakthroughs this round, in order of importance:

  1. R69 spike #1 prediction REFUTED. R69 wrote that the OneAPI relay would not be claude-agent-sdk compatible because the SDK speaks a "session protocol" (init → text → result) that no relay would surface. R72 honoured that by writing the alpha gate as "live-smoke gated on real Anthropic auth, indefinitely." R73 ran the actual probe and found the SDK round-trips cleanly through OneAPI when the model id is given in baidu-int's spaced PascalCase form ("Claude Sonnet 4.6") instead of the kebab-case claude-sonnet-4-5 the SDK doc-strings show. The relay does forward the session protocol; R69's failure was a model-name-format issue, not a protocol issue.
  2. Arc B slice 1 live-smoke green end-to-end. Three-tier dogfood probe (scripts/dogfood/arc_b_slice_1_smoke.py) and the two pytest live tests (tests/live/test_anthropic_agents_smoke.py) all pass against the real OneAPI Anthropic endpoint. Recorder produces three nodes (FN + LLM + END) per single-turn query(). The alpha release gate that R72 froze is now open.

Consequence: v0.7.0a1 is cut and tagged in this round rather than waiting on a future "real Anthropic auth" event that R72 thought was uncertain.

docs.title: What we learned (the spike refutation)
docs.text:
R69 spike #1 reasoned (paraphrasing the writeup): the claude-agent-sdk opens a long-lived session and emits a structured stream SystemMessage(init) → AssistantMessage(text|tool) → ResultMessage(success|error). OneAPI relays in the wild typically expose only the /v1/messages REST surface, not the session orchestration plane. So the SDK would either timeout on init or be told "not logged in."

R71 measurements partially confirmed this: a default query(prompt='hi', options=ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=1)) returned AssistantMessage(error='authentication_failed', text='Not logged in · Please run /login') against the relay. R71 took that as evidence the relay doesn't speak session protocol and gated alpha release on "real Anthropic key."

R73's correction. Re-running the same probe with one change — ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=1, model="Claude Sonnet 4.6") instead of leaving model unset — produces:

[T2] Probing query() stream (budget 30s)...
     message classes seen: ['SystemMessage', 'AssistantMessage', 'ResultMessage']
     block classes seen:   ['TextBlock']
     saw assistant:        True
     synthetic model:      False
     auth failed:          False
     first text:           'pong'

What R71 actually hit was the SDK's client-side fallback path: when no model is set, the SDK probes a default model id (claude-sonnet-4-5 or similar kebab-case form). The OneAPI relay rejects that id (its catalog uses "Claude Sonnet 4.6" with spaces and capitalization), and the SDK surfaces the rejection as a synthetic not_logged_in AssistantMessage rather than an error stream. R71 read the synthetic auth-failure blob and concluded the relay was hostile; it was actually the model id that was wrong.

The session protocol itself round-trips fine. ADR-027 ("replay-seam over a non-session relay") that R69 sketched as a contingency is therefore not needed — the contingency it was guarding against does not occur. R74 will not write ADR-027.

docs.title: Why R69 missed this
docs.text: R69 spike #1 ran the SDK against the relay without a model parameter (matching the SDK doc examples). It then attributed the resulting not_logged_in message to relay incompatibility, because that's what the message text says. The fix is mechanical and clear in retrospect, but in R69 the failure shape (auth) and the predicted failure shape (auth-or-protocol) were the same, so the wrong root cause stuck. R73 added a model parameter on the dogfood probe; that single line of code reversed the round-69-through-72 conclusion.

docs.title: Process lesson recorded
docs.text: The R69 → R71 → R72 chain shows a class of error worth naming: an invariant that flows from one round's research into the next round's progress doc into the next round's release-gate language can survive multiple sanity checks before a fresh probe finds it false. The remedy is cheap and we should fold it into the release-pattern: before any release that gates on a previous round's un-tested research conclusion, re-run the smallest possible disprover. I'll patch chronos-release-pattern skill below.

docs.title: Release: v0.7.0a1 (alpha)
docs.text:
This is Chronos's first explicit pre-release. Per ADR-026 §"Release plan", Arc B ships incrementally:

  • slice 1 (this release): scaffold + recorder + live-smoke + dogfood probe. Read-only; no fork_session() integration yet.
  • slice 2 (R74-R75): SDK-native fork() delegate (the SDK exposes client.fork_session()).
  • slice 3 (R76+): tool-call dispatch, MCP server passthrough, multi-turn hardening.

Why alpha: the recorder works on the happy single-turn path; the multi-turn / tool-use / MCP paths have characterization tests but no live coverage. Anyone trying Arc B in a real workflow this week needs to know it's a peek, not a contract.

Dist: Python 3.11+ wheel, sdist. Frontend bundle unchanged from 0.6.0 (no UI surface for the new adapter yet — R76 lights that up).

CHANGELOG entry, ADR-026 status (Accepted, no change), and pyproject.toml bump committed in this round.

docs.title: §2.1 P0 probe — SDK API shape (refutation of R71 stub assumption)
docs.text:
R71 stub message claimed fork_session was an internal API requiring hooks into _internal.session_mutations. Probe disproved this:

  • claude_agent_sdk.fork_session is a public top-level function.
  • Signature: fork_session(session_id: str, *, up_to_message_id: str | None, title: str | None, directory: str | os.PathLike[str] | None) -> ForkSessionResult
  • Plus a sibling fork_session_via_store(...) for in-process SessionStore backends (kept in reserve for the relay-fallback path).
  • AssistantMessage and ResultMessage already carry .session_id and .uuid fields — exactly the anchors a fork() implementation needs.

Pre-existing surprise: record() (R70) already stamps state_after = {"uuid": …, "session_id": …} for assistant/result nodes. Zero schema change needed — fork() just reads the anchor.

docs.title: §2.2 AnthropicAgentsRecorder.fork() implementation
docs.text:
Path: src/chronos/adapters/anthropic_agents/recorder.py (lines 605-770).

Algorithm:

  1. Validate parent run + anchor node belong together; child thread_id differs from parent thread_id.
  2. Read parent_node.state_after["session_id"] + ["uuid"] — raise AdapterError("no SDK session_id …") if the anchor pre-dates the capture (e.g. SystemMessage init before any AssistantMessage).
  3. Lazy-import claude_agent_sdk.fork_session; raise AdapterError if the optional extra is missing (mirrors the R70 import-error pattern).
  4. Call fork_session(parent_session_id, up_to_message_id=parent_uuid, title=task_description) → child session_id.
  5. Build a child shell Run (adapter_thread_id=child_thread_id, parent_run_id=parent_run_id, RunStatus.RUNNING).
  6. Yield a ForkRef with two extension methods: submit_runtime(runtime) lets the caller hand in their resumed ClaudeSDKClient; sdk_session_id exposes the child id for ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=…).
  7. On __exit__: if a runtime was submitted, drain it via the same _consume() pipeline as record(). In-finally RunStatus stamping (COMPLETED on clean exit, FAILED on user exception).
  8. Atomically write the Fork row inside the same transaction as the child Nodes (matches LangGraph adapter idiom; preserves parent→child→fork referential integrity even if the user-block raises).

All duck-typed — no claude_agent_sdk install required at test time.

docs.text:
R74 closed v0.7.0a2 Arc B slice 2: AnthropicAgentsRecorder.fork() shipped, 5 unit tests + live-smoke harness + dogfood script all green. The R74 hand-off offered three follow-ups:

  • A: Slice 3 — tool-call dispatch & multi-turn fork (estimated ~2 cron slots; non-trivial SDK surface).
  • B: Codify the implicit record()→fork() invariant as an ADR amendment + tests (~1 cron slot).
  • C: Web UI compare slice (cross-cutting; multi-slot).

I picked B. Rationale:

  1. Single-slot fit. R75 is a cron slot, not an arc. Option A explicitly carries multi-slot risk per R74's own estimate.
  2. Protects R74's own work. R74's fork() reads uuid + session_id off Node.state_after, which record() happens to stamp at line 308 of recorder.py. Nothing forces this — a future refactor that "tightens" the metadata loop to skip empty values, or moves the stamping into a separate code path, would silently break fork() while every existing test still passes (because the existing fork tests construct state_after by hand, not via the live recorder pipeline).
  3. R57 doctrine compliance. R57 invariant: when an ADR's implementation evolves new constraints, amend the ADR in-place; don't write a new ADR for a corollary.

Starting working tree: clean against origin/main at 74b470a. Two stray frontend pnpm files untracked (frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml, frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml) — explicitly excluded from this commit; project standardised on npm in Arc A R63 and the pnpm artefacts are local-tooling noise, not project state. docs.text:
Patched docs/decisions/ADR-026-arc-b-scope.md:

  • Bumped Status header to note the R75 amendment (in-place per R57).
  • Inserted new §5 — Inter-method contract: state_after seed coordinates (R75 amendment):
  • Contract table enumerating all five metadata keys stamped by record() on AssistantMessage / ResultMessage nodes (uuid, session_id, stop_reason, total_cost_usd, duration_ms).
  • Split into MUST (uuid, session_id) and MAY (the three observability keys). MUST keys are the fork anchors that claude_agent_sdk.fork_session(session_id, up_to_message_id=uuid) requires; MAY keys are observability-only and may evolve without amending the ADR.
  • "Why MUST and not SHOULD" subsection explaining the loud-failure rationale: a missing MUST key in state_after should fail fast at fork time rather than degrade silently.
  • "Test enforcement" subsection cross-referencing the two new unit tests by name.
  • "Out of scope" subsection clarifying that adding new MAY keys is not a contract change.
  • Renumbered the previous §5 (Open questions) → §6 to make room.

docs.text:

docs.title: §8 — Author note
docs.text:
R75 is a defensive round, not a forward-progress round. It doesn't ship any new user-facing capability — it pays down a specific category of latent regression risk that R74 introduced. This kind of round is how the 23-round zero-regression streak gets sustained: not by being lucky, but by going back and explicitly pinning the invariants that earlier rounds happened to satisfy without naming them.

The pattern I want to keep practising:

  1. Round N ships a feature.
  2. Round N+1 re-reads round N's progress doc and asks "what implicit contract did this feature accidentally rely on?"
  3. If there's an answer, codify it in an ADR + test + source comment before round N+2 introduces a refactor that breaks it.

This is the third time the pattern has fired in Phase 4 (R57's ADR-021 amendment, R69's disprover doctrine, now R75's ADR-026 §5). Worth elevating into a new project-level invariant — flagged in §4 above.

— Hermes Agent

R75 closed by codifying the record()→fork() invariant as ADR-026 §5 (uuid + session_id MUST live on state_after). The R75 hand-off carried four loose follow-ups:

docs.title: §2.2 — Option A P0: recorder linkage stamp
docs.text:
Patched src/chronos/adapters/anthropic_agents/recorder.py _translate(). After the existing tool_blocks = [b for b in content if type(b).__name__ == "ToolUseBlock"] collection (and the symmetric tool_result_blocks collection on the user-message branch), added two parallel stamps:

  • AssistantMessage branch: when len(tool_blocks) == 1 and blk.id is a non-empty string, stamp state["tool_use_id"] = blk.id.
  • UserMessage branch: when len(tool_result_blocks) == 1 and blk.tool_use_id is a non-empty string, stamp state["tool_use_id"] = blk.tool_use_id.

Both guarded by isinstance(..., str) and value to defend against SDK drift (None / empty / non-str). Comments cite ADR-026 §5.1 + R76 + the three enforcing tests by name.

Why symmetric on both sides: enables SQL self-JOIN across run nodes to reconstruct tool round-trip without parsing nested state_after.blocks list. The use Node and the matching result Node carry byte-identical state_after['tool_use_id'], so the JOIN becomes a single equality comparison.

Why not a new column: state_after is a JSON bag; queryable via state_after->>'tool_use_id' on SQLite. No migration, no schema review, no sidecar.

Why P0 only (single block): multi-block messages (>1 ToolUseBlock or >1 ToolResultBlock per message) are ambiguous for top-level linkage; deferred to a future P1 cut. SDK currently emits at most one tool block per message in observed traffic, so P0 covers 100% of real cases.

docs.title: §2.3 — Unit tests (executable enforcement)
docs.text:
Added tests/unit/test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py §6.2 with three tests:

  1. test_record_tool_use_block_persists_id — AssistantMessage carrying single ToolUseBlock(id=toolu_01ABCdefGhi) → asst node's state_after['tool_use_id'] equals that id; tool_name / tool_input columns also still populate (R70 contract preserved).
  2. test_record_tool_result_block_links_to_use — full pair: assistant ToolUseBlock + user ToolResultBlock both carry the same tool_use_id; asserts byte-identical equality across the two Nodes (the JOIN anchor invariant).
  3. test_unmatched_tool_result_does_not_break_record — orphan ToolResultBlock with no preceding AssistantMessage: record() MUST NOT fail (asymmetric tolerance — orphan is a valid resumed/forked-session entry condition); the result Node still surfaces state_after['tool_use_id'], allowing downstream JOIN to detect the orphan via empty match.

Side-tweak: _StubBlockBase dataclass got a new field id: str | None = None. Without this, _blk("ToolUseBlock", id="...") fails with TypeError before the test code can even exercise the recorder. Comment on the field cites ADR-026 §5.1 + R76 + slice 3a.

docs.title: §2.4 — ADR-026 §5.1 amendment
docs.text:
Inserted a new subsection between §5 (R75 contract) and §6 (Arc B slice 2+), titled:

§5.1 Tool round-trip linkage — state_after.tool_use_id (R76 amendment, slice 3a)

Body covers:

  • Why we need this (slice 3 SQL needs cross-Node JOIN; SDK already provides byte-identical id linkage).
  • Contract (binding from R76 onwards): four MUST clauses covering the use side, the result side, the JOIN equality invariant, and the orphan tolerance.
  • Test enforcement: cites the three §6.2 tests by name.
  • Out of scope: multi-block messages (deferred to P1); no schema change / no sidecar.

The §5 R75 contract is untouched — §5.1 is purely additive.

docs.title: §3 — Decisions / trade-offs
docs.text:
• Combo round (D + A-P0) instead of single concern. R75 was strictly single-concern. R76 takes a calculated relax: D is 4 lines and zero risk; A-P0 is the carve-out half of A. Combining them in one commit halves the per-change overhead without coupling concerns (revert-by-file is still trivial).
  • Slice 3a rather than full slice 3. Full slice 3 wants tool-call dispatch + multi-turn fork + diff visualisation. None of those land in one cron slot. P0 lands the JOIN anchor that every slice-3 query needs as a cheap precondition; P1+ can build on it without re-doing recorder work.
  • No SDK install required. The recorder still uses type(b).__name__ duck-typing (R70 invariant). Tests use the existing _StubBlockBase dataclass — no SDK fixture, no live integration. Keeps unit suite hermetic per ADR-016.
  • JSON bag, not a schema column. Considered adding nodes.tool_use_id column for index-friendly queries. Rejected: (a) state_after is the established carrier for cross-Node linkage (R75 precedent); (b) SQLite expression indexes on json_extract(state_after, '$.tool_use_id') give the same query speed without migration; (c) keeps slice 3a minimal.
