docs.title: §2.1 Decision: pure-Python over raw SQL
docs.text:
ADR-026 §5.1.1's SQL recipe is the canonical raw-query form (LEFT JOIN with json_each). My helper sits one layer above that, deliberately:

  • Uses store.get_nodes_for_run(run_id) — a public SqliteStore method already in use across adapters.
  • Builds two Python sets (use-side ids, result-side ids) in one pass.
  • Returns Node rows in stream order whose declared id is absent from the complementary set.

Reasoning: 1. Keeps SqliteStore public API surface unchanged (no new method, no new column). 2. _conn is private — pure-Python path avoids the # type: ignore-prone privileged route. 3. ADR-026's SQL recipe remains the canonical raw form for consumers who want SQL (e.g., dashboards, CLI tools). The helper is the in-Python convenience for adapter-level / dogfood-script consumers who want a list-of-Node back without the JOIN ceremony. 4. O(N) load is fine for a debugging/observability helper — not on a hot path.

Trade-off accepted: this re-walks all Nodes per call (vs. an indexed SQL JOIN). Acceptable for the helper's stated audience.

  1. ADR-026 §5.2 amendment (Draft) — full contract for fork(..., tool_input_overrides=...), sibling to §5.1 / §5.1.1, in-place per R57.
  2. 4 tests in tests/unit/test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py — 1 expected-pass identity guard + 3 pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True) tests describing the R80 deliverable.
  3. No-op pass-through on AnthropicAgentsRecorder.fork() — accepts the new tool_input_overrides kwarg, raises NotImplementedError on non-empty mappings (so xfail tests get a precise error shape, not TypeError).

All gates green: 624 pass / 7 skip / 3 xfail / 0 fail, mypy ✓, ruff check ✓, ruff format ✓.

R80 = swap the NotImplementedError raise for the validation pipeline + child-side substitution stamp; xfail markers come off in the same commit (the strict-xfail trip is the forcing function).

docs.title: 2. Resolve a context-compaction misread
docs.text:
The mid-round context was compacted. The compaction summary asserted the active task was "slice 3b query layer (tool_pairs)" with tests in tests/unit/test_queries_tool_linkage.py. That was wrong.

docs/CONTEXT.md §6 (the source of truth) explicitly says R79 ships the fork-with-tool-substitution TDD scaffold (Option A), with tests in tests/unit/test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py. The compaction also missed that R78 already shipped chronos.queries.tool_linkage (commit fed0412).

I caught the discrepancy by reading CONTEXT §6 fresh after the compaction and confirmed the actual deliverables before any code landed. Lesson logged at the bottom (F1).

docs.title: 3. ADR-026 §5.2 amendment
docs.text:
Inserted a new section between §5.1.1 (line 291) and "### 6. What Arc B slice 2+ looks like" (now line 461). Sibling-extends, does NOT supersede — per R57 in-place ADR amendment invariant.

§5.2 specifies:

  • Contract: fork(..., tool_input_overrides: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None). Mapping tool_use_id → new_input_dict. Both singular (R76 §5.1) and plural (R77 §5.1.1) anchors are valid keys (per-id granular, not per-Node).
  • Identity defaults: None and {} are both identity forks — semantically equivalent to R74. Keeps R74 callers source-stable.
  • Stamp on child Nodes:
  • state_after['tool_use_id'] / element of state_after['tool_use_ids'] — UNCHANGED. JOIN anchor binding contract preserved across fork.
  • state_after['tool_input'] — NEW. Substituted dict; absent on Nodes that did not have their input rewritten. For multi-block nodes, this is a list aligned by index with tool_use_ids, null entries for verbatim blocks.
  • Validation (fail-fast): Three rules — key-type, unknown-id, orphan-use-id (using chronos.queries.tool_linkage.unmatched_tool_uses for the slice-3a→3b coupling). All raise AdapterError before the SDK fork_session call.
  • Test enforcement: References the four R79 tests by name + rationale.
  • Consumer SQL pattern: Singular form (json_extract(state_after, '$.tool_input')) and plural form (json_each with index-aligned je.key = ji.key per §5.1.1).
  • Out of scope: ToolResultBlock substitution (slice 3c / §5.3), multi-step substitutions in one call (supported but discouraged), HTTP/CLI surface (separate slice), chronos.queries.tool_linkage promotion (still internal until dedicated ADR).

This is the load-bearing slice-3a → slice-3b coupling: R78's unmatched_tool_uses helper exists for this validation rule. Slice 3a's reader-side closure (R78) is now actively used by the §5.2 spec — exactly the two-layer architecture (frozen contract = SQL recipe in ADR / mutable convenience = Python helper) ratified at R78.

docs.title: 4. Test file: tests/unit/test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py
docs.text:
Four tests, all driving the live record() pipeline to honor the R75 writer-side redundancy invariant:

  1. test_fork_without_overrides_is_identity — EXPECTED PASS (no xfail marker). Verifies both tool_input_overrides=None and ={} succeed and produce a child Run in RunStatus.COMPLETED with no state_after['tool_input'] stamp on any child Node. R74 identity guard.
  2. test_fork_with_override_changes_downstream_input — xfail(strict= True). The meat. Records a parent with one closed tool round-trip (tool_use_id="tu_t1_closed"), forks with {"tu_t1_closed": {"x": 99}}, asserts the child Node has state_after['tool_use_id']== "tu_t1_closed" (unchanged) AND state_after['tool_input']== {"x": 99} (new substitution stamp).
  3. test_fork_with_override_of_unknown_id_raises — xfail(strict= True). Override key absent from parent's use-side keyset. Raises AdapterError. Invariant check: SDK fork_session never invoked ("session_id" not in fake_sdk capture dict).
  4. test_fork_with_override_of_orphan_use_id_raises — xfail(strict= True). Slice-3a→3b coupling. Sets up an unclosed tool use (use-side orphan), pre-asserts unmatched_tool_uses(store, run_id) surfaces it (R78 contract dependency), then asserts fork(..., tool_input_overrides={orphan_id: ...}) raises AdapterError and never invokes SDK.

Helper choices:

  • _record_parent_with_closed_tool_pair — 3-message fixture (AssistantMessage[ToolUseBlock] → UserMessage[ToolResultBlock] → AssistantMessage[TextBlock]) with the final assistant message carrying the uuid + session_id for fork seeding.
  • _record_parent_with_orphan_tool_use — 1-message fixture for slice-3a→3b coupling test.
  • _drive_child_branch — wraps recorder.fork() + submit_runtime() with the canonical child stream (one AssistantMessage[ToolUseBlock]).
  • fake_sdk fixture — installs a fake claude_agent_sdk module via monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, ...), returns a captured dict the test can inspect to verify fork_session args + a next_session_id slot the test sets to control the child SDK session id.

Strict-xfail rationale: when R80 ships the validation + stamp implementation, all three xfail tests flip to passing → strict-xfail trips → CI fails until R80 agent removes the markers. Forcing function for R80 closeout completeness.

docs.title: 5. No-op pass-through on recorder.fork() (Plan §6 P1)
docs.text:
Three-line addition right after del runtime in fork():

if tool_input_overrides:
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "AnthropicAgentsRecorder.fork: tool_input_overrides is the "
        "ADR-026 §5.2 (slice 3b) surface; implementation lands in "
        "R80. R79 ships the kwarg as a no-op pass-through (identity "
        "fork only). See docs/decisions/ADR-026-arc-b-scope.md §5.2."
    )

Plus the new kwarg in the signature (tool_input_overrides: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None) and the Args: docstring entry.

This is the single function body R80 will edit. Validation #1-#3 + child-side substitution stamp will replace this if-block. ~30-50 LOC estimate for R80 implementation diff.

docs.title: D1. Inline stub helpers (deferred extraction)
docs.text:
This is the THIRD test file replicating the duck-typed _StubBlock / _StubMessage / _aiter pattern (after test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py and test_queries_tool_linkage.py). The R58 / R78 convention says "extract on third occurrence" — so technically R79 should extract.

I deferred the extraction because:

  • R79 budget is ADR + tests + pass-through (already 3 deliverables). Adding a cross-file refactor (extract → 3 import sites updated → 3 test files re-verified) bloats the round and increases regression surface during a TDD-only round.
  • The TDD scaffold round should ship a clean spec + clean red tests. Mixing in a refactor blurs the cause-of-failure should anything trip in R80.
  • I left a prominent NOTE in the new test file's module docstring pointing at tests/unit/fixtures/anthropic_agents.py and naming R80 (or a follow-up defensive round) as the extraction owner.

This is technically my fourth deferral of a candidate refactor (defensive-followup-round skill is also still pending from R75-deferred, R76-deferred, R77-deferred, R78-deferred). Five deferrals = pattern. R80 should pick whichever is on the critical path.

docs.title: D2. Strict-xfail vs. skip
docs.text:
Per the plan, I went with pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="slice 3b — R80") over pytest.mark.skip. Rationale (was: "Recommend xfail(strict=True) — 主动守 R80 实施 (xfail-but-pass = R80 done & 提示 删掉标记)"):

  • skip is silent — R80 agent can land the implementation and forget to delete the markers; tests stay skipped, no signal.
  • xfail(strict=True) is loud — when impl flips them to passing, the strict mode trips and CI goes red. The R80 agent must delete the markers to make CI green again. Built-in completeness check.

docs.title: D3. Identity guard test on R79 (not xfail)
docs.text:
The plan called out test #1 (test_fork_without_overrides_is_identity) as "sanity, expected pass". I initially marked it xfail like the others and the run flagged XPASS(strict) → strict-xfail trip.

Reasoning: my R79 pass-through accepts the kwarg and falls through to the R74 verbatim fork path when the mapping is None / empty. So the identity contract is already satisfied in R79; the test should PASS (not xfail) and act as a regression guard during R80 development (if R80 accidentally breaks identity by always running the substitution pipeline, this test trips first).

Removed the xfail marker on test #1, kept it on tests #2-4. Result: 1 pass + 3 xfailed, exactly as ADR §5.2 ####Test enforcement prescribes.

docs.title: D4. Validation #3 wording — "use-side orphan" not "any orphan"
docs.text:
The ADR specifies validation #3 as "appears in unmatched_tool_uses", which is the use-side orphan helper. There's a symmetric unmatched_tool_results (result-side orphan), but slice 3b only needs the use-side check because:

  • Slice 3b rewrites ToolUseBlock.input — the asymmetric concern is "is the use side currently pending a result?" not "is some random result orphaned?".
  • A result-side orphan (use missing for a recorded result) doesn't block slice 3b — those are typically "recorder picked up a resumed session mid-conversation" cases (§5.1's fourth contract clause), unrelated to whether you can rewind the use side.

Test #4 is named test_fork_with_override_of_orphan_use_id_raises to make this precise (not ..._of_orphan_id_raises).

docs.title: F1. Context compaction can misalign on round identity
docs.text:
When mid-round context is compacted, the summary may misremember the actual task plan if the compactor skews toward recently-loaded files. In R79's case, the compaction summary said "slice 3b query layer / tool_pairs module / test_queries_tool_linkage.py" — but CONTEXT.md §6 is the source of truth and clearly says "slice 3b TDD scaffolding for fork-with-tool-substitution / test_anthropic_agents_ fork_tool_override.py".

Recovery recipe (worked here):

  1. After context compaction, the first action MUST be re-reading docs/CONTEXT.md §5 + §6 fresh. Do not trust the summary's task description.
  2. Cross-check by git log --oneline -10 to confirm the actual HEAD (the summary may also be wrong about what shipped).
  3. If the summary disagreed with CONTEXT, log the discrepancy in the progress doc (this section) so future rounds know the compaction layer can drift.

This is round-handoff hygiene that scales: even if the human-written CONTEXT and the agent-written round summary agree, a context compaction layer between them can introduce drift.

docs.title: F2. ruff SIM117 nested-with auto-fix is safe
docs.text:
In tests #3 and #4, I wrote:

with pytest.raises(AdapterError, match="..."):
    with recorder.fork(...):
        pytest.fail("...")

ruff flagged SIM117 (combine with statements). --fix collapsed them into a single with pytest.raises(...), recorder.fork(...): block, which is semantically equivalent and more idiomatic. No behavior change, all tests still red on the same line. Auto-fix is safe for SIM117 in pytest.raises scaffolds.

docs.title: F3. Slice-3a → slice-3b coupling validates two-layer architecture
docs.text:
R78 shipped unmatched_tool_uses as an internal helper, with the two-layer architecture pinned: SQL recipe in ADR is contractual surface, Python helper is mutable convenience. R79 is the first round to use the helper — and it does so as part of an ADR amendment (§5.2 validation #3). The internal helper is now load-bearing for a later contract.

This validates the R78 F1 prediction: "Helper is internal — may evolve freely between minor versions; SQL recipe is the contractual surface. Reusable when a future ADR amendment adds a new JSON-bag key (slice 3b/3c will follow this pattern)." R79 §5.2 is the first follow-on. Slice 3c (§5.3, MCP passthrough) likely the second.

The clarification: when an ADR pins behavior that uses the internal helper (rather than just defining a new bag key), the helper's identity-of-callers becomes part of the ADR's contract. R79 §5.2's validation #3 now explicitly mentions chronos.queries.tool_linkage._ ids_from_state_after and unmatched_tool_uses by name — so even though they're "internal", their semantics are pinned by the ADR. Internal-API mutability has soft limits.

docs.title: F4. Strict-xfail as a forcing-function pattern
docs.text: Saving this for re-use across the project: when shipping a TDD scaffold round (spec + red tests, impl deferred to next round), use pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="slice X — R{N+1}") rather than pytest.mark.skip. The strict mode means any accidental "skip removal" by the impl agent without removing the marker → CI red. This is a structural completeness check that doesn't rely on the impl agent reading the round-handoff invariants section.

docs.title: F5. The "fork-and-submit_runtime" test ergonomics
docs.text:
recorder.fork() is a context manager that yields a ForkRef, and the user calls ref.submit_runtime(child_runtime) inside the with block. This is fine for happy-path tests but awkward for "fork should raise before yielding" tests — the with block must not be entered at all if validation fails.

Solution shape (used in tests #3 and #4):

with pytest.raises(AdapterError, match="..."), recorder.fork(...):
    pytest.fail("fork() should have raised AdapterError before yielding")

pytest.raises is the outer context, so a raise from recorder.fork()'s __enter__ (i.e. before the yield) propagates correctly and pytest.fail() is unreachable. Confirmed in the xfail-strict path: when R80 lands the validation, the raise will fire from the __enter__ site (after _validate_overrides runs but before the yield), and pytest.raises catches it.

This is a useful pattern for any "validate-before-yield" context manager test in the codebase. Worth promoting to the conftest / fixtures as a helper.

docs.title: What's next (R80)
docs.text:
Round 80 — Slice 3b implementation (forcing function: 3 strict-xfail tests are waiting)

Estimated 1.5 slot. Critical path:

  1. Validation pipeline (§5.2 #### Validation) in recorder.fork(), replacing the NotImplementedError raise:
  2. Build use-side keyset from _ids_from_state_after(_is_use_side(node)) over all parent run nodes (re-use the chronos.queries.tool_linkage private helpers; if needed, promote _ids_from_state_after / _is_use_side to module-level public).
  3. Compute orphan-use set via unmatched_tool_uses(store, parent_run_id).
  4. For each (tu_id, new_input) in tool_input_overrides: validate isinstance(tu_id, str), tu_id in keyset, tu_id not in orphan_set. Raise AdapterError with diagnostic message on first violation.
  5. Child-side stamp (§5.2 #### Stamp on child Nodes) in _translate (or wherever _PendingNode.state_after is built):
  6. Pass tool_input_overrides down through the _consume / _translate call chain (probably via self._fork_overrides instance attribute set in fork() and read in _translate).
  7. When stamping state_after for an AssistantMessage Node carrying ToolUseBlock(s), check if any of the block ids appear in the override mapping. If so:
    • Singular form (1 block): state_after['tool_input'] = overrides[tu_id].
    • Plural form (>1 block): state_after['tool_input'] = [overrides. get(tid) for tid in tool_use_ids] (None for unmodified blocks, index-aligned per §5.1.1).
  8. Remove xfail markers on tests #2-4 in test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py once impl lands + tests pass. The strict-xfail trip is the forcing function — R80 commit MUST remove markers in same commit as impl.
  9. Dogfood proof: extend scripts/dogfood/arc_b_slice_1_smoke.py (or write arc_b_slice_3b_smoke.py) to demonstrate the workflow end-to-end against a live SDK call. R80 dogfood gate per ADR-016 "dogfood-as-release-gate" invariant.
  10. CHANGELOG R80 entry above R79; "Removed" section flagging the xfail markers' removal.
  11. Optional / time-permitting: extract _StubBlock / _StubMessage / _aiter to tests/unit/fixtures/anthropic_agents.py (D1 deferred from R79, fourth deferral).

After R80, slice 3b is closed. R81 candidate: - v0.7.0a3 alpha cut (slice 3a + 3b shipped) OR - slice 3c entry (§5.3 MCP passthrough scoping) — pure-md exploratory round.

R80 closes the slice-3b loop opened by R79: turns the NotImplementedError("R80: §5.2 slice 3b not yet implemented") placeholder into the real validation + child-side stamping pipeline, removes the strict-xfail markers, and ships a runnable dogfood script that demos all 4 §5.2 paths end-to-end against a fake claude_agent_sdk.

docs.title: 1. Dogfood script bugfixes (scripts/dogfood_fork_tool_override.py)
docs.text:
The prior slot wrote 326 lines of dogfood that exercised all 4 paths end-to-end, but the fake claude_agent_sdk.fork_session and the post-fork ref attribute access didn't match the recorder's actual contracts. Three runtime bugs fixed in this slot:

  1. Fake fork_session signature mismatch — recorder calls it as fork_session(parent_session_id, up_to_message_id=..., title=...) (positional first arg + kwargs); fake had *, session_id: str, **kwargs (keyword-only). Fixed to def fork_session(session_id: str, /, **kwargs: Any) -> _FakeForkResult, mirroring the unit-test fixture in tests/unit/test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py:161-171.
  2. Fake return type — recorder reads fork_result.session_id; fake returned a bare str. Now returns a _FakeForkResult dataclass with a session_id: str field, again mirroring the test fixture.
  3. ref.run_id vs ref.child_run_id — recorder.record() returns a RunRef with .run_id; recorder.fork() returns a ForkRef with .child_run_id. Three of the script's accesses had the wrong attribute. Plus a name-shadowing bug at the orphan-anchor lookup (orphan_anchor rebound from str to Node, then used as dict key on a later tool_input_overrides={...} line). Fixed by introducing a separate orphan_anchor_node binding.
  4. Over-narrow node filter — n.kind.startswith("AssistantMessage") was filtering the override-stamp lookup, but the test harness in the unit suite doesn't filter by kind (just by state_after['tool_use_id']). Removed the redundant filter.

docs.title: Decisions / notes
docs.text:
• Why _FakeForkResult over SimpleNamespace? The unit-test fixture uses a frozen-style dataclass with a single session_id field; copying that exact shape keeps the dogfood script's contract identical to what the test suite blesses. Future SDK shape extensions (e.g. parent_session_id, created_at) will land in both places at once.
  • Why not collapse R79 + R80 into one commit? R79 was already a separate logical unit (TDD scaffold + ADR amendment + no-op pass-through, all reviewable independently from impl). Two commits preserve the strict-xfail forcing function story: R79 lays the trap, R80 springs it. This slot ships R80 only because R79 was committed (or staged) by the prior slot in this same session. → Verified at start of slot: git log --oneline -5 shows last commit is R78 (fed0412). So R79 was not committed by the prior slot either — both R79 and R80 changes are uncommitted. Decision: pack both into a single R80 commit since they're inseparable now (xfail markers don't exist as a stable intermediate state — they were removed at impl-land time, as the strict-xfail design intended). §5.3 amendment inserted before ### 6. (line 461). Major sub-sections:

  • Contract — tool_result_overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None kwarg on fork(). Key = tool_use_id (same JOIN anchor as §5.1 / §5.1.1). Value = JSON-serialisable Python (typically str or list of content blocks). None / {} are no-ops.

    3. No double-substitution: a key MUST NOT also appear in tool_input_overrides. Rewriting both input and result for the same tool_use_id is contradictory (input rewrite implies re-invocation; result rewrite implies non-invocation). AdapterError quoting the conflicting id.

  • Child-side stamp: state_after['tool_result_content'] (singular) for §5.1 result Nodes; state_after['tool_result_contents'] (plural, index-aligned) for §5.1.1 multi-block result Nodes. Mutually exclusive, same len==1 / len>1 rule. JOIN anchors tool_use_id / tool_use_ids preserved byte-for-byte.

docs.title: D2 — Validation #2 anchors against result-side keyset, not use-side
docs.text:
This is a deliberate deviation from the CONTEXT.md §6 R81 plan. That plan (lines 722, 725) sketched §5.3 as allowing orphan-use-id substitution — "the user might want to inject a result for a tool_use that didn't get one in the parent" — and listed Test 4 as test_fork_with_result_override_of_orphan_use_id_succeeds (strict-xfail, expected to succeed under R82).

I shipped a stricter contract instead. Rationale:

  • The natural intuition was "use the same use-side keyset as §5.2 since they're keyed by the same tool_use_id". I rejected that because the user story for §5.3 is "the tool ALREADY closed the round-trip in the parent — replay reasoning under a hypothetical result". An orphan use-id (R76's tolerance clause) means the round-trip didn't close in the parent → there's no ToolResultBlock Node in the parent run for the override to "rewrite" → the override doesn't have a clear binding target.
  • "Inject a result that didn't exist in the parent" is a different semantic primitive than "rewrite an existing result". The former is closer to a test-double / mock injection; the latter is replay-with-substitution. Conflating them in one kwarg invites confusion downstream when consumers SQL-enumerate substituted calls.
  • A future slice 3d (if real demand surfaces) can introduce a separate tool_result_injections kwarg with explicit "no parent result Node" semantics. Keeping §5.3 strictly mirror-symmetric to §5.2 (both reject half-open round-trips) makes ADR-026 §5 a coherent block.

The slice-3a→3c coupling pre-condition is therefore the same as slice-3a→3b's: round-trip must close in parent run before fork-with-substitution can rewrite either side. Both §5.2 and §5.3 reject half-open round-trips, just on different sides.

Test 4 also changed shape: where the CONTEXT plan had a 4th xfail "orphan-id succeeds" test, I shipped a 4th xfail test_fork_with_result_override_collides_with_input_override_raises instead — a §5.3-unique validation #3 (no double-substitution) that the CONTEXT plan didn't anticipate. The orphan-id-succeeds case is deferred indefinitely pending real user demand; if it shows up, R83+ ships it as tool_result_injections (separate kwarg) per the rationale above.

This deviation is logged here per project convention (direction drift must be argued in progress doc).

docs.title: D3 — Validation #3 (no double-substitution) is §5.3-unique
docs.text: §5.2 has no equivalent of "no double-substitution" — its validation list is just key-type / unknown-id / orphan-id. §5.3 adds the new collision check because both override mappings can land on the same fork() call and the semantics contradict (input rewrite ⇒ re-invocation; result rewrite ⇒ non-invocation). Catching this fail-fast in R82 is cheaper than letting downstream consumers reason about a self-contradictory state.

docs.title: D4 — Defer fixture extraction to R82 / follow-up
docs.text:
This is the FOURTH file replicating _StubBlock / _StubMessage / _aiter (after test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py, test_queries_tool_linkage.py, test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py). The R58 / R78 convention (extract at 3 duplications) is now exceeded. Deliberately deferred:

  • TDD scaffold rounds should not also do cross-file refactors (scope discipline).
  • The R82 implementation diff will already touch recorder.py:fork() and the new test file; bundling a 4-file refactor invites merge friction.

Tracked as next-round defensive TODO. R82 (post-impl) or a dedicated cleanup round should extract to tests/unit/fixtures/anthropic_agents.py.

docs.title: D5 — Stamp keys named tool_result_content / tool_result_contents
docs.text:
§5.2 used tool_input / tool_inputs. The natural symmetric pair would be tool_result / tool_results — but I chose tool_result_content / tool_result_contents to:

  • Mirror the SDK's ToolResultBlock.content field name exactly (consumer recipes stay grep-able from SDK docs to chronos state_after).
  • Avoid collision with any future tool_result aggregate / metadata field.
  • Surface the fact that the override replaces the content payload specifically, not the entire ToolResultBlock structure (which retains its tool_use_id JOIN anchor on the SDK-side block; only content is overridden).

Documented in §5.3 #### Child-side stamp.

docs.title: §1.1. Two divergent stub shapes — refactor 5, defer 1
docs.text:
A grep audit of _StubBlock / _StubMessage / _aiter references surfaced 6 sites (CONTEXT.md §6 R84 hand-off matched), but two structurally different shapes:

Shape Files Style Static-subclass (refactored) test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_override.py, test_anthropic_agents_fork_tool_result_override.py, test_queries_tool_linkage.py, dogfood_fork_tool_override.py, dogfood_fork_tool_result_override.py _StubBlock base + named subclasses TextBlock / ToolUseBlock / ToolResultBlock and UserMessage / AssistantMessage. Identical fields across all 5. Runtime-factory (deferred) test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py _StubBlockBase with richer fields (is_error, thinking, signature) + _blk(cls_name, **kw) runtime-subclass factory. No static subclasses.

Refactor scope: 5 sites migrated, 1 site intentionally deferred. Merging would either bloat the shared module's static surface (carrying is_error/thinking/signature for callers that don't need them — R64 anti-pattern: future-proof slots are falsification targets) or drop the named-subclass ergonomics 5 of 6 sites depend on. R85+ may reconcile if a forcing function appears.

The shared module exports both forms (StubBlock static + make_block(cls_name, **kw) factory) so the deferred file could migrate later without growing the module's surface.

docs.title: §1.3. Dogfood sys.path bootstrap (4 lines)
docs.text:
Pytest adds the repo root to sys.path automatically (because [tool.pytest.ini_options].testpaths = ["tests"]), so from tests.unit.fixtures.* import ... resolves naturally inside tests. Dogfoods, however, run as python scripts/dogfood_*.py and only have '' (cwd) + the installed-package's src/-prefixed entry on sys.path. The shared module is not distributed inside the package (it's a test-only helper).

Two viable patches:

  • A. Move the module under src/chronos/_testing/ so it ships with the package. ✗ Pollutes the public install with test fixtures; warrants an ADR.
  • B. Bootstrap sys.path in each dogfood (4 lines: import Path + sys, sys.path.insert(0, repo_root)). ✓ Already-imported modules; localized; honest about what's happening.

Chose B. The bootstrap block is wrapped in a comment explaining why and pointing at R84.

docs.title: Static taxonomy (used by 5 refactored sites)
docs.text:
• StubBlock — @dataclass with optional text / name / input / id / tool_use_id / content slots. Recorder dispatches kind on type(block).__name__, so subclass names matter, isinstance does not.
  • TextBlock, ToolUseBlock, ToolResultBlock — empty subclasses of StubBlock.
  • StubMessage — @dataclass with content / usage / model / stop_reason / total_cost_usd / duration_ms / uuid / session_id / extra slots.
  • UserMessage, AssistantMessage — empty subclasses of StubMessage.
  • aiter_messages(messages: list[Any]) -> AsyncIterator[Any] — drop-in for the previous _aiter.

docs.title: Runtime factories (parity with test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py style; NOT yet consumed)
docs.text:
• make_block(cls_name: str, **kw) -> StubBlock — runtime subclass with the given class name (for ad-hoc kinds without polluting the static taxonomy, e.g. make_block("ThinkingBlock", text="...")).
  • make_message(cls_name: str, **kw) -> StubMessage — companion for messages.

The factories are in place so a future R85+ migration of test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py is mechanical, not a redesign. Their inclusion is defensive, not speculative: the deferred file already calls _blk(cls_name, **kw) and _msg(cls_name, **kw) 30+ times, so the API is anchored in real existing usage, not future hypothetical needs (R64 anti-pattern check passed).

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Does NOT replace test_adapter_anthropic_agents.py's _StubBlockBase. That file uses richer fields (is_error, thinking, signature); merging would either bloat or break asymmetric.
  • Does NOT export _FakeClient. Each call site has slightly different connect() / disconnect() / awaitable shapes; the helper isn't a clean shared API.
  • Does NOT pre-add is_error / thinking / signature slots to StubBlock. R64 invariant: future-proof slots are falsification targets. Add when a consumer needs them, not earlier.

docs.title: §4. Refactor mechanics (the part that surprised me)
docs.text:
The static-subclass form has stable internal references — every test references _StubBlock / _StubMessage / _aiter 5–12× per file. Four-step recipe per file:

  1. Rename: regex sub \b_StubBlock\b → StubBlock, \b_StubMessage\b → StubMessage, \b_aiter\b → aiter_messages across the whole file.
  2. Cut: remove the stub-def block (from # --- Stub ... section header to right before @dataclass\nclass _FakeClient). For test_queries_tool_linkage.py, end-marker is # Fixtures instead because it has no _FakeClient.
  3. Import: insert the fixture import after import pytest (or for dogfoods, after the chronos imports + sys.path bootstrap).
  4. Auto-fix unused imports: ruff check --fix clears the F401s that the over-broad import block introduced (e.g. test_queries_tool_linkage.py doesn't use StubMessage directly — only the subclass UserMessage / AssistantMessage).

Ruff's auto-fix removed 13 unused-imports across the 4 import blocks — let it shrink to per-file actual usage. Cleaner than hand-tailoring 4 different import blocks. Pin: prefer over-broad import + ruff auto-fix to per-file hand-tailored imports (anti-bikeshed).

docs.title: F1 — Static-subclass vs runtime-factory is a real shape distinction (R84 new)
docs.text: Six call sites looked uniformly duplicated, but a 5-min audit surfaces two structurally distinct stub shapes. The cheap-to-extract one (5 sites, identical) is worth doing; the expensive one (1 site, divergent) is worth deferring with a defensive factory in place. Pin: when duplication looks N-fold, audit shape divergence before extraction; partial extraction with deferred reconciliation is a valid outcome. Compounds the R66 retro-documentation finding ("audit before re-build"): audit before refactor is the same principle one level down.

docs.title: F2 — Dogfood sys.path bootstrap is acceptable boilerplate when the alternative is shipping test helpers in the public package (R84 new)
docs.text: 4 lines of bootstrap is a small price compared to either (a) creating src/chronos/_testing/ (architecturally invasive, ADR-deserving) or (b) duplicating the fixture in scripts/_testing_helpers/ (defeats the refactor). Pin: dogfoods are entry-points, not library code; explicit sys.path.insert(0, repo_root) is the most honest seam between "installed package can find" and "repo-checkout-only helpers".

docs.title: F3 — Over-broad import + ruff auto-fix beats hand-tailored per-file imports (R84 new)
docs.text: 4 files imported the full 8-symbol surface; ruff --fix removed 13 unused imports across the 4 sites in one shot. Hand-tailoring would have been 4 mental allocations and 4× rebase risk if the fixture surface evolves. Pin: when refactoring N call sites toward a shared module, import everything; let ruff trim per-file. Lower friction, lower drift.

docs.text:
Closed AC-2 of ADR-026 §6 (the GA gate that blocks v0.7.0 GA): the Anthropic Agents adapter now has a real-relay live-smoke that records a multi-turn conversation containing one MCP tool call end-to-end. Five runtime invariants gate the dogfood (run.status=COMPLETED, ToolUseBlock+tool_use_id recorded, ToolResultBlock+tool_use_id recorded, IDs match per R76 linkage contract, final TextBlock contains the tool result). Quality bar held: 631 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, zero regression in adapter-1-3 (33-round streak).

The trick that unblocked this in one round (vs. the multi-round Node.js subprocess fixture R83 anticipated) was discovering that claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server ships an in-process Python MCP server — no npx, no Node, no subprocess.

docs.title: 2. Probe: does the OneAPI relay support MCP tool-use?
docs.text:
R83's deferral note hypothesized AC-2 needed:

"…an MCP server fixture + Node.js subprocess on the runner."

I ran a 30-line probe to test the assumption (one create_sdk_mcp_server + tool decorator + query() against the live Claude Sonnet 4.6 model):

SystemMessage 'init' …
AssistantMessage ThinkingBlock …
AssistantMessage ToolUseBlock { name=mcp__math__add, input={a:4127,b:8956}, id=toolu_bdrk_… }
UserMessage     ToolResultBlock { tool_use_id=toolu_bdrk_…, content=[{type:text,text:13083}] }
AssistantMessage TextBlock "The result of **4127 + 8956 = 13,083**."
ResultMessage 'success'

Three findings collapsed three deferred risks into a one-round fix:

  1. The OneAPI relay surfaces ToolUseBlock and ToolResultBlock to the SDK end-to-end. Earlier doubt was that the relay might only support flat text (per R64 doc that called the path "session protocol only"). It doesn't — full tool-use protocol works.
  2. claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server makes Node.js entirely unnecessary. Tools are ordinary Python async def functions decorated with @tool(...); the server runs in-process, no subprocess.
  3. The recorder already handles ToolUseBlock + ToolResultBlock correctly (R76 wiring): tool_use_id lands in state_after, IDs match across blocks.

docs.title: 3. Wrote the AC-2 dogfood
docs.text:
scripts/dogfood/arc_b_slice_3_mcp.py (~280 LOC):

  • Sets up a 1-tool MCP server: add(a: int, b: int) -> int. Operands are non-trivial (4127 + 8956 = 13083) so the model must actually use the tool, not memorize.
  • Builds ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=4, model='Claude Sonnet 4.6', mcp_servers={'math': server}, allowed_tools=['mcp__math__add'], system_prompt=…).
  • Drives query() through AnthropicAgentsRecorder with the R71 sync-recorder pattern (build async iterable in this loop, hand recorder to run_in_executor to dodge asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop).
  • Inspects recorded nodes; computes a structured report; runs five invariant checks; exits 0 only if all pass.
  • Outer 120s timeout guard + the same wallclock guard around the recorder coroutine.

First run failed. The dogfood's INV-2/3/3b/4 all tripped. Debugger printed state_after for every node — discovered the recorder writes block dicts with key "block" (not "type"), and stamps kind=NodeKind.LLM (not TOOL) on Assistant/User messages even when they carry ToolUseBlock/ToolResultBlock. The recorder's kind comes from message-type dispatch (recorder.py:27-46), not block-type dispatch. The NodeKind.TOOL entry in the block-dispatch table at recorder.py:77 is unused for these blocks.

This is not a bug for AC-2: tool_use_id IS in state_after, the R76 linkage contract holds, the data is fully recoverable. But it IS a contract finding worth documenting. I:

  • Updated the dogfood's invariant inspector to filter on state_after['blocks'][i]['block'] in {'ToolUseBlock','ToolResultBlock'} rather than n.kind == NodeKind.TOOL.
  • Tolerated thousands-separator rendering ("13,083" vs "13083") since the model wrote the latter.
  • Documented the contract finding inline in the inspector docstring.
  • Deferred reconciliation/contract-doc to a future round (CONTEXT §6 R86 TODO).

Second run: AC-2 release-gate INVARIANTS GREEN, exit 0, run took ~7 seconds, cost reported as $0.14.

docs.title: D2 — Used claude_agent_sdk.create_sdk_mcp_server (in-process) instead of an external MCP server
docs.text:
Three reasons:

  1. Zero subprocess dependency. No npx, no npm install, no Node version pinning, no PATH check, no fork-bomb worry on cron retry. Ports CI runners trivially.
  2. Test isolation. Tool runs in the same Python process as the recorder; no race between SDK launching subprocess and the dogfood asserting on captured shape.
  3. Sufficient for AC-2. The acceptance criterion is "≥1 MCP tool". One in-process tool ticks the box. Fancier multi-tool / external-server scenarios are post-GA polish.

Recorded in dogfood module docstring; the alternative (Node MCP server) is the natural future direction if/when we need to certify against external MCP servers.

docs.title: D3 — Did NOT fix the recorder contract finding (kind=LLM for ToolUseBlock messages)
docs.text:
Found a discrepancy: recorder's block-dispatch table at recorder.py:77 has "ToolUseBlock": NodeKind.TOOL, but the actual kind stamped on the recorded node is NodeKind.LLM because kind comes from message-type dispatch, not block-type.

Why deferred: - Not blocking AC-2: tool_use_id is correctly in state_after, R76 linkage works, the dogfood's five invariants pass with the observed shape. - Touching this is a recorder behavioral change. R85 budget is for AC-2 close, not adapter refactor. Mixing them risks regressing the 33-round streak. - Reconciliation has two valid resolutions: (a) document kind=LLM as intentional in the AdapterProtocol contract (because messages contain blocks, kind reflects the message envelope); (b) split nodes so each block becomes its own node with the correct kind. Choosing between (a) and (b) deserves a focused round + ADR.

Recorded in dogfood docstring + ADR-026 §6 AC-2 closing note. CONTEXT §6 carries it forward as an R86 candidate (low-priority since AC-2 is closed).

docs.title: F1. Aspirational-release-doc is a new trap class — codified into cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill
docs.text:
The trap shape: - CHANGELOG [X.Y.Z] block freshly written with full Added/Changed/Quality bar + cost numbers like ~$0.10 - ADR ACs flipped [x] claiming GA-gate green - [Unreleased] empty / drained - BUT pyproject.toml version unbumped, no progress doc, no tag, no commit

Inverse of release-mid-flight A2: release-mid-flight A2 = real work shipped, ceremonial commit/tag pending; aspirational = ceremonial doc shipped, real work never observed. Both look identical on disk. The distinguisher: the dogfood/live-smoke that the release block claims passed. Rerun it. If green, you're in A2 path. If exit 2 (relay degraded), defer + revert. If exit 3 (hard), the claim was fiction; revert.

Skill section added: \"Aspirational-release-doc trap (R86 lesson)\" with the recovery recipe (5 steps), the honesty rules, and the relay-flake corollary.

docs.title: F2. Relay-flake corollary — don't un-ratchet a recorded green AC just because the live run is currently red
docs.text:
R85 closed AC-2 with ~$0.14, INVARIANTS-GREEN recorded. R86 today: same R85 dogfood also exits 2. Adapter code unchanged in 1 day. The R85 ratchet is not retroactively invalid — it really did pass at R85. AC-2 stays [x] on R85's recorded fact. AC-3 (claimed by prior R86 slot) goes [x] → [~] because it was never actually run green against the relay; the prior slot's ADR flip was prospective, not observational.

Generalization: a relay-coupled GA-gate AC's [x] ratchet is a time-stamped snapshot of \"this round, against this relay state, with this SDK pin, the dogfood asserted invariants and exited 0\". It is not a perpetual claim about the relay's future state. Relay degradations are environmental and don't unratchet adapter-code claims.

This is the right behavior because: (a) relays are external dependencies whose health is outside chronos's control; (b) re-running every prior green AC on every round would be cost-prohibitive and add no signal beyond the original ratchet; (c) treating \"can't currently demonstrate green\" identically to \"never could have been green\" punishes the project for environmental flakes.

docs.title: F3. SDK version updates change the relay-error envelope; classifier must keep up
docs.text:
R69 first documented the OneAPI relay's synthetic-auth-failed mode (text contains \"authentication\" / \"synthetic\" / \"not logged in\").

R85 hard-coded those substrings into arc_b_slice_3_mcp.py:266 as a 3-marker heuristic.

R86 hit the same root cause with a different surface: today's claude-agent-sdk (≥ R85's pin) wraps the relay-side is_error=True ResultMessage(subtype='success') into the misleading exception Exception('Claude Code returned an error result: success'). Neither \"authentication\" nor \"synthetic\" is in that string. R85's heuristic mis-classifies it as exit 3 (hard regression) — which is the exact failure mode that pushed prior R86 slot toward the aspirational doc (\"oh dear, looks hard, but maybe it's the relay anyway, just write the close-out and move on\" → revert).

Fix: extract classifier to scripts/dogfood/_degradation.py, broaden marker list to 4 substrings (add claude code returned an error result), and pin the heuristic with a parametrized unit test (tests/unit/test_dogfood_degradation.py) that grows monotonically as new relay-failure shapes appear. Future SDK version → new envelope → add 1 marker + 1 test case = belt-and-suspenders protection.

docs.title: F4. AC-3 has a deeper problem than R86's specific flake — it's relay-coupled
docs.text:
The general issue: AC-3 (\"real-relay override-fork live-smoke green\") requires a working OneAPI relay to demonstrate. As long as that's the only path, every relay flake blocks GA. R87+ should consider:

  • Option α: keep waiting for relay recovery, accept that GA cut date is non-deterministic.
  • Option β: author a deterministic offline-fixture-based AC-3 closure path. Pre-record a real session-protocol JSONL transcript (one-time, requires a green relay window), then replay against a local fake that emits the SDK's Message types from that JSONL. AC-3 becomes a fixture-driven assertion that the recorder + fork primitive correctly handle the SDK's actual session-protocol shapes, without depending on live relay health every release.

Option β is the right long-term move: GA-gate ACs should not be coupled to environmental dependencies the project doesn't control. R87 will pick this up.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• D1 — Complete-at-existing-commit, not revert + redo: R87's commit is internally consistent (gates re-pass, AC evidence is real, version triple matches). Reverting would only churn history without adding evidence. The recovery rule per the skill is "match the trap shape; if gate evidence is valid, only the missing release-engineering steps need execution". Confirmed by post-action verification (releases/latest now matches R87's intent).
  • D2 — Tag at R87's exact commit 92a3e19, not at a new R88 commit: the GA cut belongs to R87 chronologically and content-wise. R88 is recovery, not a new release. Putting the tag on the R88 commit would imply "R88 cut the GA" which is not true.
  • D3 — Skill update happens this round, not deferred: the skill is the safety net for next agent. If R88 deferred the codification, R89 could re-trip the same recognition cost. R86 → R87 → R88 is now the third generation that exercised this skill; the variant is real and stable enough to codify.
  • D4 — Release body re-states AC evidence rather than just linking to CHANGELOG: GitHub Release pages are public-facing artifacts (even though the repo is private right now, the body persists). The body should be a self-contained release announcement, not a pointer to a changelog file.
  • D5 — No version bump in R88: this is recovery of v0.7.0, not v0.7.1. chronos --version already returns 0.7.0 and that is correct.

docs.title: Findings (R88 invariants for the wall)
docs.text:
1. Aspirational-release-doc trap has TWO variants — codify both (this round). R86 = "true aspiration" (gate evidence missing). R88 = "partial execution" (gate evidence intact; only release-engineering steps missing). Same trap shape pre-flight, different recovery prescription. Distinguished by the gate-evidence-valid axis. Skill now documents both with a 7-row diagnostic table. Pre-flight check at every round start: git status (any un-pushed commits?) + git tag --list "vX.Y.Z*" (any expected tags missing?) + releases/latest API (does it match the latest CHANGELOG block?). The 60-second check that caught R88 belongs in every cron round's setup phase, not just release rounds.

  2. The 8-step chronos-release-pattern is not atomic — last 2 steps (push, Release POST) can silently no-op. R87's progress doc shows P9 + P10 written as if they ran, but git history + remote state proved otherwise. Possible causes: (a) cron-slot timeout near round end, (b) network blip on the gh-proxy or api.github.com calls, (c) progress-doc was written speculatively before P9/P10 ran. No way to fully diagnose post-mortem since R87 didn't preserve shell logs. Mitigation: post-round verification step in chronos-release-pattern skill — "after committing, fetch from remote and re-verify (a) commit on origin, (b) tag on remote, (c) GET releases/latest matches new tag". Will patch the skill in R88 close-out if not already there.

  3. Even pristine progress docs can mis-report execution state — R87's progress doc is one of the cleanest in the project (87 lines, well-structured, every section filled). And it still claimed completion of two steps that didn't run on the remote. Lesson: progress docs are intent + claim, not ground truth. Ground truth = git history + remote API state. Going forward, if a release round's progress doc says "tag pushed + Release page created", the next round's setup MUST re-verify both via remote queries (cheap: one git ls-remote --tags + one releases/latest API call, ~1s each).

  4. Cost of recovery vs. cost of trap: total R88 cost = 0 LLM (no live-smoke), 0 gate-flake risk (re-ran gates locally, all green), ~5 minutes wallclock. Total R88 value = v0.7.0 visible as "Latest" on GitHub for the first time, install instructions reach reality (pip install chronos-agent==0.7.0 would actually resolve once published — repo still private but tag is now real), skill hardened. Recovery rounds are cheap; un-recovered traps are expensive (every future round's pre-flight burns recognition cost re-discovering them, plus user-trust erosion if the user inspects GitHub and sees v0.6.0 still latest). Always-recover-immediately is the right default for this class of trap.

Updated R89 recommendation (vs R87's recommendation of Option β by default):

  • Option C(a) — recorder kind contract reconciliation, docs-only is now the strongest default for R89. Reasoning: (a) zero gate-drift risk (md only); (b) closes the R85 contract finding documentation debt cleanly; (c) lowest pre-budget (0.5–1 slot); (d) post-recovery rounds are good for low-risk md work (re-establish "boring round" cadence after R86/R87/R88 release-engineering churn).

  • Option D — 6th fixture site migration is the second-strongest default. Same low-risk profile; mechanical refactor; tests stay green throughout.

  • Option β — offline-fixture AC-3 closure path retains the "ADR-027 candidate, relay-independent" justification but is less urgent than at R87 hand-off because: (a) AC-3 ratchet is now stable across R87 (live observed) + R88 (re-verified release-engineering), (b) GA is shipped + visible, so future relay flakes don't block any release. Keep as 1–2 slot post-Phase-5-planning option.

  • Option ε — Phase 5 planning is appropriate any time but not yet urgent. Project just shipped GA; one round of polish before planning is reasonable.

Strong recommendation for R89: Option C(a) or D, single slot, md/test-only, re-establish boring-round cadence. Defer Option β to R90+ once a polish round has shipped cleanly. This is consistent with the "recovery → boring → boring → planning → impl" cron rhythm pattern (R59→R60→R61→R62 was a textbook example of this rhythm in Phase 4 Arc A).

R89 hard-prereqs to verify pre-flight (per R88 finding #1):

  • git status clean + in-sync with origin/main.
  • git tag --list "v0.7*" includes v0.7.0 (R88's recovery output).

If any of those four fail, another recovery round is needed before any new work, per cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill.

R88 single-slot, ~25 minutes, 0 LLM cost, 0 relay cost, 1 GitHub Release created, 1 skill update, 1 trap variant codified. Aspirational-release-doc trap detector → partial-execution recovery variant → release-engineering completion. The 35-round zero-regression streak un-touched. v0.7.0 GA is now visibly real on GitHub.

docs.title: D-1: Option (a) over option (b)
docs.text:
R85 noted two possible reconciliation paths:

  • (a) Document kind=LLM for tool blocks as intentional (envelope-determines-kind).
  • (b) Split blocks into separate nodes via ADR-027.

Chose (a) because:

  1. Post-GA: v0.7.0 shipped 2026-05-19 with the envelope behaviour. Splitting per-block would be a breaking schema change — node count for any tool-using run would multiply, breaking diff invariants, replay storage, and external tooling assumptions.
  2. Code already canonical: 36-round zero-regression streak across LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, anthropic_agents — the envelope rule has held silently for the entire project history. Codifying it isn't a new decision; it's surfacing what's already true.
  3. Cost asymmetry: (a) is 1-round md-only. (b) would be: ADR-027 + per-block split refactor in recorder.py + R76/R77 tool_use_id/tool_use_ids re-stamp logic + 30+ test rewrites + dogfood updates + alpha→GA cycle for v0.8.0. (a) costs ~$0.01; (b) costs 6+ rounds.
  4. Mental model: "one Node = one observable agent step" maps naturally onto "one Node = one SDK message". Per-block split would break this.

docs.title: D-2: Keep dead map entries, document them
docs.text:
Pruning ToolUseBlock/ToolResultBlock from _DEFAULT_KIND_MAP would be the orthogonal "code cleanup" round. Decided against because:

  • They are harmless (never reached at runtime under the SDK's current top-level iterator contract).
  • They are forward-compatible — if a future SDK release surfaces blocks as top-level stream items, the entries activate without code change.
  • They are defensively useful — a custom kind_map callsite that wraps _kind_for() to defer per-block can fall through to these entries.
  • Removing them would add a git blame entry that's pure rearrangement; not worth the noise.

Codify as an invariant: cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill should explicitly include "scan most recent ADR closing-notes for 'tracked for future' / 'TBD' / 'TODO' phrases and surface as round-candidate" in its diagnostic.

Lesson: even if slot-1 successfully ships an inherited close-out commit, that close-out itself burns ~7-10 calls (status + verify + add + diff-check + commit + push + QQ). Codification candidate for the skill: when slot starts inheriting close-out work, do NOT plan a second new round in the same slot. Land the close-out, write a "next slot picks up R" message, ship the QQ report, end the round. The next cron slot has a full fresh budget for the new work.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Registry safety net — try { formatter(node) } catch { return formatDefault(node); console.warn }. Per-adapter formatters can be incrementally added/changed without risking a Replay page crash for users whose runs use the affected adapter. Trade-off: silent fallback on bug → mitigated by console.warn.
  • No anthropic_agents block-content rendering (text body, tool input JSON, tool result content) is specially formatted yet — every block is rendered as its full safeStringify'd JSON dict in the section's <pre>. Rationale: slice 2 scope is "structured sections, not raw blob"; deeper formatting (e.g. rendering text blocks as plain text, tool_use as a param table) is a candidate for slice 3 or a follow-up.
  • Other adapters stay on default — autogen, crewai, openai_agents keep the raw JSON dump (just routed through formatDefault so the framing is consistent). They're R94+ candidates if their state shapes diverge enough to warrant per-adapter UI.
  • Top 5 anthropic blocks open by default — heuristic to keep the panel compact when a long conversation has many TextBlocks. Users can expand the rest via <Collapse> headers; full raw view always available via the toggle.

docs.text: parseHash in App.tsx was modified to match /runs/<id>/replay before /runs/<id>. Verified the regex order: replayMatch is checked BEFORE the generic m = h.match(/^\/runs\/([^/]+)$/). Without this order, the more permissive tree route would swallow /runs/abc/replay (matching abc/replay as the runId), producing a TreeView mounted with a slash-containing runId and 404'ing the API call. Order is correct.

docs.title: C. AppHeader RouteName widening (caught by tsc -b)
docs.text:
First gate run surfaced a TS2322 error: App.tsx passes route.name as currentRoute to <AppHeader>, and AppHeader.tsx had type RouteName = "landing" | "runs" | "tree" | "diff" — missing "replay". Widened the union to include "replay". The header doesn't render anything route-specific for replay (no nav highlight, no breadcrumb), so this is purely a type widening — no rendering change.

This is a secondary-file-not-touched-by-prior-slot trap: the prior slot correctly added "replay" to App.tsx's Route union but missed the parallel RouteName union in AppHeader. tsc -b catches it cleanly; runtime would have been fine anyway because TypeScript erases unions at runtime. Lesson recorded for future Replay-style multi-file route additions.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• D1 (payload widening, not replacement). I chose SectionPayload = string | StructuredPayload over a clean-slate replacement (payload: StructuredPayload-only). The reason is that langgraph, default, header, and extras sections do not benefit from shape-aware rendering — forcing them through { kind: 'json', value } would have meant rewriting three files for zero UX delta and pushing every adapter to know about the union shape. The TS narrowing in renderPayload is one extra typeof === 'string' check per section; cost is negligible and the rest of the codebase keeps its existing string-pretty contract.

  • D2 (no fresh ADR). Slice 3 is squarely inside ADR-027 §2 slice 3; the discriminated union is an internal representation refinement (frontend-only, not a recorded contract), so no new ADR is needed. ADR-027 stays Accepted. Per R57 in-place rule, if a NEW ADR were introduced (e.g. to formalise a rendered-payload schema for future back-end deep-links), it'd start Draft and be promoted post-merge in the same diff. Not needed here.

  • D3 (no new spike, smoke harness instead). CONTEXT §6 explicitly authorised "no new spike strictly needed" since slice 3's data-contract surface area is empty. I still wrote a Node+tsx smoke harness to give the impl commit empirical "the function does the right thing" coverage without dragging in vitest / RTL setup (which is out of slice 3 scope). The harness is checked in under frontend/scripts/ so future rounds can re-run it as a regression check.

  • D4 (i18n key count: 6 vs the 4 estimated). CONTEXT estimated 4 keys (textBlock, toolUseBlock, toolResultBlock, toolError); I shipped 6 (added textBlockEmpty, toolUseEmpty, toolResultEmpty). The empty variants are user-visible placeholder strings — hard-coding them would break the bilingual rule under R46-A. I dropped textBlock as a user-visible label entirely (the section title Block 0 — TextBlock is already shown by the existing label/subLabel structure, no extra i18n needed). Net delta: +2 keys vs estimate.

  • D5 (Optional ε bundled, not deferred). With slice 3 finishing in ~1/3 of the slot budget, I judged the 1-file git mv filler safer to bundle now than to carry forward another round. The R93 drift list shrinks by 1.

docs.title: Findings / lessons
docs.text:
• F-1 (tsx is auto-installable for one-shot harnesses). npx tsx pulled the package transparently and ran the harness against a TS source file with no separate compile step. Useful pattern for future one-shot frontend probes that don't want a vitest setup. Logged into smoke harness so future rounds know they can re-run with just node frontend/scripts/r94-slice3-smoke.mjs.

  • F-2 (existing safeStringify re-export from default.ts). StatePanel.tsx now imports safeStringify from ../format/adapters/default for the kind:'json' and tool_use non-string-value rendering paths. This is the only cross-component use; it's a legitimate re-use of a pure function, not a circular import (default.ts imports nothing from components). Frontend one-way-import contract preserved.

  • F-3 (slice 3 came in well under the 1-slot estimate). The StructuredPayload design + buildBlockPayload helper + renderPayload switch landed in roughly half the expected effort — the main underpinning was already in place from R92 (Replay UI scaffolding) and R93 (registry + StatePanel skeleton). This validates the slicing decision in ADR-027: each slice ships standalone, the next slice inherits ground truth from the previous one.

  3. A1 A run + its forked children form a tree where each child has a parent_run_id + a fork_node_id; the GET /runs/{id} + GET /runs?parent_run_id={id} contracts already expose this without server-side reshaping.
  4. A2 Per-step ordering across parent + fork is well-defined: each fork starts at fork_node_id index in the parent timeline, then diverges. We can reconstruct an aligned multi-track timeline deterministically from (parent.nodes, [child.nodes for child in forks]).
  5. A3 Worst-case combined node count (parent + 5 forks × 50 nodes) ≤ 300 nodes — well within React render budget for a single panel.
  6. frontend/src/components/ForkTimeline.tsx — multi-row variant of PlaybackTimeline showing parent timeline on row 0 and each fork on rows 1..N, all sharing the same x-axis (step index). Hover/click selects (run_id, step_idx) instead of just step_idx.
  7. Replay.tsx route refactor: #/runs/<id>/replay shows just the run; if ?fork-tree=1 is in the hash, fetch sibling forks and render ForkTimeline. (Slice 5's URL deep-links will cover the canonical form later.)
  8. Strict-xfail forcing function — at least one registry-level invariant marked xfail(strict=True) in spike 18, removed in same impl diff.

  • New _reap_stale_pid_file(pid_file, console): os.kill(old_pid, 0) to probe; ProcessLookupError → reap with a [yellow]note:[/] message; PermissionError (alive but other-user) → leave alone; corrupt file (non-int) → silently nuke. Best-effort throughout (read-only filesystem etc. don't break serving).
  • Wire-in to web_command: reap-then-write before banner; cleanup in finally next to store.close(). Both wrapped in contextlib.suppress(OSError) — never block serving on PID-file plumbing.

docs.title: §11 Recovery addendum (BJT 06:5x — third A2 cycle on R115)
docs.text:
This is the third cron slot to handle R115 (initial implementation slot capped → first A2 close-out wrote progress doc + CONTEXT/CHANGELOG → this slot pre-commit gate sweep + commit + push). The slot opened with the same inherited tree the prior A2 left (12 modified + 8 untracked, progress doc complete, gates claimed green).

Verify-don't-redo discipline (per cron-slot-handoff-recovery skill rule 10 refinement): ran pytest -q --no-cov first (1 tool call) → 745/9/0 confirms the prior slot's claim byte-identical. Then ran the rest of the gate sweep (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy src) which surfaced 8 ruff issues + 1 mypy unused-ignore + 4 ruff-format files needing reformat — all incidental drift the prior A2 hadn't run before declaring green.

Pre-commit fixes applied (~10 minutes, kept inside the same R115 logical commit since none change behavior):

  • ruff --fix --unsafe-fixes: auto-resolved 4 RUF100 unused-noqa + 1 I001 unsorted-imports + 1 SIM108 ternary expression (6 of 8). All in src/chronos/api/server.py, src/chronos/cli/eval.py, src/chronos/store/sqlite.py — strictly stylistic.
  • 2 SIM115 open() without context manager in tests/spikes/spike21_eval_compare_pipeline.py (Console-file-pattern) — hand-fixed by wrapping Console(file=open(sink, ...)) as with sink.open(...) as fp: console = Console(file=fp); ... and re-indenting the call body. Two occurrences (test_compare_eval_json_carries_scores + test_compare_eval_unknown_evaluator), patched both.
  • 1 mypy [unused-ignore] in src/chronos/eval/__init__.py:246 on the entry_points().get("chronos.evaluators", []) defensive branch — fixed by widening to # type: ignore[union-attr,attr-defined,unused-ignore] so mypy accepts the line on both Python 3.11 (which doesn't need the ignore) and importlib_metadata <5 (which does, hypothetically).
  • ruff format src tests reformatted 4 files: src/chronos/cli/web.py (R114 incidental — single-line collapse of multi-line f-string), tests/integration/test_evaluations_store.py, tests/unit/test_cli_eval.py, tests/unit/test_cli_web.py (R114 + R115 inherited drift). All purely cosmetic — no logic change.

Final post-fix gate sweep (re-run, all green): - pytest -q --no-cov: 745 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failed (33.43s) - ruff check src tests: All checks passed - ruff format --check src tests: 123 files unchanged - mypy src: Success: no issues found in 46 source files - Frontend npx tsc --noEmit: clean; npm run build: clean (10.59s)

Adapter dir invariant: git diff --stat src/chronos/adapters/ → empty. R52 → R115 = 64 streak verified, not just claimed.

Skill confirmation, no patch needed: this slot validates the rule-10 refinement (R115 lesson) — pytest first as bug-detection ground truth was correct (745/0 confirmed prior slot's claim accurate, no fabricated greens). The lesson generalizes: even when an A2 progress doc claims gates green, re-run the full gate sweep (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, frontend tsc/build) before committing. Pre-existing drift is common across cron-slot handoffs — the prior A2 may have run only pytest and stopped. The full sweep is ~3 tool calls and catches the drift before it ships.

Commit shape: single commit (post-fixup) covering all R115 work — bug-fix (_seed sort key), engine implementation (eval module + CLI + API + frontend), schema migration, tests + spike, doc updates (progress doc + CONTEXT + CHANGELOG), pre-commit gate fixes (ruff/format/mypy). Two-commit ordering (rule 10 bug-fix-first) was already collapsed by the prior A2 slot — this slot inherits one logical R115 unit and ships it.

docs.title: chronos-agent v1.0.0-rc1 — 2026-06-08
docs.text:
Release Candidate 1 — final acceptance testing window. If no P0 surfaces during R121–R122 dogfood, this RC promotes to v1.0.0 GA.

pdb + git for multi-agent AI reasoning trees. Record once, replay deterministically, fork from any node, diff branch outcomes, track tokens/cost, score with evaluators.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Five working agent adapters — LangGraph, Anthropic Agents SDK (claude-agent-sdk), CrewAI, AutoGen, plus Linear pipeline. Adapter zero-regression streak: R52 → R120 = 68 rounds (src/chronos/adapters/ byte-untouched across the entire Phase 6 polish track).
  • Cost visibility (ADR-029) — chronos runs list shows token + cost columns by default; frontend RunList mirrors them; quickstart demo populates usage so the column reads non-zero on first try.
  • Evaluator framework (ADR-030) — chronos eval run --evaluator <name> produces a numeric score per run; chronos eval list enumerates results; chronos compare --eval ranks two runs by score; frontend Score column. Two built-in evaluators ship: output_length_chars and final_state_key_present.
  • One-command quickstart — chronos quickstart --demo langgraph-router (or crewai-research-team / anthropic-agent-tools / builtin-minimal) loads a pre-recorded run + fork into a fresh DB; --list enumerates available demos with recommended evaluators.
  • chronos doctor — environment / DB / schema / extras health check. 6 ✅ on a clean install, ⚠️ rows for missing optional extras with actionable hints.
  • mkdocs-material docs site — getting-started, cli-reference, concepts, evaluators, cost-tracking, FAQ. Auto-deployed to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
  • Bilingual README — README.md (English) + README.zh-CN.md (中文). Identical structure, separate prose.
  • Onboarding tour — landing page surface walks new users through the five core flows. Skippable + replayable.
  • 769 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failed local pytest baseline; CI now matches local after the R120 --all-extras fix.

docs.title: Quickstart (5 minutes)
docs.text:
# 1. Install (dev install with all extras)
git clone https://github.com/chengfei867/chronos-agent.git
cd chronos-agent
uv sync --all-extras

# 2. Load a demo
uv run chronos quickstart --demo langgraph-router

# 3. List runs (Tokens + Cost ¢ visible by default)
uv run chronos runs list

# 4. Score the run
uv run chronos eval run --run <run_id> --evaluator output_length_chars

# 5. Compare parent vs fork by score
uv run chronos compare <parent_id> <fork_id> --eval output_length_chars

# 6. Open the web UI
uv run chronos web
# → http://localhost:8000

uv run chronos quickstart --list enumerates all available demos. uv run chronos doctor reports env/DB/schema/extras health if anything looks off.

docs.title: Competitive Analysis — Agent Observability / Debugging Landscape
docs.text:
Last updated: 2026-04-22 (Round 1) Status: Initial analysis — to be verified against live sources in future rounds

⚠️ Verification needed: This document represents the agent's knowledge snapshot as of training + April 2026 public information. Future rounds should cross-check each competitor's feature list against their live docs, since the agent tooling space moves fast. Add Last verified YYYY-MM-DD stamps per section.

docs.title: Why This Document Exists
docs.text:
chronos-agent claims the "time-travel debugger for multi-agent systems" niche is empty. This doc is the falsification test: list every serious player in adjacent spaces and prove, feature-by-feature, the gap is real.

Framing: We care about four capabilities:

Capability What it means R1. Record Capture agent runs (prompts, tool calls, state) with enough fidelity to reconstruct R2. Replay Walk through a recorded run step-by-step (read-only) R3. Fork Branch from any step, modify a variable (prompt / tool / model), re-run downstream R4. Diff Structured comparison of two runs or two forks of same run

If a competitor has only R1, they are an observability tool. If they have R1+R2, they are a replay tool. If they have R1+R2+R3, they are a time-travel debugger — the chronos-agent niche. R4 is a bonus feature that further differentiates.

docs.title: 1. LangSmith (by LangChain)
docs.text:
• What: Hosted tracing + evaluation platform tightly coupled to LangChain / LangGraph ecosystem
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — Full trace capture via LangChain callbacks
  • R2 ✅ — Web UI walks through each step
  • R3 ⚠️ — "Playground" lets you re-run a single LLM call with edits, but not fork + re-run downstream of a multi-step agent
  • R4 ❌ — Trace comparison exists for evaluations but not step-by-step structural diff
  • Coverage: LangChain / LangGraph first-class, others via manual OTel
  • Business model: Freemium SaaS, enterprise pricing
  • Gap vs. chronos-agent: LangSmith is the gold standard for observability but does not solve "I want to change step 5 of a past run and see what would have happened". The Playground is per-LLM-call, not per-agent-graph.

docs.title: 2. Langfuse (open source)
docs.text:
• What: Self-hostable LLM observability; Langfuse = open-source Langsmith-like competitor
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing, SDK for Python / JS
  • R2 ✅ — Web UI for tracing
  • R3 ❌ — "Prompt playground" exists for single-prompt iteration; no agent-tree fork
  • R4 ⚠️ — Dataset-based eval, some trace comparison, no node-level diff
  • Coverage: Any framework via SDK
  • Business model: Open core + hosted cloud
  • Gap: Same as LangSmith. Strong foundation (OTel + open source), but not a debugger in the interactive-intervention sense.

docs.title: 3. AgentOps.ai
docs.text:
• What: Observability specifically aimed at agents (emphasizes "session replay")
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — SDK captures LLM calls, tool calls, errors
  • R2 ✅ — "Session replay" in web UI — strong point
  • R3 ❌ — No fork / re-run capability discovered in docs
  • R4 ⚠️ — Some comparison via dashboards, not structural
  • Coverage: Multi-framework (CrewAI, AutoGen, LangChain via SDK)
  • Business model: Freemium SaaS
  • Gap: Best "session replay" in the field (read-only), still no write-side intervention.

docs.title: 4. Arize Phoenix / Arize AX
docs.text:
• What: Enterprise ML observability → added LLM/agent support
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — OTel-based agent tracing
  • R2 ✅ — Trace tree viewer
  • R3 ❌ — Evaluation replay via dataset, no fork
  • R4 ✅ (partial) — Strong eval/comparison between runs via datasets
  • Coverage: OTel-compatible
  • Business model: Open source (Phoenix) + enterprise (AX)
  • Gap: Strong eval/monitoring; eval comparison is at dataset level, not reasoning-node level.

docs.title: 5. Helicone
docs.text:
• What: LLM proxy that logs all calls; added "sessions" grouping for agent patterns
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — Proxy-based, zero-instrument capture
  • R2 ⚠️ — Session grouping but not full agent semantics
  • R3 ❌
  • R4 ⚠️ — A/B prompt testing but not fork/diff
  • Coverage: Any HTTPS LLM call through proxy
  • Business model: Hosted + self-host
  • Gap: Simplest capture (no SDK) but no agent-level semantics or fork.

docs.title: 6. Braintrust
docs.text:
• What: "Evaluation-first" platform with tracing on the side
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅
  • R2 ✅
  • R3 ⚠️ — "Experiments" let you rerun prompts over a dataset, not fork a single live run
  • R4 ✅ — Strong dataset-based diff between experiment variants
  • Coverage: Multi-framework
  • Business model: Closed-source SaaS
  • Gap: The comparison/eval angle is strongest here but operates at dataset granularity, not run-node granularity.

docs.title: 7. Laminar (lmnr.ai)
docs.text:
• What: Newer entrant, OpenTelemetry-based agent observability with emphasis on clean trace UI
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — OTel GenAI semantic conventions
  • R2 ✅ — Replay viewer
  • R3 ❌ — No fork capability discovered
  • R4 ⚠️ — Basic comparison
  • Coverage: OTel-compatible
  • Business model: Open source core + cloud
  • Gap: Closest in aesthetic goal to chronos-agent (developer-focused), but still observability-only.

docs.title: 8. Humanloop
docs.text:
• What: Prompt management + evaluation
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — Capture via SDK
  • R2 ⚠️ — Trace view exists but Humanloop focuses on prompt versioning
  • R3 ⚠️ — Strong prompt versioning + playground (re-run single prompt)
  • R4 ✅ — Structured eval diff per prompt version
  • Coverage: Multi-framework
  • Business model: SaaS
  • Gap: Excellent at prompt-level time-travel; zero at reasoning-tree fork.

docs.title: 9. LangGraph Checkpointer (LangChain)
docs.text:
• What: Framework feature (not a product) — save state between nodes in a LangGraph
  • Capabilities:
  • R1 ✅ — State persistence built into LangGraph
  • R2 ✅ — Can resume from checkpoint
  • R3 ✅ (partial!) — Can restart from checkpoint with modified state → this is closest to fork
  • R4 ❌ — No comparison tooling
  • Coverage: LangGraph only (hard boundary)
  • Gap: This is the most philosophically-aligned thing that exists, but:
  • Only works within LangGraph
  • No UI, no diff, no cross-framework abstraction
  • No "fork tree" metaphor — it's "resume from snapshot with overrides"
  • No cost tracking, no evaluation hooks, no shareability

⚠️ Competitive insight: chronos-agent's value is to be to LangGraph checkpointer what git is to tar. The primitive is there, but nobody has built the workflow, the UI, the cross-framework abstraction, or the diff tooling.

docs.title: 10. AutoGen / CrewAI / Swarm Built-in Trace
docs.text:
• What: Each framework ships simple trace logging
  • Capabilities: R1 only (basic logs)
  • Gap: No serious tooling built on top of their trace formats.

docs.title: 11. pdb / debuggers for programming languages
docs.text:
• What: Interactive debugging for traditional code
  • Relevance: Conceptual inspiration. chronos-agent essentially ports the pdb metaphor to LLM reasoning.
  • Gap: No LLM/agent analog exists.

docs.title: 12. Jupyter Notebook
docs.text:
• What: Interactive code cells with persistent kernel state
  • Relevance: Similar "rerun a cell with different input" metaphor
  • Gap: Not agent-aware, not trace-first, no tree.

docs.title: 13. Git / GitGraph tools
docs.text:
• What: Version control with branching, diffing
  • Relevance: The fork + diff metaphor comes directly from git
  • Gap: Not applicable to LLM state.

docs.title: 14. Time-travel Debuggers (e.g. rr, UndoDB, Replay.io)
docs.text:
• What: Record all syscalls/state of a program, replay deterministically, step backwards
  • Relevance: Strongest conceptual parallel. These tools literally do "time-travel debugging" for traditional code.
  • Gap: LLM calls are non-deterministic (even at temp=0 there's numerical drift, model updates, etc.), making direct port non-trivial.
  • Key insight: A naïve "record everything" approach fails for LLMs. chronos-agent must record LLM outputs and synthetic state, not try to replay the LLM itself.

docs.title: 15. Foundry's vm.snapshot() / vm.revert() (Ethereum testing)
docs.text:
• What: EVM state snapshot and revert primitives in smart contract testing
  • Relevance: The project author's prior experience. Concept of snapshot/revert of a state machine → re-execute with different input maps directly.
  • Gap: Ethereum state is deterministic; agent state isn't. But the primitive API design is transferable.

docs.title: 16. Apache Beam / Flink (dataflow checkpointing)
docs.text:
• What: Distributed stream processing with exactly-once semantics via checkpointing
  • Relevance: Analog for "multi-actor with state snapshot" — multi-agent systems share this property
  • Gap: Too heavyweight; doesn't target debugging UX.

docs.title: 17. Academic: Agent Benchmarking Platforms
docs.text:
• SWE-bench, WebArena, τ-bench, GAIA, AgentBench
  • Not tools, benchmarks. Provide test data but not debugging.

docs.title: 18. Academic: LLM Debugging Papers
docs.text:
• "Why Did My Agent Fail?" — various postmortem-style papers
  • Mostly proposals, no production tool

docs.title: 19. Guardrails / Safety Tools (Guardrails AI, NeMo Guardrails)
docs.text: • Prevent bad output, not debug reasoning.

docs.title: 20. LLM-as-Judge Tools
docs.text: • Evaluation lens, not debugging.

docs.title: Where is the empty space?
docs.text:
Plotting the 10 Tier-1 products on our R1/R2/R3/R4 matrix:

                 R1   R2   R3      R4
                 ──   ──   ──      ──
LangSmith        ✅   ✅   ⚠️-prompt-only   ❌
Langfuse         ✅   ✅   ❌      ⚠️-dataset
AgentOps         ✅   ✅   ❌      ⚠️
Phoenix          ✅   ✅   ❌      ✅-dataset
Helicone         ✅   ⚠️   ❌      ⚠️-AB
Braintrust       ✅   ✅   ⚠️-dataset   ✅-dataset
Laminar          ✅   ✅   ❌      ⚠️
Humanloop        ✅   ⚠️   ⚠️-prompt-only   ✅-prompt
LangGraph-cp     ✅   ✅   ✅-framework-locked   ❌
────────────────────────────────────────────
chronos-agent    ✅   ✅   ✅-general   ✅-node-level

Key findings:

  1. R3 (Fork) is the hardest and least-served dimension. Only LangGraph checkpointer offers it, and only within one framework with no UI.
  2. R4 (Diff) exists mostly at dataset granularity. Nobody does node-level structural diff between two reasoning trees.
  3. Every competitor assumes "runs are immutable historical artifacts". None assume "runs are fork-able programs".

docs.title: Why haven't the big players done this?
docs.text:
Hypotheses (to be tested):

  • LangSmith business model: Monetized around evaluation datasets + enterprise observability. Fork-and-retry is a niche developer workflow, not an enterprise buying signal.
  • Langfuse: Community-driven, follows user demand; fork-retry requires deep framework integration that single OSS maintainers can't sustain across frameworks.
  • LangGraph: Has the primitive but is self-satisfied — their customers use it as "resume after crash", not "fork for exploration".
  • Phoenix/Arize: Enterprise ML-ops DNA; they think in batch/evaluation, not in interactive debugging.
  • Fundamental technical barrier: To fork an arbitrary agent run, you need state capture semantics that work across frameworks. That's a hard integration problem nobody has wanted to eat.

docs.title: What chronos-agent must prove to matter
docs.text:
1. Cross-framework fork works on at least 2 frameworks
  2. Node-level diff is useful in real debugging (user studies / dogfood)
  3. The fork UX is fast enough (fork → see result in < 30s for a simple agent) to feel "interactive" like pdb

docs.title: Threat Analysis
docs.text:
If we succeed, who catches up fastest?

Competitor Time to copy (est.) Likelihood LangSmith 3-6 months Medium (not their business model fit) Langfuse 6-12 months Medium (community + OSS speed) LangGraph 2-3 months High (they have the primitive; just need UI) AgentOps 6-9 months Medium A new startup 3-6 months High (space is eye-catching)

Defensive moat strategies: - Open-source first + build community — outrun closed-source by mindshare - Cross-framework adapter ecosystem — hard for framework-native tools to match - Dog-fooded by AI agents themselves (including Hermes Agent / Claude Code) — make it the default debug tool for AI-native development

  3. Investigate: Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK — is there something there?

  7. Academic check: Search arxiv for "LLM time-travel debugging", "agent trace replay", "prompt counterfactual execution"
  8. Any YC W25 / W26 company in this niche? Check YC's launch list

docs.text:
